articles.title: Jerry Jones is frustrated with Dallas' 2-4 record and makes a major decision that hinges on next three games
articles.standfirst: The Dallas Cowboys could be looking at a completely lost season if they won’t beat the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7.
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys could be looking at a completely lost season if they won’t beat the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7.
articles.body:
Coming into the 2026 NFL season , the Dallas Cowboys were considered somewhat of a Super Bowl dark horse . The team showed flashes of greatness under first-year head coach Brian Schottenheimer last season, and the front office made a lot of changes on the defensive side of the ball during the offseason.

Through six games this season, though, those changes aren’t proving fruitful at all. The Cowboys have given up over 20 points in every single game this season , including 24 to the Jalon Daniels -quarterbacked Tampa Bay Buccaneers . What’s amplifying the defense’s flaws is that the offense isn’t picking up the slack .

Dak Prescott is going through a brutal two-game stretch, and Dallas has scored a combined 29 points over the last two weeks . This upcoming three-game stretch will essentially make or break the Cowboys’ season. Dallas will play against the Jalen Hurts -less Philadelphia Eagles , Arizona Cardinals , and Indianapolis Colts over the next three weeks.

Jerry Jones says Dallas Cowboys could be buyers, and potentially sellers, at NFL Trade Deadline

What makes that stretch even more intriguing is that it leads up to the NFL Trade Deadline on November 10 . If the Cowboys lose even two of those games, Jerry Jones could be enticed into selling off some pieces in order to get back draft capital for the future . On the contrary, if the Cowboys win all three games, Jones would be willing to make a trade to help the team . He revealed as much to the media recently.

“ I’ll be real clear, I could see being active at the trade deadline if it was something that could help the team this year… But I don’t rule it out now (selling if the right offer comes along).”

Jones loves pulling off trades, so it wouldn’t surprise anyone if it comes to fruition at the deadline. But it will all depend on how these next three games go for the Cowboys.

articles.title: Brian Schottenheimer accepts the reality in Dallas after falling to 2-4
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys are in trouble, and their own head coach admitted what many in Dallas didn’t want to hear after a 2-4 start.
articles.summary: The Cowboys are in trouble, and their own head coach admitted what many in Dallas didn’t want to hear after a 2-4 start.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer refused to hide from the pressure surrounding the team and accepted part of the responsibility for Dallas’ disappointing start to the season. Sitting at 2-4 , the coach acknowledged that the Cowboys have earned much of the criticism coming their way after a frustrating opening stretch.

Schottenheimer admits Cowboys deserve criticism

Schottenheimer spoke with reporters Thursday as Dallas prepares for a crucial Monday Night Football matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles . His comments came after back-to-back losses to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Green Bay Packers , results that have increased the pressure on both the team and coaching staff.

“I think it comes with the territory. I think some of it is deserved. We’ve got to play better. I’ve got to coach better. When you grow up in a family where your dad was a head coach for over 20 years, you understand that this is part of the job description. No one likes it. I block out most of it. Some of it gets to me because doing this job and having to speak to you guys is part of it. But at the same time, I’ve got strong shoulders. I know what kind of coach I am. I know what this team is capable of, and that’s what I focus on,” Schottenheimer said.

The Cowboys coach also discussed the influence of his father, Marty Schottenheimer , who spent 21 seasons as an NFL head coach with the Cleveland Browns, Kansas City Chiefs, Washington Commanders, and San Diego Chargers.

Brian explained that growing up in that environment taught him an important lesson: criticism and scrutiny are unavoidable parts of leading a team at the highest level.

The pressure on Schottenheimer continues to grow. In his first 23 games as Dallas’ head coach, he has posted a 9-13-1 record , a mark that highlights the challenges surrounding the franchise’s current direction.

After the loss to the Packers, Schottenheimer defended his players’ effort and fight but admitted that mistakes have been the biggest issue. He specifically pointed to the five turnovers committed over the last two games, a costly trend that has directly impacted the Cowboys’ results.

For Schottenheimer, the solution must come from within. The coach acknowledged that the players need to perform better, but he also accepted that he must improve his own coaching decisions from the sideline.

He also explained that some of the outside criticism inevitably reaches him because his role requires constant interaction with the media and accountability for the team’s performance.

Cowboys look to turn things around against Eagles

At 53 years old, Schottenheimer admitted that nobody enjoys going through a difficult stretch like this, but said he tries to block out most of the outside noise. He remains confident in his ability and believes the Cowboys still have the talent to accomplish their goals this season.

Dallas entered the 2026 campaign after back-to-back seasons with only seven wins, hoping to take the next step and establish itself as a legitimate contender in the NFC East . Instead, the early results have created more questions than answers.

The Cowboys will visit the Philadelphia Eagles , who also sit at 2-4, to close out Week 7 of the NFL season in Monday Night Football next Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET (5:15 p.m. PT) at Lincoln Financial Field .

The goal for Schottenheimer and Dallas will be avoiding their second three-game losing streak under his leadership while proving they still have what it takes to compete in the division.

articles.title: Brian Schottenheimer drops Jerry Jones truth bomb regarding Cowboys’ trade deadline plans
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys are sitting at 2-4, but Jerry Jones refuses to wave the white flag.
articles.summary: The Cowboys are sitting at 2-4, but Jerry Jones refuses to wave the white flag.
articles.body:
With a 2-4 record, the idea that the Dallas Cowboys could completely change their approach ahead of the NFL trade deadline is beginning to gain traction. Instead of making the aggressive moves that have traditionally defined the franchise, some believe Dallas should shift into seller mode before November 10 to recover some of the draft capital it has spent in recent moves.

The Cowboys are projected to have only four picks in the 2027 NFL Draft and have already surrendered a second-round selection in 2028 . Because of that, some analysts have suggested a potential partial sell-off of key pieces, with George Pickens emerging as one of the names to watch, especially since Dallas has not played like the championship contender it expected to be.

However, that scenario does not appear to be part of the organization’s plans. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones is not ready to give up on the season, and head coach Brian Schottenheimer backed that mindset when he was asked Thursday at The Star whether the team should stop pursuing moves before the deadline.

“No. 1, Jerry is never afraid to make moves. And No. 2, no, we’ve got a lot of football left. And we’re excited about winning a big game in Philadelphia,” Schottenheimer said.

Cowboys rule out becoming sellers at the trade deadline

Despite their difficult start, Dallas remains in the playoff race, largely because of the situation in a battered NFC East . Two starting quarterbacks in the division have already been ruled out for the remainder of the season, while another, Jayden Daniels , has struggled after suffering a dislocated elbow.

As long as that opportunity remains, the Cowboys do not appear willing to abandon the season before the trade deadline.

Jones was asked during the league meetings in New York about his approach heading into the deadline and left the door open for Dallas to be active if the right opportunity presents itself.

“I’ll be real clear, I could see being active at the trade deadline if it was something that could help the team this year,” Jerry Jones said.

When reporter Albert Breer directly asked Jones if he could envision Dallas acting as sellers before the deadline, the Cowboys owner gave a blunt response:

With the pressure mounting and a crucial matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles approaching, the Cowboys will have little margin for error to prove they can still compete — or risk being forced to reconsider their plans before the trade deadline.

articles.title: Michael Irvin loses his temper and insults the Cowboys players: “Jokers”
articles.standfirst: The Super Bowl winner hits out at Dallas after their loss to the Green Bay Packers
articles.summary: The Super Bowl winner hits out at Dallas after their loss to the Green Bay Packers
articles.body:
Michael Irvin has delivered a scathing assessment of the Dallas Cowboys after their 23-13 defeat to the Green Bay Packers , questioning whether the latest setback will prompt any meaningful improvement.

The franchise legend expects more disappointment unless the team addresses the defensive problems that have repeatedly undermined its performances as the loss at Lambeau Field marked Dallas ' third defeat in a primetime game this season, leaving the Cowboys at 2-4.

Irvin was particularly frustrated by the familiar mistakes he witnessed against Green Bay , insisting the NFC East team's latest performance offered little reason to believe a turnaround was imminent.

“I couldn’t even put nothing with that, like hoping that that would be the last,” Irvin said on The White House podcast. “I know this won’t be the last with them jokers out there playing the way they’re playing.

“This, I knew was going to happen. That’s why I sucked it and enjoyed all of my victories Saturday night. I enjoyed my victory Saturday night because I knew Sunday night was going to be different. And it was. The same exact things, man.”

His anger centered on Dallas ' inability to prevent opposing receivers from finding space in its secondary as the Cowboys entered the matchup with Green Bay after an underwhelming defensive display against Tampa Bay Rays .

And the former wide receiver believes the issues remain unresolved heading into a Week 7 clash with the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football.

“I saw the exact same s**t I’ve been seeing in all the other weeks,” Irvin said. “People running wide open in the flats. People running wide over across the field. We sat here and watched football all day long.

“I have not seen anyone running as wide open as we saw when we watched the Green Bay Packers wide receiver running through that secondary of the Dallas Cowboys.”

Cowboys struggle as Prescott's turnovers prove costly

Jordan Love completed 23 of 41 passes for 276 yards, throwing one touchdown and one interception as his numbers could have been even better, with Matthew Golden dropping two potential scoring passes and Christian Watson unable to complete another catch.

Love connected with Golden for a nine-yard touchdown on the Packers ' opening drive before scoring on a one-yard run. Green Bay 's offense created further opportunities throughout the contest, while its defense restricted Dallas to just 13 points.

Whilst Dak Prescott completed 34 of 54 passes for 258 yards, throwing a late six-yard touchdown to Ryan Flournoy . However, interceptions halted consecutive Cowboys possessions that had reached inside Green Bay 's 30-yard line.

The Cowboys trailed 17-0 at halftime, their first scoreless opening half since November 2021 and also committed 11 penalties for 108 yards in a game that featured 22 flags between the teams, meaning the Dallas needed to correct their mistakes rather than repeat them.

articles.title: The Cowboys have turned Dak Prescott into something he was never meant to be: how much longer can he keep it up?
articles.standfirst: Dak Prescott is taking too many hits as heavy blitzes expose the Cowboys’ biggest problem
articles.summary: Dak Prescott is taking too many hits as heavy blitzes expose the Cowboys’ biggest problem
articles.body:
D ak Prescott is throwing more than ever, and opposing defenses are making him pay for it. The Cowboys quarterback has attempted 246 passes in six games, an average of 41 per game and pressure has piled up during Dallas’ two straight losses.

The concern is not simply that Prescott is getting hit. Teams are sending extra defenders after him, and Dallas has struggled to find an answer.

Opponents are sending extra players after Dak

One reason Prescott is under pressure is the blitz. That’s when the opposing defense sends extra players to rush the quarterback, hoping to reach him before he can throw. The Cowboys’ blockers have to pick them up, while Dak has less time to find a receiver.

The Buccaneers and Packers used that approach against Dallas. Prescott faced 34 pressures over the last two games, including 21 against Green Bay. That’s a 35.4% pressure rate across his 96 pass attempts in those games, well above the 22.4% league average cited by Pro Football Reference.

The Cowboys’ coach knows Dak is taking too much punishment. “Dak got hit way too much in these last two games,” Brian Schottenheimer said, adding that the team has to keep him clean.

It’s harder for Dallas to slow down those rushes when the running game isn’t working. The Cowboys are averaging 76 rushing yards per game, near the bottom of the league. When they can’t make defenses respect the run and they fall behind they end up asking Dak to throw even more.

Dallas needs to block better, give the running game a chance and find quick plays that help him get the ball out safely.

The Cowboys visit the Eagles in Week 7. If they don’t give Prescott more help, opposing defenses will keep testing the same weakness and the question of how much he can carry will only get harder to ignore.

articles.title: Brian Schottenheimer denies that his job is in jeopardy following the 2-4 record that has Jerry Jones so concerned
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys head into a massive clash with the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7
articles.summary: The Cowboys head into a massive clash with the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7
articles.body:
Brian Schottenheimer is refusing to abandon his approach as the Dallas Cowboys struggle at 2-4, with consecutive defeats exposing defensive problems and recent offensive inconsistency.

The head coach remains confident he can reverse the slide without surrendering play-calling duties as Schottenheimer , who took charge in 2025, has managed just one week above a .500 record and sits at 9-13-1 overall.

With pressure mounting, owner Jerry Jones will be watching closely as Dallas prepares for a crucial divisional meeting as the Cowboys have lost to the Green Bay Packers and Tampa Bay Buccaneers whilst they also blew a golden chance to beat the Baltimore Ravens .

The struggles are raising questions about whether a change in offensive leadership could help but Schottenheimer has no plans to hand over the playcalling duties heading into Week 7 as the season hangs in the balance.

“No, absolutely not,” Schottenheimer said to 105.3 The Fan. “I have incredible confidence in our offense. We have not played well the last two weeks, we have addressed a lot of the reasons why. We haven’t changed who we are.

“We are still a good explosive offense with weapons. We can hurt you a lot of different ways. I certainly haven’t lost the ability to call plays. I’m an elite play-caller in this league, and it can change around quickly.”

His confidence comes despite the Cowboys ' recent results, although their overall offensive production has not collapsed as Dallas ranks 12th in points scored and 13th in total yards.

The offense is generally okay outside of specific moments but it’s the other side of the football that is the issue as turnovers and a struggling defense contributing heavily to the team's problems.

Cowboys defense faces another major test against Philadelphia

Dallas has allowed 26.5 points and 382.5 yards per game, ranking 25th in scoring defense and 31st in total yards allowed and the unit has also struggled to generate takeaways, recording just three, while surrendering 149.8 rushing yards per game.

The worst mark in the league, the Cowboys ' offensive line presents a contrasting picture, but the tackle positions remain vulnerable and consistently gives up pressure, opening the door for Philadelphia to exploit those weaknesses.

Although injuries have depleted its edge-rushing options as Jalyx Hunt , Nolan Smith and Jonathan Greenard are all dealing with injuries, the Eagles ' task of disrupting Dak Prescott and the Dallas offense is a favorable one.

But the Eagles enter the matchup with problems of their own as four consecutive defeats have intensified scrutiny of their offense, which ranks near the bottom of the league in scoring and total yardage.

Injuries to Jalen Hurts and Saquon Barkley have contributed, but questions about coaching and execution remain as Nick Sirianni struggles on playcalling just two years on from his Super Bowl win.

Dallas could look to establish a more balanced attack against a Philadelphia team struggling to sustain drives as Javonte Williams has scored seven rushing touchdowns this season, along with a receiving score, despite averaging only 3.7 yards per carry.

Prescott 's passing volume has been substantial, while CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens have emerged as productive targets as the duo have combined for 1005 yards and five touchdowns.

One thing not in doubt is that Monday’s NFC East showdown therefore carries significance for both struggling teams.

articles.title: A few words from Jerry Jones confirm the Cowboys' interest in signing Troy Aikman
articles.standfirst: Aikman has hinted he will leave ESPN at the end of his current contract
articles.summary: Aikman has hinted he will leave ESPN at the end of his current contract
articles.body:
J erry Jones has offered a fresh indication that Troy Aikman could have a future in the Dallas Cowboys ' front office, praising the former quarterback's football knowledge and ability to succeed in a leadership role. The comments come as Dallas struggles at 2-4 and questions grow about its direction as when asked about the possibility of bringing Aikman into the organization, Jones was enthusiastic about what the three-time Super Bowl champion could offer.

Although no appointment has been confirmed, the Cowboys owner and general manager made clear that he considers Aikman qualified for the challenge and Jones made his feelings clear. “Well, that’s a loaded question,” Jones said on 105.3 The Fan. “[There’s] nobody more qualified than Troy Aikman. I’m a big Troy Aikman believer in terms of his ability to get the job done. I don’t know anybody who knows more [about] football.” It was not the first time Jones had addressed the prospect this month as he similarly praised Aikman 's potential at an owners meeting in New York , despite previously acknowledging that the Cowboys had not approached him about a front-office position. “No, I think when I said no, Troy is very capable,” Jones said. “And he’s so, really, relatively speaking, he’s in his youth as careers go and he’s very capable of doing any one of a number of things, certainly anything to do with football. “I don’t know of any area, short of getting back out on the field. I don’t know of any area that Troy wouldn’t be qualified and competent to go into.” Aikman has already gained experience away from broadcasting, serving as a special consultant for the Miami Dolphins during their search for a new general manager and head coach earlier this offseason. He has also previously indicated that working with Jones again would not necessarily be an obstacle. However, Dallas remains a particularly complicated destination because Jones has maintained control of football operations since purchasing the franchise. His son Stephen Jones is heavily involved in personnel decisions, while other members of the family occupy senior executive positions.

Aikman's ESPN future adds intrigue as Cowboys struggle

The timing of Jones ' comments is notable because Aikman is approaching the end of his five-year ESPN deal as his future beyond the season remains uncertain – especially after Joe Buck has reportedly secured a six-year, $1.08 million extension agreement. Aikman is reported to be furious with the fact that he wasn’t told about the sum involved by the network or Buck, and he has said he will become a free agent after ESPN 's first Super Bowl broadcast in February 2027. articles.title: The Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders strike a life-changing deal with Jerry Jones
articles.standfirst: The iconic dance squad has secured official union recognition from the Cowboys, opening the door to negotiations over pay, benefits and working conditions
articles.summary: The iconic dance squad has secured official union recognition from the Cowboys, opening the door to negotiations over pay, benefits and working conditions
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders have scored a significant victory away from the football field, with owner Jerry Jones ' organization agreeing to recognize their newly formed union as their official representative in future contract negotiations.

Announced on Friday, October 23, the development marks an important milestone for one of the most recognizable cheerleading squads in professional sports.

The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Association (DCCA) will now represent the dancers in collective bargaining with the franchise, giving them a formal route to negotiate pay, benefits and workplace expectations.

The agreement follows years of debate over the compensation offered to cheerleaders, whose performances and public appearances have become a major part of the Cowboys ' identity.

However, while the union's recognition is a significant step forward, the two sides have not yet announced a new collective bargaining agreement or any additional salary increases.

In a statement announcing the development, the Cowboys organization praised the squad's contribution to the franchise.

"The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders are an esteemed part of the Cowboys organization, deeply respected for the talent and dedication they exhibit," it read. "They remain one of the most sought-after opportunities for talented dancers worldwide."

The announcement quickly attracted attention from fans, many of whom celebrated the cheerleaders' success while questioning why the squad had needed to fight so hard for better compensation in the first place.

How the cheerleaders reached this turning point

The road to union recognition has been shaped by years of complaints about pay and working conditions.

A major moment came in 2019, when the Cowboys settled a lawsuit brought by former cheerleader Erica Wilkins over allegations of unfair compensation. The settlement doubled the game-day rate from $200 to $400 and increased hourly pay.

The issue returned to the spotlight through Netflix's America's Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders.

The documentary series offered viewers a closer look at the demanding preparation, physical commitment and pressures associated with making the squad.

The second season, released in 2025, also highlighted the cheerleaders' campaign for higher salaries.

Members reportedly secured a 400% pay increase that year, a substantial improvement after years of concerns about whether their compensation reflected the work involved.

The latest agreement could give the dancers a stronger position in future discussions, rather than leaving individual members to raise concerns without collective representation.

The exact priorities for the first round of negotiations have not yet been announced, but wages, benefits and working conditions are central issues the union can address.

Fans were quick to express their support online. One supporter celebrated the decision while taking a dig at the struggling football team, writing: "Good. They deserve better pay since they are the only ones on the team that win."

Another fan focused on the financial side of the announcement, posting: "That's amazing. Their pay and benefits are ridiculous. Get that bag, ladies."

A further supporter drew on personal experience as a dancer, writing: "As someone who was paid $25 a game dancing for the Chicago Bulls , I love this," adding, "Cheerleaders and dancers bring a lot of entertainment value to events, and it's about time they're not only appreciated, but paid!"

Others expressed hope that the development could inspire similar changes across professional sports.

One fan wrote: "Hopefully this will evolve into an NFL cheer union so every NFL Cheer squad can be in it. It'll be like how the players have the NFLPA."

The Cowboys cheerleaders' growing visibility has helped bring these concerns to a much wider audience.

Their Netflix exposure has turned the squad into a recognizable entertainment brand, while also drawing attention to the difference between their public profile and the compensation they historically received.

The wider significance is clear: union recognition gives the cheerleaders a collective voice, although it does not guarantee that every demand will be accepted. The eventual outcome will depend on negotiations between the DCCA and the Cowboys .

Meanwhile, the football team has its own problems to solve. Dallas entered Week 7 with a 2-4 record following a 23-13 defeat to the Green Bay Packers . The Cowboys are scheduled to face the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday, October 26, at 8:15 p.m. ET.

For the cheerleaders, however, the union announcement represents progress after years of campaigning. The next step is turning that recognition into a contract that reflects their contribution to one of the NFL's biggest franchises.

articles.title: Troy Aikman opens the door to a return to his Cowboys and sends a message to Jerry Jones: "If Jerry came to me..."
articles.standfirst: The Dallas legend says he would welcome a conversation with the Cowboys owner about a possible role in the organization
articles.summary: The Dallas legend says he would welcome a conversation with the Cowboys owner about a possible role in the organization
articles.body:
Troy Aikman has made his position clear: if Jerry Jones believes the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback could help improve the franchise, he would be willing to listen.

The Pro Football Hall of Famer has spent years working as one of the leading voices in NFL broadcasting, but his future beyond the current season is uncertain.

With his ESPN contract due to expire after the upcoming Super Bowl, speculation has intensified over whether Aikman could move into a football operations role.

Now, his latest comments have given Cowboys supporters a reason to wonder whether a reunion could become a genuine possibility.

Speaking to Mike Fisher on the Fish Report, Aikman was asked whether he would sit down with Jones to discuss a potential return to the organization where he built his legendary playing career. His response was unequivocal.

"Oh, I absolutely would," Aikman said. "I would have lunch, breakfast, or dinner with Jerry anytime he wants it, and it wouldn't necessarily have to be because it's a job interview. We go back a long way, we've been through a lot. Our relationship is complicated, even he would agree with that, but it is one I believe that is built on respect.

"I would welcome any conversation with Jerry ... If Jerry came to me and felt in his heart that I could lend some services that would help make them better, I'd have a hard time not taking a good look at that."

Those comments represent a significant opening for a franchise that has not won a Super Bowl since the 1995 season. Aikman has not committed to joining Dallas, but he has made it clear that he would not automatically dismiss an approach from Jones.

Jerry Jones has already praised Aikman's football knowledge

The possibility of Aikman returning to the Cowboys gained momentum after Jones publicly expressed confidence in his former quarterback's abilities.

Speaking on Dallas sports radio station 105.3 The Fan, the Cowboys owner gave a strong endorsement of Aikman's football credentials: "(There's) nobody more qualified than Troy Aikman . ... I'm a big Troy Aikman believer in terms of his ability to get the job done. I don't know anybody who knows more (about) football."

Jones ' comments suggest that he recognizes the experience and knowledge Aikman could bring to the organization.

The former quarterback understands the demands of playing at the highest level and has spent decades analyzing the modern NFL through his broadcasting career.

However, admiration alone does not guarantee a reunion. The Cowboys would need to identify a position that fits Aikman's expertise and determine how his responsibilities would work within the franchise's existing structure.

Dallas is currently struggling through a difficult 2026 campaign. The Cowboys entered Week 7 with a 2-4 record after losing to the Green Bay Packers , leaving them third in the NFC East and facing mounting pressure to improve.

Against that backdrop, bringing in an experienced football voice could appeal to supporters looking for changes beyond the playing roster.

Aikman's complicated history with Dallas could shape a reunion

Aikman was the first overall pick in the 1989 NFL Draft, becoming the first player selected after Jones purchased the Cowboys . Their partnership helped transform Dallas into a dominant force during the 1990s.

Across his 12 seasons with the franchise, Aikman won three Super Bowls and became one of the most accomplished quarterbacks of his generation. He was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2006.

Despite that shared success, Aikman has acknowledged that his relationship with Jones has not always been straightforward.

Their history includes years of professional collaboration, disagreements and the challenges that can arise when a franchise's owner plays such a prominent role in football decisions.

Aikman's description of their relationship as complicated is therefore particularly significant. Rather than suggesting that every past issue has disappeared, he emphasized the respect that he believes remains between them.

That could provide a foundation for a conversation about the Cowboys ' future, even if the pair do not agree on every aspect of how the organization should operate.

Could Aikman leave broadcasting for a football role?

Aikman's contract with ESPN is due to expire after the 2026 season, culminating in the network's coverage of Super Bowl LXI in February 2027. He has said he expects to become a free agent at the end of the season and will consider his options.

His future is not limited to a possible return to Dallas. Aikman worked as a consultant for the Miami Dolphins during the offseason, helping the franchise with its searches for a general manager and head coach.

That experience demonstrated that his knowledge could be useful away from the broadcast booth.

A move into a front office would represent a significant change, particularly given the lucrative nature of his television career. But Aikman's comments suggest that the opportunity to help an NFL team improve could be worth considering if the right circumstances emerged.

He has also indicated that a specific title would not necessarily be the deciding factor. A consulting position, an advisory role or another football-related job could all be possibilities if both sides believed the arrangement would work.

For Dallas, the question is whether Jones is prepared to turn his public praise into a concrete offer. The owner has shown that he values Aikman's judgment, while the former quarterback has now confirmed that he would welcome a conversation.

There is no agreement in place, and Aikman has not announced plans to leave broadcasting for the Cowboys . Still, his willingness to listen changes the conversation around a potential reunion.

If Jones believes his former quarterback can help guide the franchise through its current struggles, he now has a clear invitation to make contact. Whether that leads to breakfast, lunch or dinner remains to be seen, but Aikman has left the door open.

articles.title: Dak Prescott puts an end to the Cowboys' losing streak and points out the problem Dallas is facing
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys quarterback knows time is running out for Dallas after consecutive defeats
articles.summary: The Cowboys quarterback knows time is running out for Dallas after consecutive defeats
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys can’t afford to let their season slip further away. At 2-4, Dallas heads into Monday night’s NFC East clash against the Philadelphia Eagles following consecutive defeats to Tampa Bay and Green Bay, scoring just 29 points across those games.

Quarterback Dak Prescott understands that the team must respond quickly if it hopes to remain competitive in the division.

Although there’s still an opportunity to improve their standing, the Cowboys can’t continue wasting chances against opponents they believe they should beat.

“I would say determined, and I would hope urgent,” Prescott said. “We can only say ‘we’ve got a lot of games in front of us’ for so long. Might be already past us, right? We’ve got to go win. Gotta go win. You’ve gotta go win.

“You want to give yourself a chance to be a winning team, to be a playoff team, you’ve got to win as many games as you can.

When you drop two games, and particularly games that we didn’t expect to drop, it makes it that much harder. So urgent, urgent to get it done now.”

A stronger running game could transform Dallas’ offense

The Cowboys’ rushing attack needs to become a more dependable part of Dallas’ offensive strategy. Establishing the run would make Dallas less predictable, prevent defenses from concentrating exclusively on Prescott’s passing game and create better opportunities for play-action plays.

A productive ground attack could also help the Cowboys control possession and give the offense a more balanced approach. Without that consistency, opposing defenses can focus on disrupting Prescott and forcing mistakes when Dallas falls into obvious passing situations.

Philadelphia defensive coordinator Vic Fangio presents another challenge. The Eagles frequently rely on four or fewer pass rushers, but Prescott expects they could increase their blitzing after Dallas struggled to handle pressure in recent games.

He doesn’t anticipate Fangio abandoning his defensive principles, although he believes the coordinator could adjust his approach against the Cowboys.

Dallas must therefore improve its protection and capitalize on opportunities when they arise. Prescott entered Week 7 with 1,639 passing yards, 10 touchdowns and five interceptions, completing 66.3% of his passes.

While those numbers demonstrate his contribution through the air, the offense needs to become more reliable in every area.

Reducing turnovers will also be essential. Costly mistakes can erase promising drives and put additional pressure on a defense that’s already struggled to deliver consistent performances this season.

Prescott has also welcomed the challenge of playing at Lincoln Financial Field, where Philadelphia’s passionate supporters create an intimidating road environment.

“It’s one of the few opportunities that you get that you feel like you’re truly on the road,” Prescott said. “You know you’re hated. It’s you guys and those guys on that sideline versus the world, it feels like.

“And that’s what football is supposed to be when you go on the road and you go to someone else’s house.”

Monday night offers Dallas an opportunity to regain momentum, but the team must address its offensive shortcomings if it wants to keep its postseason hopes alive.

articles.title: Cowboys legend calls out Brian Schottenheimer for his ill-advised comments about George Pickens
articles.standfirst: Brian Schottenheimer’s criticism of George Pickens doesn’t sit well with Cowboys legend
articles.summary: Brian Schottenheimer’s criticism of George Pickens doesn’t sit well with Cowboys legend
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer has drawn criticism for publicly challenging George Pickens , prompting franchise legend Dez Bryant to question whether the coach’s approach could create unnecessary pressure for the star receiver.

Ahead of Dallas’ matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles, Schottenheimer emphasized that Pickens must contribute beyond catching passes.

The coach specifically highlighted blocking responsibilities and helping the running game, stressing that every player must embrace a team-first mentality.

While some believe the public criticism could motivate Pickens to improve, Bryant sees potential problems with handling the situation this way.

Responding to former ESPN reporter Ed Werder on X, Bryant reminded critics that Pickens has emotions and shouldn’t be judged solely on his performances.

“At the end of the day...Pickens is still human,” Bryant wrote on X. “He has emotions. The Cowboys only go to him in notable, critical situations and rely on him to make a play...all because of his contract.

“The psychology behind it is what’s messed up, and it doesn’t work in his favor when the world thinks he doesn’t care… let’s really talk about it.”

Schottenheimer , however, believes Pickens ’ responsibilities extend beyond making receptions, as the coach explained that effective blocking helps create running lanes, while receivers who contribute away from the ball can make the offense more dangerous.

George Pickens responds as Cowboys face mounting pressure

Pickens offered a measured response when reporters asked about Schottenheimer’s remarks. Rather than challenging his coach, the receiver maintained that he was following instructions and emphasized the importance of improving collectively.

“I’m doing what they tell me to do,” Pickens said according to NBC Sports. “I feel like if you narrow the comments down, you’re talking about the team. Most definitely, I feel like as a team, just keep improving.”

Pickens ’ response seemed to downplay any potential tension between the two, although it didn’t resolve the debate over whether Schottenheimer should have addressed his concerns publicly.

The receiver’s production highlights why he remains valuable to Dallas. Through six games, he had recorded 33 receptions for 428 yards, establishing himself as an important component of the passing attack. His longest reception was 53 yards, demonstrating his ability to generate explosive plays.

Nevertheless, Pickens has faced questions about his involvement, particularly with CeeDee Lamb receiving more targets. Finding ways to utilize both receivers effectively will be crucial as Dallas attempts to revive an inconsistent offense.

Pickens also enters the season under the franchise tag, leaving his long-term future uncertain. Although he hasn’t publicly expressed frustration over his contract situation, the circumstances add another dimension to Bryant’s concerns about the pressure surrounding him.

Schottenheimer’s expectations aren’t necessarily unreasonable because blocking, discipline and off-ball contributions matter, especially when an offense struggles to establish its running game, but potentially exposing a player to additional public scrutiny is a risky move.

Whether Schottenheimer’s comments inspire Pickens or simply intensify the spotlight remains uncertain.

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders want My Chemical Romance to change its controversial concert costumes
articles.standfirst: The company sent the band a cease-and-desist letter that could impact future shows
articles.summary: The company sent the band a cease-and-desist letter that could impact future shows
articles.body:
T he Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders are taking legal action against M y Chemical Romance after the rock band featured dancers wearing uniforms resembling the iconic blue-and-white outfits during a violent staged shootout at a sold-out Hollywood Bowl concert.

Pro Silver Star Ltd., the company that owns the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders (DCC) brand, filed for a temporary restraining order and temporary injunction on Friday, October 23, accusing the band of misusing the cheerleaders’ federally registered uniform and damaging the brand’s reputation. The filing seeks to stop the disputed costumes from appearing in the band’s remaining Hollywood Bowl performances.

At the center of the dispute is a theatrical sequence in My Chemical Romance’s production of The Black Parade , which transforms the band’s 2006 concept album into a dystopian stage spectacle complete with pyrotechnics and simulated armed conflict.

During the October 21 performance, female dancers wearing outfits resembling the DCC uniform appeared onstage with rifles before being depicted as casualties in a staged firefight, according to the complaint filed by attorney Alex Spiro.

The company says it is not trying to dictate the band’s music

Silver Star argues that the resemblance was so convincing that some concertgoers and social media users believed the performers were actual Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, creating an unwanted association between the organization and the violent scene. The company included side-by-side images of the official uniform and the concert costumes, along with screenshots of online reactions, in its filing.

Cowboys Cheerleaders say the issue is the uniform, not the performance

Silver Star is drawing a distinction between My Chemical Romance’s artistic freedom and its use of a recognizable brand identity. The company says it is not trying to dictate the band’s music, choreography, political messaging or decision to stage a simulated gun battle. Instead, it wants the performers to stop wearing costumes it considers too similar to the DCC uniform.

“Silver Star does not ask Defendants to change their setlist, narrative, politics, choreography, or even their decision to put gun-toting performers on stage. Silver Star asks only that those performers not wear the DCC Uniform while doing it,” the filing states. “The universe of alternative costume designs is effectively unlimited,” it adds.

The company also says it sent My Chemical Romance a cease-and-desist letter on October 22. According to the complaint, the band did not comply with the request, prompting Silver Star to seek emergency court intervention. The legal dispute centers on the uniform’s protected status and whether its use in the concert production infringes Silver Star’s rights or damages the goodwill associated with the DCC brand. The allegations have not yet been resolved by a court.

My Chemical Romance faces pressure ahead of more shows

The timing gives the dispute immediate consequences. My Chemical Romance has additional Hollywood Bowl performances scheduled for October 24, 30 and 31, following the October 21 opening show and the October 23 performance.

Silver Star’s request for a temporary restraining order and injunction puts the disputed costumes at the center of a legal fight that could affect the remaining dates. A request for emergency relief, however, is not the same as a court order; the filing itself does not establish that the band is legally prohibited from using the outfits.

My Chemical Romance had not immediately responded to The Wrap’s request for comment, according to the publication’s report. The concern for the Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders is protecting a carefully cultivated identity. The question now is whether a court will intervene before the band’s Hollywood Bowl run concludes.

articles.title: The player who fits the profile Jerry Jones is eyeing for the Cowboys ahead of the deadline has been revealed
articles.standfirst: Cowboys identify $76 million pass-rusher as ideal trade target after Joey Porter Jr. deal
articles.summary: Cowboys identify $76 million pass-rusher as ideal trade target after Joey Porter Jr. deal
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys could make another significant move before the NFL trade deadline, with Arizona Cardinals pass-rusher Josh Sweat emerging as a potential target for owner and general manager Jerry Jones.

After acquiring cornerback Joey Porter Jr. from the Pittsburgh Steelers, Dallas appears to be considering another defensive addition to address its disappointing start to the 2026 season.

ESPN insider Jeremy Fowler reported that league executives view Sweat as an ideal fit for the Cowboys. Dallas is 2-4 after losing 23-13 to the Green Bay Packers, but the NFC East remains within reach.

With the November 10 deadline approaching, Jones could decide that strengthening the defense is essential to keeping the team's playoff hopes alive.

Dallas' defensive struggles are substantial as the team has ranked near the bottom of the league in total defense and sacks, making pressure on opposing quarterbacks a clear priority.

Josh Sweat emerges as a potential solution for Dallas

Fowler's report highlights Dallas' need for additional edge-rushing production, identifying Sweat as a player who matches the organization's profile.

The Cowboys have struggled to pressure opposing quarterbacks consistently, making an established pass-rusher an attractive option as they attempt to recover from their early-season setbacks.

Sweat brings valuable experience, having established himself as a productive defensive playmaker during his NFL career. The 29-year-old signed a four-year contract worth approximately $76 million with Arizona in 2025 and remains under contract beyond this season.

He recorded 12 sacks last season, giving Dallas a potential reinforcement with a track record of disrupting offenses.

Arizona's position could influence negotiations. If the Cardinals determine their playoff prospects aren't strong enough, trading a veteran for future draft selections could become an appealing option.

The team has already made a notable move involving wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. and could consider further changes if it prioritizes future assets.

Dallas' recent activity suggests Jones is willing to spend draft capital to improve the roster. The September acquisition of Porter cost the Cowboys a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round selection, demonstrating their willingness to address defensive weaknesses through trades.

That aggressive approach, however, comes with risks.

The Cowboys have limited draft flexibility after several transactions, so surrendering additional picks for Sweat could complicate their long-term plans.

Dallas must decide whether a single pass-rusher can make enough difference to justify another substantial investment, particularly with the team still trying to establish consistency under pressure.

Jones must decide whether another defensive addition can help Dallas compete now. Sweat appears to fit the team's most pressing need, but the price Arizona demands could determine whether the Cowboys pursue him seriously.

articles.title: Troy Aikman launches a scathing attack on a Cowboys wide receiver: "He embarrassed me"
articles.standfirst: The Dallas legend has questioned the Cowboys' route running and effort after consecutive defeats, although he stopped short of identifying the player behind his extraordinary criticism
articles.summary: The Dallas legend has questioned the Cowboys' route running and effort after consecutive defeats, although he stopped short of identifying the player behind his extraordinary criticism
articles.body:
Troy Aikman has delivered a blistering assessment of the Dallas Cowboys ' offense, claiming one wide receiver produced a performance so poor that it left him embarrassed.

The three-time Super Bowl champion did not reveal the player's identity, but his remarks have intensified scrutiny of George Pickens following criticism from head coach Brian Schottenheimer .

Dallas heads into Monday night's NFC East clash against the Philadelphia Eagles under pressure to rediscover its offensive rhythm.

Consecutive defeats to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Green Bay Packers have exposed several weaknesses, leaving quarterback Dak Prescott and his supporting cast facing difficult questions ahead of a crucial divisional matchup.

Speaking to Cowboys reporter Mike Fisher, Aikman made clear that Prescott should not shoulder all the responsibility for the team's recent struggles.

The former Dallas quarterback instead pointed to the protection in front of Prescott , arguing that repeated pressure has made the passing game significantly more difficult to execute.

"Last week, I think most people would say it was not a good game for him, but I would tend to disagree a little bit," Aikman explained.

"I don't think it was a good game for everybody. I think you could have put any quarterback out there on the field last week and the results would have been the same. They had way too many free runners on the quarterback.

"Some of that was due to them bringing an extra rusher, but they also had four-man rushes and guys were blowing up Dak . It's hard to play quarterback when that's happening and they change the looks quite a bit."

However, the former quarterback believes the problems extend beyond the offensive line. He was also unimpressed by the receivers' route running, suggesting their inability to consistently create separation has contributed to Prescott's difficulties.

Asked whether Dallas ' wideouts had been running crisp routes, Aikman was unequivocal in his response.

"No, and they haven't [ran crisp routes] in a while," Aikman said.

He subsequently delivered his most severe criticism, revealing that one particular receiver had left him deeply disappointed: "It's a helpless feeling when you're back there and you know you're about to get hit and you've got nowhere to go with the football, so those things have to be better. Brian Schottenheimer , he addressed it, I've talked about it in years past. I won't name names either, but there's one particular player I was embarrassed. It's the worst performance I've ever seen from a wide receiver on a football field."

George Pickens under scrutiny after Schottenheimer's comments

Although Aikman did not name the receiver or specify precisely which performance prompted his assessment, attention has turned towards Pickens .

The speculation follows Schottenheimer's recent comments about the wideout's responsibilities when Dallas has possession of the ball.

The Cowboys coach challenged Pickens to contribute more consistently as a blocker, particularly when the offense is attempting to establish its running game.

“But he needs to understand that he impacts us in the running game as well,” Schottenheimer said. “And he’s got to do the same thing in the run, picking up safeties and blocking corners, just like [running back] Javonte [Williams] does picking up blitzes so he can catch balls. And that’s part of the team-first mindset, and GP does understand that.”

Those remarks have fuelled speculation that Pickens could be the receiver Aikman had in mind. Nevertheless, the former quarterback has not publicly confirmed the player's identity, meaning the connection remains unverified.

There is also important context to consider when evaluating Pickens' contribution. He was one of Dallas' standout performers during the 24-16 defeat against Tampa Bay on October 9, recording nine receptions for 130 yards and a touchdown, according to the Cowboys' official website.

That performance illustrates why the criticism should not automatically be interpreted as a verdict on his entire season.

Aikman's comments were directed at an unnamed player, and his concerns about Dallas ' offense encompass route execution, pass protection and the team's collective discipline.

The former Cowboys star has questioned the receiving corps before. During the 2024 season, he criticised the team's route running and specifically raised concerns about CeeDee Lamb 's execution, arguing that inconsistent routes can make it difficult for a quarterback to anticipate where his targets will be.

Dallas now has an opportunity to respond on the field against Philadelphia. The Cowboys were 2-4 heading into the Week 7 matchup, while the Eagles had also struggled to build momentum, leaving the NFC East contest particularly significant.

For Prescott and the coaching staff, improving protection and getting more dependable contributions from the receivers will be essential.

Aikman's criticism has put the spotlight on the details that can determine whether a passing attack functions effectively, and Monday night's game offers Dallas a chance to show whether those issues are being addressed.

articles.title: Michael Irvin takes credit for Deion Sanders' career: “I put him on the map”
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys legend credits a spectacular interception by Coach Prime for creating an iconic moment during their Miami-Florida State rivalry
articles.summary: The Cowboys legend credits a spectacular interception by Coach Prime for creating an iconic moment during their Miami-Florida State rivalry
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys legend Michael Irvin has made a bold claim about Deion Sanders’ rise to football stardom, suggesting that a memorable moment during their college careers helped introduce Coach Prime to a national audience.

During a YouTube video segment, Irvin revisited the fierce rivalry between the Miami Hurricanes and Florida State Seminoles, recalling a play that became an important moment in Sanders ’ early football journey.

Irvin explained that he regularly jokes with Sanders about being responsible for putting him on the map. However, the former wide receiver clarified that his claim wasn't based on his own reputation.

He believes Sanders ' spectacular performance against him helped create the defensive back's breakthrough moment.

According to Irvin , he ran a route and initially thought he'd beaten Sanders . The young defensive back recovered, intercepted the pass and celebrated while holding the football, creating an image that Irvin recalled being featured in Sports Illustrated.

“It was Miami Florida State, and boom, I ran down up beat him, and he came back and intercepted that ball, pushed me down, caught the ball, and held the ball up and ran the other way,” said Irvin .

“That was the picture they used of his big major coming out in Sports Illustrated. That was the picture I said. I made Deion. But Deion and I came up together.”

Michael Irvin's claim comes with a college football timeline twist

Although Irvin remembers the encounter as a defining moment in their relationship, the timeline requires clarification. Irvin played for Miami during the 1985 season, while Sanders arrived at Florida State as a freshman in 1986. Consequently, they weren't freshmen together, despite Irvin's recollection of their early college days.

Their football paths eventually crossed again in the NFL. Sanders joined the Dallas Cowboys in 1995, reuniting with Irvin after their college rivalry. Together, they helped Dallas capture Super Bowl XXX, adding another memorable chapter to their relationship.

Irvin established himself as one of the most celebrated receivers in Cowboys history, winning three Super Bowls with the franchise before entering the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2007.

Sanders also enjoyed an outstanding professional career, playing for multiple NFL teams, winning two Super Bowls and earning Hall of Fame induction in 2011.

Sanders ' coaching career has recently attracted attention for different reasons. On Saturday, Colorado suffered a 57-24 defeat against Oklahoma State after holding a 24-23 halftime lead. The Buffaloes surrendered 34 unanswered points in the second half, extending their losing streak to five games.

Following the loss, Sanders voiced frustration over his team's struggles to maintain discipline during games, despite meeting expectations in other areas of the program.

“We’re so disciplined in this and that, and this and that, and every darn thing we do, but it seems like as soon as we go in the field, we’re not disciplined,” Sanders said after the game as per Brent Schotenboer of USA Today.

“I really don’t understand it, because we are disciplined in every area of this program, when it comes to academics, when it comes to being somewhere on time, when it comes to wearing the proper uniform, when it comes to just your manners in the building.

“Everything. But [when] we get on the field at the most critical moments, we blow it.”

articles.title: Stephen Jones defends Brian Schottenheimer and downplays the Cowboys' ambitions with controversial remarks
articles.standfirst: Stephen Jones stands by Brian Schottenheimer as Cowboys face mounting pressure after 2-4 start
articles.summary: Stephen Jones stands by Brian Schottenheimer as Cowboys face mounting pressure after 2-4 start
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys executive Stephen Jones has dismissed suggestions that his team has reached must-win territory, despite mounting pressure on head coach Brian Schottenheimer following a disappointing 2-4 start to the season.

Speaking on 105.3 The Fan ahead of Monday night’s divisional showdown against the Philadelphia Eagles, Jones insisted that Dallas still has time to recover and turn its campaign around.

“When we’re this early in the season, I don’t think anything is a must-win game,” Jones said, adding that the team needs to focus on execution rather than outside criticism.

His comments have raised eyebrows among fans who expected far more from a roster built to compete for the NFC East title. Dallas enters the Philadelphia clash following consecutive defeats against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Green Bay Packers, leaving little room for further mistakes.

The latest setback came in Green Bay, where Dallas suffered a 23-13 loss after falling behind 17-0 at halftime. Eleven penalties for 108 yards, two turnovers and an inconsistent offense contributed to another frustrating performance.

Schottenheimer acknowledged the situation afterward, admitting that his team had created its own problems and needed to find a way out of its current predicament.

Stephen Jones backs his coach despite mounting pressure

Rather than intensify speculation about Schottenheimer’s future, Jones publicly defended the coaching staff and expressed confidence that improvements were coming.

He praised defensive coordinator Christian Parker’s progress while conceding that Dallas shouldn't expect an immediate return to the dominance associated with the legendary Doomsday Defense. The Cowboys have surrendered 382.5 yards per game and allowed 26.5 points per contest, highlighting the scale of their defensive struggles.

“I’ve been visiting with our staff on both sides of the ball. I think Christian is feeling better and better each week,” said Jones .

“Certainly, I’m not saying we’re gonna go out there and be the Doomsday Defense or anything like that, but I do feel like we’re getting better each week.”

Jones also backed Schottenheimer’s offensive leadership, describing him as an excellent play-caller and insisting that the coaching staff understands what needs fixing.

Meanwhile, star receiver CeeDee Lamb has offered a different perspective on Dallas’ immediate challenge. Despite the rivalry’s intensity, Lamb dismissed the idea that facing Philadelphia carries special significance for him, treating it as another game on the schedule.

Lamb also admitted that the Cowboys’ position is shocking, given the talent available on offense.

“Very shocking. But at the end of the day, it is the reality of things. Knowing who we have on this offense, all on the same field, we know we deserve to be averaging 30. So, let’s get back to that,” said Lamb .

He also pointed to the competitive NFC East as a reason for optimism, arguing that Dallas still has an opportunity to challenge for the division if it starts performing to its potential.

That opportunity makes Monday’s matchup particularly significant. Philadelphia has dealt with injuries, potentially giving Dallas an opening to regain momentum against its division rival. A victory could restore confidence, while another defeat would intensify scrutiny of Schottenheimer and his staff.

articles.title: Jerry Jones gives a tour of the interior of his $33 million mansion in Texas to remind the Cowboys what they should be striving for
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys owner opens his $33 million home to reveal the Super Bowl trophies and memories his struggling team must aspire to recreate
articles.summary: The Cowboys owner opens his $33 million home to reveal the Super Bowl trophies and memories his struggling team must aspire to recreate
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has offered a rare glimpse inside his Texas mansion, showcasing reminders of the franchise’s most successful years while his current team works to rediscover its winning identity. The tour highlighted the standard Jones still wants Dallas to reach.

Jones welcomed Fox News host Steve Doocy for an eight-minute tour. Features included a dining room seating 12 beneath an impressive chandelier and a foyer chair once used by former US secretary of state Henry Kissinger .

The property’s reported $33 million value adds to its grandeur, but its most meaningful aspects were tied to football.

In the two-storey library, Jones showed off three Super Bowl trophies and championship rings earned during the Cowboys’ dynasty years.

Dallas last won the Super Bowl following the 1995 season, leaving the franchise without a title for nearly three decades. Doocy joked about the missing trophies, highlighting the long wait and the team’s defensive difficulties.

Jones explained the scale of the changes made this season. Dallas has overhauled its defensive personnel, coaching staff and schemes, he said, while acknowledging that the transition has required more time than expected.

"We've changed out the personnel dramatically. We've changed out the coaching staff totally. We've changed out the schemes involved. That first year we won one game,” said Jones .

“We're evolving, but it's probably a little more time needed than I had anticipated when we made these changes this year."

One photograph in the home carries particular significance for Jones . It features Troy Aikman, Emmitt Smith and Michael Irvin , the celebrated trio who helped the Cowboys capture three championships. Jones described their contributions as among the greatest experiences of his life.

Troy Aikman could offer Dallas a path back to greatness

The memories on display also raise questions about whether Aikman could help the Cowboys build another winning era. The Hall of Fame quarterback has long expressed interest in working in an NFL front office, and uncertainty surrounding his broadcasting future could open a door.

Aikman has said he’d welcome a meal and conversation with Jones , whether or not it involved a job interview. Their relationship has been complicated, but he believes it’s grounded in respect.

Aikman was Jones ’ first draft pick and spent 12 seasons leading Dallas, giving him an intimate understanding of the organization.

Jones has praised Aikman’s abilities, saying he’d be qualified for a range of football-related roles. Aikman has also consulted with the Miami Dolphins, although his responsibilities there haven’t developed into a clearly defined front-office position.

There’s no confirmation that Dallas intends to hire its former quarterback for the time being. His broadcasting future also remains uncertain, with Aikman acknowledging that he’s gained a fresh appreciation for the profession as he considers what comes next.

Still, the possibility is intriguing. Aikman could bring championship experience and credibility to a franchise eager to move beyond disappointment.

Jones ’ mansion preserves the Cowboys’ glorious past, but the challenge is translating those memories into present-day results. Whether Aikman becomes part of that effort remains to be seen.

articles.title: "For God's sake, sign Troy!": Desperate Cowboys fans beg Jerry Jones to bring back Aikman
articles.standfirst: Troy Aikman could be open to a Cowboys reunion, and fans are already begging Jerry Jones to make it happen
articles.summary: Troy Aikman could be open to a Cowboys reunion, and fans are already begging Jerry Jones to make it happen
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys supporters are making their feelings clear: they want Jerry Jones to bring franchise legend Troy Aikman back to the organization, potentially giving the Hall of Fame quarterback a role in the team's front office.

Aikman's broadcasting future has become a talking point amid uncertainty surrounding his ESPN role beyond the 2026 NFL season. With questions about his next career move, a return to Dallas could offer an intriguing alternative.

The three-time Super Bowl champion has gained experience away from television, having worked as a consultant for the Miami Dolphins during their search for a general manager and head coach.

Jones has praised Aikman's football knowledge and abilities, suggesting his former quarterback could handle a variety of responsibilities within the sport.

“Troy is very capable, and he’s so, really relatively speaking, he’s in his youth as careers go,” Jones said. “And he’s very capable of doing any one of a number of things, certainly anything to do with football.

“I don’t know of any area short of getting that kind of feeling, I don’t know of any area that Troy Aikman wouldn’t be qualified and competent to go into.”

Cowboys supporters want Aikman back in Dallas

Speaking with Cowboys insider Mike Fisher, Aikman made it clear that he'd welcome a conversation with his former employer. He said he'd happily meet Jones for breakfast, lunch or dinner, even if the gathering wasn't intended as a job interview.

Their relationship, Aikman acknowledged, has been complicated, but remains rooted in mutual respect as he was Jones' first draft pick and spent 12 seasons playing quarterback for Dallas, helping deliver three Super Bowl championships.

Aikman said that if Jones approached him with a genuine opportunity to improve the Cowboys, he'd find it difficult not to seriously consider the offer. That openness has given supporters reason to imagine a reunion.

Fans took to social media to make their wishes known. One pleaded, "For the love of god, hire Troy ASAP," while others urged Jones to sign the former quarterback without delay.

Dallas hasn't reached an NFC Championship Game since the 1995 season, leaving supporters eager for changes that could help the franchise compete at the highest level. They hope Aikman's experience and football knowledge could strengthen decision-making behind the scenes.

However, fan enthusiasm doesn't mean a reunion is imminent. Aikman has previously indicated that Dallas hasn't offered him a front-office position, despite glowing comments.

The biggest obstacle may be the Cowboys' existing management structure. Jones remains closely involved in football decisions, while his son Stephen Jones holds a prominent role in personnel operations. Giving an outside executive meaningful influence could require a clear division of responsibilities and authority.

Neither side has confirmed formal negotiations, but Aikman's willingness to listen has reopened a conversation supporters have wanted to see develop.

Whether Jones acts remains uncertain.

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys vs Philadelphia Eagles: What time is today's game and Where to watch Monday Night Football
articles.standfirst: Two fallen giants of the East collide with pride and the season on the line.
articles.summary: Two fallen giants of the East collide with pride and the season on the line.
articles.body:
There are NFL rivalries that need little introduction, and the one between the Dallas Cowboys and the Philadelphia Eagles is one of them. This Monday, October 26, both teams will meet again on Monday Night Football, with the spotlight on the NFC East .

Cowboys vs Eagles: Time and where to watch Monday Night Football

The Week 7 matchup between Dallas and Philadelphia will be played at Lincoln Financial Field. Kickoff is scheduled for Monday, October 26, at 8:15 p.m. (7:15 p.m. Central Time and 5:15 a.m. Pacific Time). As for NFL season coverage, it's spread across various networks, but you can watch this Monday Night Football game on the following channels and streaming services:

Streaming: Disney+, ESPN App, YouTube TV, Hulu + Live TV, Fubo, DIRECTV, y Sling TV.

The matchup corresponds to Week 7 of the regular season, a stage in which every victory can carry weight in the battle to improve positions within the division.

Preview of the game at Lincoln Financial Field: two teams looking to halt their decline

The standings tell a cruel story for both teams. In the NFC East division, the New York Giants lead with a 3-1-2 record, followed by the Eagles in second place and the Cowboys in third, with the Washington Commanders bringing up the rear. At the conference level, Dallas is ranked 24th and Philadelphia is right behind them at 26th out of 32 teams. The point differential makes for an interesting contrast: the Eagles have scored just 106 points and allowed 137, while the Cowboys have a more prolific offense but an equally porous defense, having given up 159 points. Translated into what we will see on the field: Dallas comes in as the team that moves the scoreboard, while Philadelphia has struggled to find the end zone.

The main duel: the streak they both want to break

Few rivalries in the NFL carry the historical weight of the Eagles vs. Cowboys, but this year both sets of fans are on edge. Recent form offers no comfort to either side. The Eagles started the season with two close wins but have since sunk into a four-game losing streak: 7-27 in Chicago, 20-24 at home against the Rams, 17-19 in Jacksonville , and, most worryingly, a 14-25 loss to Carolina at Linc Stadium last week. Scoring just 14 points at home is the kind of performance that sets off alarm bells. The Cowboys are experiencing a similarly frustrating rollercoaster ride. After falling 20-28 in their season opener against the Giants, they responded with a resounding 37-20 victory over Washington , only to then alternate between a loss, a win, and two consecutive defeats: 16-24 against Tampa Bay and 13-23 in Green Bay. The pattern is clear: when Dallas' offense is on fire, they can compete with anyone; when it's off, their defense can't hold the team together. The good news for the neutral fan: two offenses capable of exploding and two defenses that concede points to a high-scoring game.

Implications for divisional fighting

Although the playoff outlook is bleak for both teams, this is a divisional game, and those carry double the weight emotionally and mathematically. The Giants, leading the NFC East at 3-1-2, are within striking distance: a win here keeps the winner in the hunt for the top spot in a division that no one has dominated. Losing, on the other hand, would leave the defeated team three games behind first place and in a precarious position regarding divisional play-offs, where head-to-head matches carry significant weight. For a team with four losses after six weeks, every game is now practically an elimination match.

What the betting market says for Cowboys vs Eagles and game prediction

Despite being one spot lower in the conference, the Cowboys are the betting favorites. The market assigns them an implied probability of 64.8% (1.52 odds), compared to 35.2% for the Eagles (2.85) as the home team. In the handicap section, Dallas is favored at -4 points (1.96), reflecting confidence in their more productive offense. The total points are around 44 (over 1.93 / under 1.96), a line that supports the expectation of a high-scoring game, given the two porous defenses we'll see at Linc. This is a classic rivalry game where the standings matter less than the momentum of the moment. Dallas has the more reliable offense of the two, and the market reflects that, but playing in Philadelphia is never easy, and the Eagles will be desperate to end a four-game losing streak in front of their home crowd. I'm leaning towards an open game that will be decided in the fourth quarter. If Dallas' offense comes alive—as it did against Washington and Houston—the Cowboys should pull off a close win; if it fizzles out, Philadelphia has the motivation and home-court advantage to pull off an upset. My prediction: Cowboys win by a single point in a high-scoring affair, with over 44 points being the most likely outcome.

articles.title: Former NFL MVP proposes a strange trade involving Dak Prescott to Jerry Jones that could worsen the Cowboys' situation
articles.standfirst: Boomer Esiason has floated a blockbuster quarterback swap between the Dallas Cowboys and Los Angeles Chargers
articles.summary: Boomer Esiason has floated a blockbuster quarterback swap between the Dallas Cowboys and Los Angeles Chargers
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys and Los Angeles Chargers have endured difficult starts to the 2026 NFL season, prompting former NFL MVP Boomer Esiason to suggest a dramatic solution: swapping their starting quarterbacks.

Esiason believes Dak Prescott could benefit from moving to Los Angeles , while Justin Herbert could give Dallas a new direction.

However, although the proposal would generate enormous headlines, it is far from certain that either franchise would improve by making such a significant change.

The Chargers entered Week 7 at 0-6, while Dallas sat at 2-4. Both teams have struggled to meet expectations, but their problems extend beyond the quarterback position.

Speaking on his Kickoff with Boomer and Valenti show, Esiason imagined what the unusual deal could look like.

"Could you see Justin Herbert wearing a Dallas Cowboys uniform? Let's just fantasize about that for a second," he said.

He then outlined the potential exchange: "I mean, Justin Herbert goes to the Cowboys , and Dak Prescott goes to the Chargers , that would be amazing. That would be great for the NFL, great for football. Now, both of these guys probably have no-trade clauses in their contracts.

“But, maybe both of the guys are sick and tired of where they are, by the time we get to the end of the season. I think that would be a dream scenario for all of us who cover the NFL. I don't know that would help, and I don't think Dak is going anywhere."

Why a Herbert-Prescott swap could backfire on Dallas

Herbert , 28, offers Dallas a younger quarterback who could potentially lead the franchise for years. Prescott , 33, brings greater experience, having spent his entire NFL career with the Cowboys since being drafted in 2016.

However, age alone does not make a trade worthwhile. Herbert would have to adjust to a new coaching staff, offensive system and supporting cast, while Prescott would face the same challenge in Los Angeles. Neither quarterback could guarantee an immediate turnaround.

The financial implications could also complicate negotiations. Prescott signed a four-year, $240 million extension in 2024, and Dallas restructured his contract in 2026 to create salary-cap space.

Those moves pushed significant cap obligations into future seasons, making any trade more complicated than simply exchanging quarterbacks.

There is also the question of whether Prescott is actually the Cowboys ' biggest problem. Dallas has struggled defensively, particularly on third downs, while offensive-line issues have added pressure on the attack. Replacing the quarterback would not automatically fix those weaknesses.

Jerry Jones has more immediate concerns

Prescott has already made clear that Dallas cannot afford to keep waiting for its season to improve.

"We can only say we've got a lot of games in front of us for so long. Might be already past us, right? We've got to go win," Prescott said, via ESPN.

"You've got to go win. You want to give yourself a chance to be a winning team, to be a playoff team. You got to win as many games as you can, and when you drop two games, in particular games that we didn't expect to drop, it makes it that much harder. So urgent, urgent to get it done now."

The Cowboys face Philadelphia on Monday night, October 26, in a divisional matchup that could help determine the direction of their season.

Both teams entered the contest at 2-4, making the result particularly important for their playoff ambitions.

For Jones , the priority should be addressing Dallas' broader problems rather than pursuing a headline-grabbing quarterback exchange.

Herbert's age and talent make the idea intriguing, but surrendering an established franchise quarterback could introduce fresh uncertainty at a time when the Cowboys need stability.

Esiason's proposal is an entertaining hypothetical, not a confirmed trade discussion. Unless both quarterbacks and both organisations were willing to consider such a move, it is unlikely to progress beyond debate.

For Dallas, the safer route may be improving the roster around Prescott instead of gambling that a different quarterback would solve everything.
