articles.title: Dez Bryant handcuffed and held at gunpoint by police after Texas road rage incident
articles.standfirst: The retired NFL star has questioned how officers handled a confrontation that ended with him being handcuffed in front of his children
articles.summary: The retired NFL star has questioned how officers handled a confrontation that ended with him being handcuffed in front of his children
articles.body:
Dez Bryant expected an ordinary visit to a restaurant in Texas, but a confrontation with two motorists ended with the former Dallas Cowboys receiver lying on the ground in handcuffs as armed police officers investigated an alleged threat involving a firearm.

The 37-year-old said his girlfriend and children arrived while officers were dealing with the situation, turning what began as a disagreement over reckless driving into a particularly distressing experience for his family.

Footage obtained by OutKick shows Bryant and two other men lying facedown on the ground while police assess the situation. An officer can be seen aiming a rifle in their general direction as a woman tells authorities that nobody involved is carrying a gun.

Bryant has since criticized the officers' approach, arguing that they failed to properly consider his version of events before taking action.

According to Bryant , the confrontation began when two men driving recklessly cut him off as they approached the same restaurant.

The disagreement continued after they stopped, with Bryant claiming one of the men suggested he would produce a firearm during their argument.

"He go to threatening me and basically saying, um, he'll insinuate that he'll, you know, he'll shoot me or whatever," Bryant recalled.

Bryant acknowledged responding aggressively to the alleged threat, telling the man he should be prepared to use a weapon if he produced one.

"You pull that gun, I'm telling you right now, you better use it because if you don't I'm going to do something to you," Bryant said.

No firearm was ultimately produced during the exchange, according to Bryant . Instead, one man began recording with his phone, which the former NFL player admitted pushing away.

Police were subsequently contacted, and Bryant said he welcomed their involvement because he expected them to investigate what had happened.

Ex-Cowboys star describes frightening police response

The situation became more serious when responding officers ordered all three men onto the ground before handcuffing them.

Bryant said his family arrived while the police response was underway, leaving his children to witness their father being detained.

"I get on the ground," Br y ant explained. "My lady pulled up, she got my children, and they seen everything that's going on."

The retired receiver was placed inside a police vehicle while officers questioned those involved. He was eventually released with a citation, while the other two men were also allowed to leave.

Bryant questions police handling of confrontation

Although nobody was injured, Bryant believes the officers should have conducted a more thorough investigation before deciding how to handle the situation.

"I would rather you guys take us all down to the police station and do the proper investigation instead of just taking somebody else's side," Bryant added. "I felt like it was very one-sided."

Despite his criticism, Bryant emphasized that the incident hadn't changed his generally positive relationship with local law enforcement.

He described knowing an officer whose son plays football alongside his child, explaining that their previous interactions had always been friendly.

The 37-year-old said his girlfriend and children arrived while officers were dealing with the situation, turning what began as a disagreement over reckless driving into a particularly distressing experience for his family.

Footage obtained by OutKick shows Bryant and two other men lying facedown on the ground while police assess the situation. An officer can be seen aiming a rifle in their general direction as a woman tells authorities that nobody involved is carrying a gun.
Bryant has since criticized the officers' approach, arguing that they failed to properly consider his version of events before taking action.
According to Bryant , the confrontation began when two men driving recklessly cut him off as they approached the same restaurant.
The disagreement continued after they stopped, with Bryant claiming one of the men suggested he would produce a firearm during their argument.
"He go to threatening me and basically saying, um, he'll insinuate that he'll, you know, he'll shoot me or whatever," Bryant recalled.
Bryant acknowledged responding aggressively to the alleged threat, telling the man he should be prepared to use a weapon if he produced one.
"You pull that gun, I'm telling you right now, you better use it because if you don't I'm going to do something to you," Bryant said.
No firearm was ultimately produced during the exchange, according to Bryant . Instead, one man began recording with his phone, which the former NFL player admitted pushing away.
Police were subsequently contacted, and Bryant said he welcomed their involvement because he expected them to investigate what had happened.

Bryant said his family arrived while the police response was underway, leaving his children to witness their father being detained.

Although nobody was injured, Bryant believes the officers should have conducted a more thorough investigation before deciding how to handle the situation.

articles.title: Jerry Jones fires shots at his own locker room during MNF
articles.standfirst: erry Jones issued a strong warning before Cowboys-Eagles and reminded Dallas of what happened the last time they faced a team with a backup quarterback.
articles.summary: erry Jones issued a strong warning before Cowboys-Eagles and reminded Dallas of what happened the last time they faced a team with a backup quarterback.
articles.body:
B rian Schottenheimer ’s Dallas Cowboy s arrived in Philadelphia to face the Eagles in a tension-filled matchup, while former lineman Marcus Spears recalled the battle spirit that defines this historic rivalry. However, Dallas also faced challenges, as two players were ruled out with injuries before the game.

Franchise owner Jerry Jones knew the contest represented a difficult test, especially against an Eagles team arriving without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts and with Tanner McKee in charge of the offense.

Before the game, Jones spoke with Jason Kelce and Pat McAfee , where he issued a blunt warning about the danger of underestimating Philadelphia.

“The last time we played a team that had a backup quarterback we got our a** kicked, ” Jones said.

The Cowboys owner was referring to the Week 5 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , when Dallas fell 24-16 to a team that started undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels in place of the injured Baker Mayfield .

The Cowboys and Eagles entered the Week 8 Monday Night Football matchup tied for second place in the NFC East , both with 2-4 records, trailing only John Harbaugh’s New York Giants , who sat at 4-2-1.

The pregame buildup was also marked by the reaction of Skip Bayless , one of Dallas’ most well-known fans, who expressed surprise at seeing the Cowboys listed as favorites against Philadelphia. The former FOX Sports analyst is well aware of his team’s inconsistency — capable of showing its best version against tough opponents or falling unexpectedly to inferior teams.

With the game about to begin, the feeling was that a much tighter contest than expected could unfold. Jerry Jones’ warning was no coincidence: few people know the Cowboys’ ups and downs better than the franchise owner himself.

articles.title: Dak Prescott delivers a statement win for the Cowboys against the Eagles on MNF
articles.standfirst: Dak Prescott put on a show under the bright lights, leading the Cowboys to a massive Monday Night Football win over the Eagles.
articles.summary: Dak Prescott put on a show under the bright lights, leading the Cowboys to a massive Monday Night Football win over the Eagles.
articles.body:
D ak Prescott delivered a statement performance under the bright lights, throwing for 212 yards and three touchdowns as the Dallas Cowboys defeated the Philadelphia Eagles 38-21 on Monday Night Football, handing their NFC East rivals a fifth consecutive loss.

Prescott connected twice with CeeDee Lamb for touchdowns and guided Dallas to one of its most complete offensive performances of the season. The victory improved the Cowboys to 3-4, keeping them alive in the NFC East race behind the New York Giants , who lead the division with a 4-2-1 record.

Meanwhile, the Eagles continue to spiral. Philadelphia dropped its fifth straight game , its longest losing streak since 2016, falling to 2-5 in what has quickly become a disastrous season.

With Jalen Hurts expected to miss the remainder of the year due to blood clots in his lungs, the Eagles turned to Tanner McKee , but the young quarterback was unable to provide the spark the team desperately needed. McKee completed 23 of 35 passes for 211 yards , with one touchdown and one interception.

Dallas consistently finished long drives with points, while Philadelphia struggled to keep pace.

After trailing 21-20 late in the third quarter , Prescott found Lamb for his second touchdown of the night on a perfectly placed 16-yard pass in the corner of the end zone . Prescott then added a two-point conversion on the ground to give the Cowboys a 28-21 lead.

Brandon Aubrey contributed with field goals of 55, 27 and 24 yards , extending Dallas’ advantage to 31-21 before Javonte Williams sealed the victory with a two-yard touchdown run.

Williams was one of the biggest stars of the night, rushing for a career-high 155 yards and a touchdown . The Cowboys finished with 204 rushing yards, their first 150-yard rushing performance by a player since Ezekiel Elliott in 2018 .

McKee’s final mistake came late in the fourth quarter when linebacker DeMarvion Overshown intercepted a pass, ending Philadelphia’s hopes of a comeback.

Eagles show brief signs of life but collapse late

Philadelphia finally found offensive rhythm in the third quarter, putting together its first touchdown drive of the season that lasted nearly 10 minutes. McKee connected with rookie Makai Lemon for a four-yard touchdown to give the Eagles a brief 21-20 lead.

But the offense disappeared after that, and Philadelphia failed to score again as its season continued to slip away.

Cowboys strike early in offensive battle

The game started with fireworks from both sides. Dallas opened with a field goal, but Philadelphia responded with Saquon Barkley’s eight-yard touchdown run.

Barkley returned after missing more than two games with a hamstring injury and showed flashes of his old form, but the issue continued to bother him. He finished with 62 rushing yards on seven carries after spending time on the sideline receiving medical attention.

Prescott helped Dallas take control before halftime, throwing touchdown passes to Lamb (nine yards) and George Pickens (21 yards) to give the Cowboys a 20-14 advantage at the break.

Pickens’ touchdown was a highlight-reel play, escaping tight coverage and dragging his left foot in the back of the end zone to complete the spectacular grab.

A tough night during Jeffrey Lurie’s celebration

The loss came on a night when Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie was inducted into the team’s Hall of Fame .

Lurie purchased the franchise in 1994 and helped transform Philadelphia into one of the NFL’s most consistent organizations , including four Super Bowl appearances since 2004 and the two championships in franchise history.

But instead of celebrating on the field, Eagles fans watched their team suffer another painful defeat as the franchise faces one of its biggest challenges in years.

articles.title: Dak Prescott defends Brian Schottenheimer from criticism following Cowboys victory: “I don't blame him”
articles.standfirst: Prescott acknowledged Schottenheimer's frustration with criticism while making clear where the Dallas players stand
articles.summary: Prescott acknowledged Schottenheimer's frustration with criticism while making clear where the Dallas players stand
articles.body:
A convincing victory over the Philadelphia Eagles should have given Brian Schottenheimer plenty to celebrate, but the Dallas Cowboys head coach appeared more interested in leaving his postgame press conference than discussing his team's impressive performance.

Dallas secured a 38-21 win on Monday Night Football, ending a difficult stretch that had intensified scrutiny of Schottenheimer 's offensive decisions and raised questions about the direction of the team.

Yet the coach offered little enthusiasm during his media appearance, delivering unusually brief answers before departing. According to reporter Nick Harris , it was Schottenheimer 's shortest postgame press conference since taking charge.

When someone asked whether he was feeling okay, Schottenheimer responded: "I'm great. Excited for our guys."

Quarterback Dak Prescott , however, suggested there was more behind his coach's restrained reaction, acknowledging the frustration that had accumulated during Dallas' recent struggles.

Prescott didn't attempt to disguise Schottenheimer 's mood when questioned about his coach following the victory.

"Definitely hungry, pissed off version of Shotty," Prescott told reporters. "It's not like he's naive. It's not like he hadn't heard some noise about him.

"And whether it's the call in the games or whatever doubt that's been out there. But we've got his back. He knows that."

The quarterback's remarks reflected the pressure surrounding Schottenheimer after consecutive defeats against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Green Bay Packers left Dallas with a 2-4 record.

Prescott emphasized that the players understood their coach's commitment and remained responsible for delivering improved performances.

"I mean, everybody handles everything differently. And so I don't blame him to an extent," Prescott added.

"And yeah, we've got his back. More importantly, it's just about us going out there and executing on Sundays."

Cowboys offensive problems fuel criticism

The victory over Philadelphia followed two disappointing offensive performances that had raised concerns about Dallas' consistency.

Against Green Bay, the Cowboys managed 303 total yards and committed two turnovers, contributing to a run of five giveaways across two games.

Dallas had also struggled to establish its running game, averaging just 94.3 rushing yards per contest entering the Eagles matchup despite ranking seventh in passing production.

Those problems prompted speculation about whether Schottenheimer should surrender offensive play-calling responsibilities to coordinator Klayton Adams .

Speaking on 105.3 The Fan, radio host Shan Shariff supported such a move.

"I think that Brian Schottenheimer should give the play-calling to Klayton Adams," Shariff said.

Jerry Jones maintains faith

Cowboys owner Jerry Jones had already expressed confidence in the coaching staff before Monday's victory.

"We're in good shape," Jones told 105.3 The Fan, insisting the organization was prepared to address its recent problems.

The win improved Dallas' record to 3-4 and provided Schottenheimer with a welcome response after increasing criticism.

Prescott 's comments also reinforced the support the head coach continues to receive within the locker room, even as outside questions persist.

The Cowboys have demonstrated they can produce an effective offensive performance against a division rival. Their next challenge is proving that Monday's improvement represents a lasting change rather than another isolated result.

articles.title: Brian Schottenheimer finds his formula: Why Dallas must stick with running game after crushing Philadelphia
articles.standfirst: Dallas dominated Philadelphia after abandoning its pass-heavy approach, raising questions about why the adjustment took so long
articles.summary: Dallas dominated Philadelphia after abandoning its pass-heavy approach, raising questions about why the adjustment took so long
articles.body:
Dak Prescott has spent much of the season carrying the responsibility for the Dallas Cowboys ' offense, but Monday night's victory over the Philadelphia Eagles offered a reminder that even an accomplished quarterback benefits from having reliable support on the ground.

After consecutive defeats exposed problems with Dallas' offensive approach, head coach Brian Schottenheimer made a significant adjustment against the Eagles , placing greater emphasis on establishing the running game rather than relying almost exclusively on Prescott's passing.

The change produced immediate results. Dallas rushed for 204 yards on 38 attempts, overwhelming Philadelphia on its way to a convincing 38-21 victory that improved the Cowboys ' record to 3-4.

Prescott finished with 212 passing yards and three touchdowns, producing a 118.1 passer rating despite attempting just 27 throws.

The contrast with Dallas' previous two games was striking, suggesting Schottenheimer may finally have discovered how to get the best from an offense that entered the season with considerable expectations.

Running back Javonte Williams was central to Dallas' resurgence, delivering a career-high 155 rushing yards on 25 carries.

His performance forced Philadelphia to account for the ground attack, creating opportunities for Prescott to operate without facing the same relentless pressure that had disrupted him in previous games.

"We knew we had to create some balance," Prescott said afterward, acknowledging the importance of establishing a dependable running game.

That balance had been largely absent during defeats against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Green Bay Packers .

Dallas ran the ball just 13 times against Tampa Bay before recording 15 rushing attempts across 78 offensive plays in Green Bay.

Opponents exploited that predictability by pressuring Prescott , who completed only 20 of 38 passes for 194 yards without a touchdown against additional rushers across those two games.

Against Philadelphia, Williams ' productivity allowed the Cowboys to dictate the tempo rather than constantly asking Prescott to overcome difficult situations.

Schottenheimer faces important decision

Although Monday's performance represented significant progress, the quality of Philadelphia's defense provides some necessary context.

The Eagles entered the game with four consecutive defeats, significant injury problems and a rushing defense that had struggled throughout the season.

Nevertheless, Dallas' previous victory against the Houston Texans also featured a more balanced offensive approach, with 25 rushing attempts helping produce a 34-30 win.

The consistency between those successful performances suggests Schottenheimer should consider making the running game a permanent foundation of his offensive strategy.

Doing so would also reduce the pressure on Prescott while creating more favorable opportunities for receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens .

Opportunity to build momentum against Cardinals

Dallas will attempt to extend its resurgence when the Arizona Cardinals visit AT&T Stadium on Sunday.

Arizona enters the matchup with a 2-5 record after allowing the Denver Broncos to rush for 159 yards, presenting another opportunity for Williams to influence the outcome.

Schottenheimer has already emphasized the importance of improved blocking from his receiving corps, including Pickens , highlighting the collective effort required to maintain an effective ground attack.

The Cowboys remain below .500, meaning one impressive victory cannot erase their earlier struggles.

However, the win over Philadelphia demonstrated that Dallas can control games without depending entirely on Prescott 's arm.

Schottenheimer 's challenge is to turn that successful adjustment into a consistent approach rather than allowing the offense to return to its previous habits.

articles.title: ‘Treat everybody fair’: Dez Bryant speaks out after assault citation
articles.standfirst: The former NFL star acknowledges knocking a cellphone out of another man's hand during the confrontation
articles.summary: The former NFL star acknowledges knocking a cellphone out of another man's hand during the confrontation
articles.body:
D ez Bryant is demanding a thorough investigation after a confrontation in Southlake, Texas , left the former Dallas Cowboys wide receiver handcuffed on the ground with a police officer pointing a firearm in his direction. Bryant was cited for misdemeanor assault following the Oct. 25 incident, but he maintains that he was threatened before the encounter escalated and questions how officers handled the investigation.

“There’s only one real victim here… and that’s me,” Dez wrote in a social media post as he pushed back against the circumstances that led to the citation. The incident has drawn attention not only because of Bryant’s status as one of the most recognizable players in Cowboys history , but also because his two daughters witnessed the police response. Bryant says his biggest concern was seeing his children watch their father lying on the ground with a gun pointed at him.

The former NFL star acknowledges knocking a cellphone out of another man's hand during the confrontation. However, he argues that the incident should be investigated in full, including the events that preceded the physical contact and the alleged threat against him.

A traffic dispute escalates in a Southlake parking lot

According to Bryant’s account to OutKick , the confrontation began Sunday afternoon after he encountered two drivers he believed were driving recklessly and had cut him off near Kimball Avenue. The parties eventually ended up in the same parking lot near Chiloso Mexican Bistro in Southlake.

Bryant said he approached the drivers to confront them about their behavior on the road. The exchange became heated, and he alleged that one of the men implied he might shoot him.

Dez recalled warning the man that if he pulled a gun, he had better use it. He subsequently acknowledged knocking the man's cellphone out of his hand after the driver began recording the argument. The other man called police, and Bryant said he encouraged him to do so because he expected officers to investigate the alleged threat.

Instead, Bryant said, the responding officers ordered those involved to the ground at gunpoint. Video shared with OutKick shows Bryant and two other men lying facedown in the parking lot in handcuffs, with an officer holding a firearm in Bryant’s direction.

Why police drew their weapons

The Southlake Police Department said officers responded at approximately 12:59 p.m. Sunday to reports of a fight involving multiple people and a possible weapon. According to department spokesperson Capt. Blas Hernandez , officers drew their firearms as a precaution to address potential threats and protect everyone at the scene.

Several people were temporarily detained, but officers recovered no firearms. Police said the confrontation began with a traffic dispute before escalating into an argument and an alleged assault. Bryant was issued a citation for assault by contact, a Class C misdemeanor, and released at the scene. He was not arrested.

Bryant, however, believes the investigation did not adequately consider his allegations. He accused officers of relying too heavily on the other party’s cellphone footage without fully examining what happened before the recording began. He also said he wanted investigators to review any available surveillance footage of the initial traffic incident.

“I felt like it was very one-sided,” Bryant told OutKick, expressing frustration that he was the only person cited. Dez has maintained that he acted in self-defense and wants authorities to conduct a more comprehensive review of the encounter. His citation directs him to appear at Southlake Municipal Court on or before Nov. 20.

Beyond the citation itself, Bryant has emphasized the emotional impact of the police encounter, particularly because his daughters witnessed their father being detained. His girlfriend arrived at the scene with the children and recorded part of the incident. Dez said the sight of an officer pointing a gun in his direction while he was on the ground was especially troubling.

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys Super Bowl hero admits he’s a diehard Eagles fan, and Jerry Jones is fine with it
articles.standfirst: Despite the longstanding rivalry, football is a business after all.
articles.summary: Despite the longstanding rivalry, football is a business after all.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys continue hoping for a true franchise turnaround. It has now been over three decades since they last reached a Super Bowl . Jerry Jones is still leading the way, but he hasn’t been able to capture that 1990s magic.

Aside from not being able to build the same type of roster as before, Jones is also missing an elite head coach like he had in Jimmy Johnson . Jones hired Johnson away from the Miami Hurricanes , where he won a National Championship .

With the Cowboys, Johnson was named Coach of the Year in 1990 then won back-to-back Super Bowls a few years later. After some tension between Jones and Johnson, the two mutually parted ways in 1994 . That's when the Philadelphia Eagles , the Cowboys' division rivals, tried to swoop in to sign Johnson.

Jimmy Johnson nearly was hired by the Philadelphia Eagles right after leaving the Dallas Cowboys

As Johnson recently revealed, the reason he gave the Eagles the light of day is because he's secretly a fan of the franchise . That fandom stems from a close friendship with Jeffrey Lurie , who has been the owner of the Eagles since 1994 .

Apparently, if that had happened, Jones would have had no hard feelings about Johnson heading to a fierce rival. Jones was quoted in 1994 by The Oklahoman as saying: " That'd be good. From my perspective, I think it would be good to play him a couple times a year. I bet he'd like it, too. "

By the sound of it, Johnson very much would have liked joining the Eagles. Johnson chose a different path, though, opting to give a TV analyst gig a shot. But he soon got the coaching itch again, leading to him joining the Miami Dolphins in 1996.

Ray Rhodes was coming off of a Coach of the Year season in 1995 with the Eagles the offseason that Johnson became available. There was no way Lurie would let Rhodes go after such a stellar season to pursue Johnson. Rhodes didn't last much longer, but neither did Johnson in Miami - and the Eagles ended up hiring Andy Reid not long after anyway.

articles.title: Jerry Jones backs Dak Prescott but sends a blunt warning about the Cowboys’ biggest flaws
articles.standfirst: Jerry Jones is standing firmly behind Dak Prescott, but the Cowboys owner knows the team’s biggest problems cannot be ignored.
articles.summary: Jerry Jones is standing firmly behind Dak Prescott, but the Cowboys owner knows the team’s biggest problems cannot be ignored.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys delivered an authoritative statement with their victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football , a win that keeps the team alive in the NFC East race at 3-4. The schedule also looks more favorable for Dallas, with several accessible matchups and a healthy number of home games in November.

However, the Cowboys still face a significant obstacle: the surprising New York Giants , who sit at 4-2-1 and have found a new competitive edge with quarterback JJ McCarthy .

Despite the issues the roster has shown, Dallas appears to have found a path to stay in the fight. Yet one concern could still change the team’s trajectory: the physical condition of star quarterback Dak Prescott .

In the 38-21 win over the Eagles, Prescott finished with 212 passing yards and three touchdowns without an interception . Still, at certain points—especially early in the game—he showed uncharacteristic inaccuracy. Missed throws he normally completes raised questions about whether he is truly at 100 percent.

Dak Prescott is dealing with two injuries this season

The Cowboys quarterback has been playing through discomfort throughout the campaign. The first issue surfaced in Week 4 against the Houston Texans, when he suffered a cut on his hand after an opposing player accidentally stepped on it.

“It’s nothing. It just got stepped on,” Prescott explained after the game.

The more concerning moment came in Week 6 against the Green Bay Packers , when he took a hard hit from Zaire Franklin that affected his ribs.

Prescott himself acknowledged the impact:

“I took a good hit. A hit to the ribs, got the wind knocked out of me. But I wasn’t coming out of the game. It was, just give me a second and we can get back going.”

Jerry Jones dismisses the idea that injuries are affecting Prescott

In an interview with 105.3 The Fan , Cowboys owner Jerry Jones addressed his quarterback’s physical state and denied that the lingering issues explain recent inaccuracies.

“I wouldn’t think there is enough that he is banged up to get into being off on his throws. I just, when I look at how other quarterbacks play, when I look at how they throw the ball, Dak is unique in his way, but I can’t say enough about what he meant to stay in there and the throws that he did make. We just have got to realize, they (the defensive players) have something to do with it, too.”

For the Dallas owner, Prescott showed an improved version against Philadelphia, particularly in reading defenses and making decisions after two difficult outings.

“He’s got to sit there and not only get it to the right one depending on how the defense is playing, but he has got to get it out of there and help his protection. He did that last night. I don’t have any criticism about where he went with the ball or where he threw the ball,” Jones said.

If Prescott is still dealing with residual discomfort, he will have little time to recover. The Cowboys return to action next Sunday at 1 p.m. ET , at a pivotal moment for their aspirations in the NFC East .

articles.title: Russell Wilson pushes Jerry Jones to pull off massive trade for Maxx Crosby
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys need defensive help, and Russell Wilson has a bold solution: make a blockbuster trade for one of the Raiders’ biggest stars.
articles.summary: The Cowboys need defensive help, and Russell Wilson has a bold solution: make a blockbuster trade for one of the Raiders’ biggest stars.
articles.body:
D allas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has earned a reputation as one of the most aggressive owners in the NFL trade market and, with his team sitting at 3-4 and looking to reinforce a vulnerable defense, Russell Wilson believes there is a move capable of changing the course of the season.

During the most recent episode of his digital series “Set Hut!” , the quarterback suggested that Dallas should attempt a high-impact trade for Las Vegas Raiders edge rusher Maxx Crosby . For Wilson, the Cowboys need to take an aggressive stance and add a player who can transform their defensive unit.

"If you're (living in) Jerry's world right now, I'm definitely thinking trades. I'm thinking 'Who can I get? Who can make a difference for us?' It may be an edge rusher. Could it be a Maxx Crosby, for example? Could they go get Maxx Crosby? Can the Dallas Cowboys pull the trigger? I'm just saying…" Wilson said.

"Jerry's not afraid to spend his money, so I'm just saying… If I was the GM of the Dallas Cowboys, I'm knocking on the door… I'm knocking on that door (for Crosby)."

Could Maxx Crosby end up in Dallas?

The 2026 season has not been easy for one of the Raiders’ biggest defensive stars. After a trade attempt with the Baltimore Ravens failed to materialize during the past offseason, Crosby has endured a complicated start to the campaign with Las Vegas, which currently holds a 3-4 record.

In seven games, the star defender has recorded just two sacks, including one-and-a-half in the Week 1 victory over the Miami Dolphins .

However, his low production may be more related to a lack of support around him than to a drop in his level of play. Opposing teams have identified Crosby as the primary threat of the Raiders’ defense, a unit that currently ranks 29th in the NFL .

The biggest obstacle for Dallas would not be Crosby’s talent, but rather the price they would have to pay to acquire him.

The Cowboys already surrendered a first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft as part of the trade for defensive tackle Quinnen Williams , though they still have a first-round selection obtained in the historic move that sent Micah Parsons out of the team.

With the season entering a decisive point, Dallas faces pressure to improve a defense that has shown consistency issues. The arrival of a player like Crosby could give the team a dominant presence on the defensive line.

Now the question is whether Jerry Jones will be willing to make another high-impact move before the trade deadline and whether the Cowboys consider Maxx Crosby the piece they need to compete again in the NFC East.

articles.title: The Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders never tire of winning: the new legal battle has given them another reason to celebrate
articles.standfirst: The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders have scored a significant victory after My Chemical Romance reportedly agreed to stop using controversial lookalike uniforms
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders have scored a significant victory after My Chemical Romance reportedly agreed to stop using controversial lookalike uniforms
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders have another reason to celebrate after their legal challenge against My Chemical Romance reportedly prompted the rock band to abandon the disputed costumes for its remaining concerts.

The dispute began after dancers appeared in blue-and-white outfits resembling the cheerleading squad's famous uniforms during My Chemical Romance 's theatrical performances at the Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles.

The costumes became a source of controversy because the performers subsequently took part in a staged gunfight as part of the production.

Pro Silver Star Ltd., the company that owns the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders brand, responded by seeking a temporary restraining order and an injunction to prevent the band from continuing to use the outfits.

The legal filing argued that the performance risked damaging the reputation of a recognisable name in American sports and entertainment.

Now, according to a subsequent court filing reported on October 28, My Chemical Romance has agreed not to use the costumes during the remaining shows on its current tour.

A lawyer representing the cheerleaders' owner documented the development, writing: “On October 26,2026, I received an email from David Byrnes stating that Defendant My Chemical Romance “will not be performing any remaining shows on its current tour with dancers in the cheerleader costumes your client objects to.””

The reported agreement represents a practical win for the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders , although it does not necessarily mean that every aspect of the wider legal dispute has been resolved.

Why the My Chemical Romance costumes sparked a legal fight

The controversy centres on My Chemical Romance's The Black Parade, a theatrical concert production built around a fictional authoritarian world, dramatic staging and scenes of armed conflict.

During the band's October 21 performance at the Hollywood Bowl, female dancers appeared in outfits that Pro Silver Star said closely copied the cheerleaders' signature look. The costumes featured white boots, white shorts, blue tops and white vests decorated with blue stars.

According to the legal complaint, the performers subsequently carried rifles during a staged firefight and were depicted being shot before crawling offstage. The company argued that placing a recognisable cheerleading uniform in that setting could associate its brand with violence.

The filing also claimed that audience members and social media users mistakenly believed the dancers were actual Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders . The company argued that the resulting online discussion threatened the goodwill built around the squad over decades.

Pro Silver Star's legal action was not a demand for My Chemical Romance to abandon its artistic concept altogether.

Instead, the company argued that the band could continue performing its music and staging the fictional conflict without using outfits resembling the cheerleaders' protected uniform.

The complaint stated: “Silver Star does not ask Defendants to change their setlist, narrative, politics, choreography, or even their decision to put gun-toting performers on stage.

Silver Star asks only that those performers not wear the DCC Uniform while doing it. The universe of alternative costume designs is effectively unlimited.”

A recognisable brand worth protecting

The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders have become one of the most recognisable cheerleading organisations in professional sport.

Their blue-and-white uniforms are closely associated with the Dallas Cowboys , while television appearances and documentaries have helped introduce the squad to audiences beyond American football.

That visibility also makes the uniform an important part of the organisation's identity. Pro Silver Star argued that the costumes were not simply generic stage clothing, but a distinctive design connected to a specific brand.

The case raised questions about where artistic expression ends and commercial identity protection begins.

Musicians regularly use costumes, imagery and theatrical storytelling to create memorable performances, but those creative choices can lead to legal disputes when they resemble protected designs or potentially confuse audiences.

The reported agreement allows the band to continue its shows without the particular outfits at the centre of the complaint.

My Chemical Romance had two further Hollywood Bowl performances scheduled for October 30 and 31, meaning the decision could affect the final dates of its residency.

For the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders , the development is a welcome outcome in a dispute over how their famous image is used.

While the legal proceedings may have further implications, the reported commitment means the contested costumes are not expected to return for the remaining performances.

The episode demonstrates that even a celebrated musical act can face limits when its stage production uses imagery closely associated with another organisation. For the cheerleaders, protecting their identity has delivered another victory, this time outside the football field.

articles.title: Jerry Jones is going to do it: He'll bring back a Cowboys legend to help them become Super Bowl champions again
articles.standfirst: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has opened the door to a reunion with Troy Aikman
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has opened the door to a reunion with Troy Aikman
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys could be preparing for a reunion with one of the most important figures in their history.

Jerry Jones has made it clear that he would welcome the opportunity to bring Troy Aikman back into the organisation, potentially giving the franchise legend a role in shaping the team's future.

Aikman's broadcasting career is approaching a crossroads, with his ESPN contract set to expire after the 2026 NFL season.

The former quarterback has not received an extension like his longtime Monday Night Football colleague Joe Buck , who signed a reported six-year, $108 million deal in September.

Speaking on Dallas radio station 105.3 The Fan on Tuesday, October 27, Jones was asked whether he would consider employing Aikman in a front-office position.

“Yes, I could and would,” Jones said regarding if he’s open to Aikman taking up a role within the organization. “It’s that simple because I do think that much of him with his basic command and knowledge of NFL football. He’s certainly qualified to do anything mentioned. He’s outstanding.

“The answer is not necessarily that we’re going to do anything more direct with the team at this time, but don’t rule it out. It is very possible.”

The comments followed a conversation between the pair before Dallas defeated the Philadelphia Eagles 38-21 on October 26.

While Jones has not confirmed a formal offer or a specific position, his remarks have raised the prospect of Aikman returning to the franchise where he built his legacy.

Why Troy Aikman could be the Cowboys' next big addition

Aikman is far more than a familiar face for Cowboys supporters. Selected first overall in the 1989 NFL Draft, he spent 12 seasons in Dallas and led the franchise to three Super Bowl championships during the 1990s.

He was named Super Bowl XXVII MVP and later inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

His experience could be valuable to an organisation that has struggled to return to the sport's biggest stage. Dallas has not won a Super Bowl since the 1995 season, despite remaining one of the NFL's most prominent franchises.

Aikman has also indicated that he would seriously consider returning if Jones believed he could help the team.

“We’ve been through the highest of highs, we’ve been through some pretty tough moments as well. Our relationship is complicated. I think he would agree with that, but it is one that’s built, I believe, on respect,” the Hall of Famer told Mike Fischer last week.

“This week, he said some really kind things, which meant a lot to me, quite honestly. So, yeah, I would welcome any conversation with Jerry, and quite honestly I don’t know if there would be, or if there ever would be an opportunity. But if Jerry came to me and felt that, in his heart, I could lend some services that would help make them better, I would, I’d have a hard time not taking a good look at that.”

A return would require more than nostalgia

Although the possibility of a reunion will excite Dallas fans, Aikman's responsibilities would be crucial. Jones already serves as the Cowboys ' owner and general manager, so a meaningful front-office appointment would need a clearly defined role and influence.

Aikman has gained valuable insight into the game through his broadcasting career and recently served as a consultant during the Miami Dolphins ' search for a head coach and general manager. That experience could provide a foundation for a position involving football operations, player evaluation or strategic advice.

His relationship with Jones has not always been straightforward, but both men have spoken positively about the respect that remains between them.

Aikman is expected to complete the current NFL season with ESPN before considering his next step. For now, there is no confirmed agreement with Dallas, and Jones has explicitly stopped short of announcing an immediate appointment.

Nevertheless, the possibility is real enough to keep Cowboys supporters watching closely. Bringing Aikman back would reconnect the franchise with a central figure from its championship era, although any return would need to deliver more than sentimental value.

If Jones and Aikman can agree on a role that genuinely strengthens the organisation, the reunion could become an important development in Dallas's pursuit of another Super Bowl title.

articles.title: Jerry Jones receives trade deadline advice: He can’t afford mistakes with these Cowboys
articles.standfirst: After crushing the Eagles, the Cowboys sparked a new debate: Is Dallas’ roster fine and is coaching the real issue?
articles.summary: After crushing the Eagles, the Cowboys sparked a new debate: Is Dallas’ roster fine and is coaching the real issue?
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys finally found some answers after an inconsistent start to the season. Their dominant road victory over the Philadelphia Eagles improved their record to 3-4 and, more importantly, marked the first time this year that both the offense and defense performed at a high level in the same game.

The win even convinced some analysts that Dallas does not need to make major moves before the trade deadline and that the biggest issue is not the talent on the roster.

“The players are fine. They need coaching upgrades… I will argue all day: It's not talent,” said FS1 sports media personality Colin Cowherd, according to Herd w/ Colin Cowherd on X .

Colin Cowherd believes Cowboys' biggest issue isn't the roster

Cowherd’s stance comes amid the ongoing debate over whether the Cowboys need to improve their roster, especially on defense, to become a legitimate contender this season. Dallas’ defensive unit got off to a concerning start , including a disappointing performance against the New York Giants , and has shown several consistency issues in the weeks since.

While the win over Philadelphia was a major boost, it is also worth noting that the Eagles entered the matchup without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts and several other key players, leading some to believe it was not a definitive test of Dallas’ true potential.

articles.title: Troy Aikman's return to the Cowboys hits a snag for Jerry Jones: "They had a lot of disagreements"
articles.standfirst: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has left the door open for Troy Aikman to return to the organization
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has left the door open for Troy Aikman to return to the organization
articles.body:
The prospect of Troy Aikman returning to the Dallas Cowboys has generated excitement among fans, particularly with uncertainty surrounding his future as an NFL broadcaster.

However, a potential reunion with owner Jerry Jones may be more complicated than their recent public comments suggest.

Jones has openly welcomed the possibility of bringing the Hall of Fame quarterback into the Cowboys ' organization, while Aikman has admitted that he would seriously consider an offer.

Yet Ed Werder , a veteran NFL reporter who has covered Dallas for decades, believes the pair's history makes a professional partnership difficult to imagine.

The central issue, according to Werder , is their past disagreements over how the franchise should be managed. Although Aikman and Jones remain respectful of one another, their differing views on football operations could become a significant obstacle if they were to work together again.

Aikman recently discussed their relationship with Cowboys insider Mike Fisher , explaining that he would be willing to meet Jones regardless of whether a job was on the table.

“I would have lunch, breakfast, or dinner with Jerry any time he wants it. And it wouldn’t necessarily have to be because it’s a job interview. Just because, you know, we go back a long way. . . . I came in, I was 22 years old. I was his very first draft pick. There’s a lot within that relationship, both from the beginning, when he began as the owner, when I began my NFL career as a quarterback for 12 years of my life, playing for him, and then, even in the years that have followed, you know, we’ve been through a lot,” he told Fisher .

Aikman acknowledged that their relationship has experienced both extraordinary success and difficult moments, but insisted that respect remains at its foundation.

“We’ve been through the highest of highs, we’ve been through some pretty tough moments as well. Our relationship is complicated. I think he would agree with that, but it is one that’s built, I believe, on respect. This week, he said some really kind things, which meant a lot to me, quite honestly,” he said.

“So, yeah, I would welcome any conversation with Jerry, and quite honestly I don’t know if there would be, or if there ever would be an opportunity. But if Jerry came to me and felt that, in his heart, I could lend some services that would help make them better, I would, I’d have a hard time not taking a good look at that.”

Ed Werder questions whether the Cowboys reunion could work

Jones has been equally complimentary about his former quarterback. Speaking on Dallas sports radio station 105.3 The Fan, the Cowboys owner praised Aikman's work ethic and football knowledge while acknowledging that the two men have experienced their share of disagreements.

“He’s one of the hardest working, most focused people that I’ve ever been around,” Jones said on 105.3 The Fan.

“When you’re around each other, a part of that makeup can make it where you have your ups and downs. I think the world of him. I’ve seen his image and had it in my eyes since I walked in the NFL. He’s outstanding. The answer is not necessarily that we’re going to do something more direct with the team at this time, but don’t rule it out. It is very possible.”

Despite those encouraging words, Werder believes the pair's professional history would make a return difficult.

During an appearance on The Dan Patrick Show, the reporter pointed to the uncertainty surrounding Aikman's broadcasting career and his relationship with ESPN partner Joe Buck before explaining why he doubts the former quarterback will join Dallas' front office.

“Well, Dan, you and I know that ESPN never lets valuable people leave the company, so it’s quite surprising to both of us, I think, that Troy Aikman is not returning on an extension and gonna be Joe Buck’s partner after this 25 years they’ve had together,” Werder told DP.

“Troy really values loyalty, and I don’t think he feels like that’s been in existence in this partnership this year, either with the company or with Joe Buck ,” Werder said.

“It certainly seems to me like they’ve already decided they’re moving on from Troy Aikman. And whether there’s a place for Troy in broadcasting, I don’t know. There should be. To me, there’s the best there is still. He’s the gold standard.”

Werder went further in his assessment of a potential return to Dallas, arguing that Aikman's experience playing under Jones as the Cowboys' general manager could make it difficult for them to work together.

“Troy played for Jerry as a GM. He didn’t think it went all that well. I don’t see him working in the Cowboys’ front office, regardless of what happens on TV,” Werder wrote in a post on X, as reported by Pro Football Network.

The concern is not simply whether the two men like or respect each other. A front-office position would require them to agree on personnel decisions, coaching appointments and the broader direction of the team.

Werder has questioned whether their philosophies are compatible enough to make that possible.

Aikman's Cowboys legacy remains difficult to match

Aikman was selected first overall by Dallas in the 1989 NFL Draft and spent 12 seasons with the franchise. He led the Cowboys to three Super Bowl championships, winning Super Bowls XXVII, XXVIII and XXX during their dominant run in the 1990s.

His experience and understanding of the organization would make him an attractive figure for a franchise that has struggled to recapture that championship success. Dallas has not won another Super Bowl since its victory in January 1996.

Aikman has also explored opportunities beyond broadcasting, including a consultancy role with the Miami Dolphins during their search for leadership. That experience could offer a pathway toward a more formal football operations position, should he decide to leave television.

However, Jones has traditionally maintained significant control over the Cowboys ' football decisions, serving as both owner and general manager. Hiring a high-profile former quarterback would not necessarily mean surrendering that authority, but it could create tension if their views on running the franchise diverged.

For now, neither man has announced an agreement or confirmed that formal negotiations are underway.

Jones has made his interest clear, and Aikman has expressed a willingness to listen. Whether that mutual openness can overcome decades of complicated history remains the biggest question surrounding a possible return.

Werder's skepticism is not confirmation that a deal is impossible, but it serves as a reminder that nostalgia alone may not be enough to bring one of the Cowboys' greatest players back into the organization.

articles.title: Is a George Pickens trade really possible? In Jerry’s World anything can happen
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys insist George Pickens remains a key piece, but with the trade deadline approaching, Jerry Jones’ unpredictable history keeps the door open to a shocking move.
articles.summary: The Cowboys insist George Pickens remains a key piece, but with the trade deadline approaching, Jerry Jones’ unpredictable history keeps the door open to a shocking move.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys enter NFL Week 8 with renewed confidence after one of their best performances of the season, defeating the Philadelphia Eagles 38-21 on Monday night. However, one situation continues to generate questions within the team: the future of George Pickens .

The star wide receiver returned to the center of the conversation after head coach Brian Schottenheimer questioned his impact beyond the passing game, and his role during the win over Philadelphia fueled speculation about a potential move before the NFL trade deadline .

With the deadline set for November 10 , a fan asked respected NFL insider Tom Pelissero on Substack about the possibility of Dallas making a surprise move and sending Pickens to another team, despite owner Jerry Jones downplaying the chances of a trade.

Pelissero said he is not ruling out any scenario, especially because the Cowboys continue to look for help at one of their biggest areas of need: the pass rusher position. However, he acknowledged that including Pickens in a potential deal would be a complicated decision.

“Making as many trades as the Cowboys have since the Micah Parsons blockbuster naturally depletes draft capital—but if there’s a will, there’s a way. Edge rusher is the biggest need on Dallas’s defense, so I wouldn’t rule anything out. They were, after all, the runner-up in the Maxx Crosby sweepstakes last March,” Pelissero wrote.

Will the Cowboys actually trade George Pickens?

Although Pickens had a strong performance against the Eagles with four receptions for 57 yards and a touchdown , it drew attention that he played 12 fewer snaps than Ryan Flournoy .

The situation came after Schottenheimer said on October 22 that the receiver needed to understand that he also has an important impact on the Cowboys’ running game.

Despite the speculation, Pelissero believes it is unlikely that Dallas will move on from one of its top offensive weapons before the deadline.

“As for Pickens, he’s still an important piece of the Dallas offense, and the Cowboys won’t be out of the NFC East race in 12 days. Also, he’s making over $1.5 million on the franchise tag, so a team would need a big chunk of cash and cap space to make it work.”

For now, all indications point toward Pickens remaining in Dallas , although his role within the offense will be one of the biggest storylines to monitor as the trade deadline approaches.

articles.title: CeeDee Lamb’s shocking Cardinals curse is fueling his Week 8 revenge
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys star is using that painful streak as extra motivation ahead of their Week 8 showdown.
articles.summary: The Cowboys star is using that painful streak as extra motivation ahead of their Week 8 showdown.
articles.body:
Rumors surrounding George Pickens and the Dallas Cowboys continue to grow, but the team’s focus is now locked on its next challenge: a matchup against the Arizona Cardinals that carries some recent uncomfortable history for Dallas.

Heading into the NFL’s Week 8 game , CeeDee Lamb acknowledged there is special motivation in facing Arizona, a team that has become a genuine nightmare for the Cowboys in recent years.

The star receiver is still looking for his first career win against the Cardinals after a losing streak that has followed him since he entered the league.

CeeDee Lamb wants to end Arizona’s dominance

Lamb was asked whether the Cowboys are approaching this week with a different level of focus after last season’s loss to Arizona.

“I’ve never beat the Cardinals since I’ve been in the league, so that’s kind of fair to say,” Lamb said. “I wouldn’t say heightened focus, but it’s definitely another take.”

The reality is that Arizona has owned this recent rivalry. The Cardinals have won four straight meetings against Dallas (2020, 2022, 2023, and 2025) , including three victories at AT&T Stadium .

For Lamb, one of the keys to Arizona’s success against the Cowboys has been the intensity they bring to these games.

“They’ve always had more energy,” Lamb said. “Just coming out in the game, they’re more excited regardless of if it was at 12 o’clock, Sunday night, Monday night. We played them in primetime. They beat us there. So just coming in, treating them as if they are a Super Bowl-contending team, which they may be, you know what I’m saying? So hats off to them in their prep. And we just got to go match them, if not overpower them.”

Cowboys arrive with confidence after beating the Eagles

Although Lamb’s comment about Arizona as a potential contender raised eyebrows among some fans, Dallas heads into the game with momentum from one of its strongest offensive performances of the season.

The Cowboys defeated the Philadelphia Eagles 38-21 on Monday night , restoring confidence after weeks of criticism.

For Lamb, that win confirmed the team had rediscovered its identity.

“No, that’s exactly who we are. We’re better balanced,” he said. “We could beat you in a run game. We could beat you in the pass [game].”

CeeDee Lamb believes he can beat any coverage

Beyond the team’s overall performance, Lamb also made clear that he has complete confidence in his individual talent and ability to create problems for any defense.

“I think my ability to line up anywhere in the offense and run any route on the route tree,” Lamb said. “I feel like I could (beat) anybody in front of me, and I’m standing on that.”

Now the Cowboys will look to build on the momentum from their win over Philadelphia while ending a streak that has turned the Cardinals into one of their toughest recent opponents.

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys linked yet again to defensive star in order to save 2026 season
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys’ defense hasn’t seen any major improvements and continues to be the team’s Achilles heel.
articles.summary: The Cowboys’ defense hasn’t seen any major improvements and continues to be the team’s Achilles heel.
articles.body:
Coming off of a 38-21 road victory, Jerry Jones and the Dallas Cowboys can once again start dreaming big. Even though they’re still sporting a losing record at 3-4 , the NFC East appears wide open, and the offense is back on track.

The team’s defense remains its Achilles heel . Given Jones’ penchant for pulling off big trades, rumors have begun swirling once again, and it’s a familiar name that’s on the Cowboys’ radar: Las Vegas Raiders pass rusher Maxx Crosby .

Longtime Cowboys radio reporter says Cowboys are going to get Maxx Crosby

Crosby has been linked to the Cowboys for quite some time now. Longtime Cowboys reporter and former front office executive Bryan Broaddus has made a bold prediction that Crosby will be a Cowboys player before the trade deadline .

Sometimes you have to think about, you have no pass rush, and it's a shame that it hasn't materialized like we all thought it might. I'm gonna make a bold prediction: I think they're gonna get Maxx Crosby. I think they're gonna go get Maxx Crosby.

The Raiders haven’t exactly been benefiting from his services this season, as their defense is struggling mightily. Crosby has also, literally, been traded recently. The Raiders sent him to the Baltimore Ravens this past offseason, only to see the AFC North team pull out of it after Crosby’s medical tests came back unfavorably.

Dallas could really use an elite defensive player like Crosby. They’ve been clamoring for pass-rushing help ever since the team traded away Micah Parsons . Jones isn't afraid of giving up draft capital if he believes there's hope of a playoff run for his team. A loss in Week 8 could change everything, though.

articles.title: Troy Aikman regrets putting Jerry Jones in a difficult position after admitting he would return to the Cowboys
articles.standfirst: Pressure continues to grow in Dallas after an underwhelming start to the 2026 NFL season
articles.summary: Pressure continues to grow in Dallas after an underwhelming start to the 2026 NFL season
articles.body:
T roy Aikman 's uncertain broadcasting future has created fresh speculation about a possible return to the Dallas Cowboys , but the Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback now says he regrets putting owner Jerry Jones in an uncomfortable position. A possible return to Dallas would come amid growing scrutiny of head coach Brian Schottenheimer as the Cowboys ' disappointing start to the 2026 NFL season prompted questions about his offensive play-calling, leadership.

Schottenheimer 's record and offensive production had fuelled the debate as Dallas started the campaign 2-4, while defeats against the Carolina Panthers and the Green Bay Packers saw the offence score only 29 points combined. The situation prompted calls for Aikman to return to the franchise that gave him his football career and he recently acknowledged that he would consider returning to Dallas in a front-office capacity. However by discussing the possibility publicly and prompting questions to be given directly to Jones about the subject, the ESPN analyst felt he had placed the Cowboys owner in a difficult situation. "The last thing I want is – I was answering a question," Aikman said to Dallas’ The Ticket show. "And I think it's really unfair to Jerry that he then has to answer these questions. “As far as, 'Hey, would you bring Troy back, or would you have a role for him?' I mean, there's no real good answer that he could give." The pair subsequently discussed the subject before the Cowboys ' matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles – which Dallas managed to win to move into second place in the division. And Aikman said he wanted to make clear that he had not expected Jones to respond to the growing speculation as he admitted he didn’t want the owner to be pressured into answering the question. "We briefly touched on it just,” Aikman continued. “Because I felt that maybe I backed him into a corner that he didn't deserve to be backed into. He didn't ask for it. And so, we're clear on that. “He totally understood, and yet, he was very complimentary if something like that were to ever take place with the idea that we're not having those conversations at this time."

Why has Jerry Jones left the door open for an Aikman reunion?

Jones has nevertheless made it clear that a return for the three-time Super Bowl champion remains a possibility as Aikman’s situation with ESPN continues to factor into the speculation. A reported disagreement between Aikman and Joe Buck has added uncertainty and potentially drove a wedge between the former quarterback and the broadcasting network. And during his weekly appearance on 105.3 The Fan, the Cowboys owner was asked about bringing him back as the comments followed Aikman 's admission that he would be interested in exploring a role if he believed he could make a meaningful contribution. "The answer is not necessarily that we're going to do anything more direct with the team at this time, but don't rule it out. It is very possible,” Jones said as he continues to explore how to guide the team to the Super Bowl . Aikman has also questioned Schottenheimer 's emphasis on relationships and culture, arguing that an NFL head coach is ultimately judged by results as he made the point that positive relationships mean little if they do not translate into victories. The victory over the Eagles has helped calm troubled waters for the moment with 3-4 Dallas now one win behind in the NFC East to the 4-2-1 New York Giants , but Aikman still urged caution about treating one victory as proof that Cowboys have resolved its problems.

However by discussing the possibility publicly and prompting questions to be given directly to Jones about the subject, the ESPN analyst felt he had placed the Cowboys owner in a difficult situation. "The last thing I want is – I was answering a question," Aikman said to Dallas’ The Ticket show. "And I think it's really unfair to Jerry that he then has to answer these questions. “As far as, 'Hey, would you bring Troy back, or would you have a role for him?' I mean, there's no real good answer that he could give." The pair subsequently discussed the subject before the Cowboys ' matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles – which Dallas managed to win to move into second place in the division. And Aikman said he wanted to make clear that he had not expected Jones to respond to the growing speculation as he admitted he didn’t want the owner to be pressured into answering the question. "We briefly touched on it just,” Aikman continued. “Because I felt that maybe I backed him into a corner that he didn't deserve to be backed into. He didn't ask for it. And so, we're clear on that. “He totally understood, and yet, he was very complimentary if something like that were to ever take place with the idea that we're not having those conversations at this time."
Why has Jerry Jones left the door open for an Aikman reunion?

Jones has nevertheless made it clear that a return for the three-time Super Bowl champion remains a possibility as Aikman’s situation with ESPN continues to factor into the speculation. A reported disagreement between Aikman and Joe Buck has added uncertainty and potentially drove a wedge between the former quarterback and the broadcasting network. And during his weekly appearance on 105.3 The Fan, the Cowboys owner was asked about bringing him back as the comments followed Aikman 's admission that he would be interested in exploring a role if he believed he could make a meaningful contribution. "The answer is not necessarily that we're going to do anything more direct with the team at this time, but don't rule it out. It is very possible,” Jones said as he continues to explore how to guide the team to the Super Bowl . Aikman has also questioned Schottenheimer 's emphasis on relationships and culture, arguing that an NFL head coach is ultimately judged by results as he made the point that positive relationships mean little if they do not translate into victories. The victory over the Eagles has helped calm troubled waters for the moment with 3-4 Dallas now one win behind in the NFC East to the 4-2-1 New York Giants , but Aikman still urged caution about treating one victory as proof that Cowboys have resolved its problems.

articles.title: Dak Prescott's desperate complaint about Erin Andrews' outfit at a Cowboys game: “What are we doing?”
articles.standfirst: The FOX Sports reporter revealed why her Christmas-inspired outfit caught the quarterback's attention
articles.summary: The FOX Sports reporter revealed why her Christmas-inspired outfit caught the quarterback's attention
articles.body:
Erin Andrews has spent years reporting from NFL sidelines, but her wardrobe choices have attracted almost as much attention as the action on the field.

The FOX Sports reporter recently revealed that Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott once questioned her decision to wear a Christmas-green suit during a game, prompting an amusing exchange between the two.

Speaking on her Calm Down with Erin and Charissa podcast, Andrews recalled that players haven't always been shy about commenting on her clothing.

She explained that she generally avoids wearing team colors because she doesn't want her appearance to suggest she's supporting one side over the other.

However, that approach didn't prevent an awkward encounter with Prescott during a Christmas Eve matchup. Andrews remembered wearing a green suit, explaining that her choice had everything to do with the holiday rather than football loyalties.

“Oh, and I’ve had players call me out, like literally call me out,” she said. “They’ll be like, ‘Oh, really? Wow. What, what are you doing?’ I was working a Dallas Cowboys Christmas Eve game years ago, and I had a fabulous, like, Christmas green suit, and the Cowboys won.

“And Dak was like, ‘What are we doing?’ And I was like, ‘I swear to God, this is all about Christmas.’ Like, he goes, ‘You couldn’t wear red?’ And I was like, ‘I wore red for Thanksgiving.’ Like, come on.”

Andrews refuses to let fashion criticism dictate her sideline style

The green suit isn't the only outfit that's sparked conversation. Andrews previously made headlines after wearing a dramatic black-and-white fur coat during a 49ers-Eagles wild-card playoff game in Philadelphia.

Some viewers compared the look to Disney villain Cruella de Vil, but the reporter was delighted with the outfit and defended her decision.

“In the wind, I know it looked like a Beyoncé video. It felt fun, it felt fabulous, it felt like a big event, it felt like a big wild-card playoff game on Fox. It was the perfect time to wear this piece, and I’m so excited we did it,” she said.

Andrews has also been open about the pressures of live reporting. Following the October 25 Packers-Lions game at Detroit's Ford Field, she criticized her own halftime performance during her podcast.

A lengthy conversation with Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur , combined with a last-minute scramble for injury updates, left her short on preparation time and breathless when she went on air.

“I’m fully f***ing out of breath, which is inappropriate,” Andrews said.

“Like, get it together, sister. In through the nose, out through the mouth. It was all because the ramp was so long.”

She described the experience as a learning opportunity and recalled Tom Brady offering a sympathetic “Aww” after she promised to get herself together.

These moments highlight the unpredictable nature of sideline reporting for Andrews . Whether dealing with Prescott's fashion commentary or racing to deliver accurate updates, the job requires here to be on point at all times.

articles.title: Former NFL player demands that if Jerry Jones signs Troy Aikman, he should also sign another Cowboys legend: “That’s not right”
articles.standfirst: Former NFL star calls out Jerry Jones over potential Cowboys reunion plan
articles.summary: Former NFL star calls out Jerry Jones over potential Cowboys reunion plan
articles.body:
Former NFL cornerback Asante Samuel has jokingly challenged Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones over his reported interest in bringing Troy Aikman back to the organization.

Samuel believes that if the franchise wants to reunite with its legendary quarterback, another member of its championship-winning past deserves an invitation: Michael Irvin.

The discussion comes as Aikman's future in television remains uncertain. The Hall of Fame quarterback, who currently works as an analyst for ESPN's Monday Night Football, recently suggested there's a 50-50 chance he won't return to broadcasting next year.

Aikman's contract with ESPN expires after the Super Bowl in February 2027, and reports have raised questions about whether the network intends to offer him an extension. His broadcasting partner, Joe Buck , secured a new five-year agreement in September, adding another layer to the uncertainty surrounding Aikman's position.

With his television future unresolved, the former Cowboys quarterback could potentially explore opportunities elsewhere, including a return to the franchise where he established his legacy.

Jones has already expressed interest in that possibility, leaving the door open for Aikman to take on a significant position within the organization. During a recent radio appearance, the Cowboys owner described a potential reunion as "very possible."

Samuel quickly weighed in on the possibility, suggesting that Jones shouldn't bring Aikman back without also finding a place for Irvin .

"How can Jerry Jones hire Troy Aikman and not bring Michael Irvin along. That’s not right," Samuel wrote on X.

Asante Samuel believes Michael Irvin deserves a place in potential Cowboys reunion

Samuel's suggestion carries a connection to Dallas' successful past. Aikman and Irvin were central figures during the Cowboys' dominant run in the 1990s, establishing themselves as one of the NFL's most productive quarterback-receiver combinations.

Together, they helped Dallas capture three Super Bowl championships, building a legacy that remains closely associated with the franchise's greatest era.

Their on-field chemistry was particularly impressive, with Aikman completing 641 passes to Irvin across 128 games together. Those connections produced 9,949 receiving yards and 54 touchdowns.

Irvin was a major offensive weapon throughout that period, while Aikman provided the leadership and consistency that helped the Cowboys compete for championships. Their contributions made them two of the most recognizable figures in franchise history.

Bringing the pair back into the organization could also create an opportunity for Dallas to benefit from their experience and understanding of what it takes to build a championship-caliber team. Both players know the expectations that come with representing one of the NFL's most recognizable franchises.

Aikman has previously expressed interest in working in an NFL front office, and his consulting experience with the Miami Dolphins could provide a foundation for a move into an executive position.

However, there's no confirmation that Dallas has made a formal offer or that discussions have progressed beyond the possibility raised by Jones .

Whether Aikman eventually leaves broadcasting remains another important question. With ESPN yet to secure his future beyond the current season, the 59-year-old could soon face a significant career decision.

articles.title: Arizona Cardinals vs Dallas Cowboys: Where to watch today's game and what time they play at AT&T Stadium
articles.standfirst: Cowboys and Cardinals look to take off in Arlington: two offenses hungry to win in Week 8
articles.summary: Cowboys and Cardinals look to take off in Arlington: two offenses hungry to win in Week 8
articles.body:
The AT&T Stadium in Arlington opens its doors this Sunday, November 1, 2026 for a showdown between two teams arriving at NFL Week 8 with the same urgency: to climb out of the middle-of-the-pack muddle and string together wins.

The Dallas Cowboys host the Arizona Cardinals in an interconference clash where momentum rules, and both locker rooms arrive with opposite feelings after last week's game.

The Week 8 outlook for Dallas and Arizona

The Cowboys are coming off a statement performance: a 38-21 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on the road in Week 7, their most lopsided win of the year.

That result places them second in the NFC East, behind the New York Giants, and gives them some breathing room in an uneven season. Dallas has scored 189 points, the most productive offense in its division.

Across from them, the Cardinals are going through a difficult stretch. Arizona fell 16-30 at home to the Denver Broncos last week and sits in last place in the NFC West. The most worrying number in the desert is on defense: 208 points allowed, the worst figure in the entire conference. That bleeding on defense will undoubtedly be the main storyline of the game.

Contrasting forms: one resurging and the other declining

The recent momentum clearly favors the home team. Dallas has won three of its last five matchups, including the already mentioned blow to the Eagles and a 34-30 road victory over the Houston Texans.

Their problem has been consistency: they also suffered setbacks such as the 31-34 loss at home to the Baltimore Ravens, a game that sums up the Cowboys' offensive-but-fragile season.

Arizona, meanwhile, has lost five of seven. Their only recent relief was a tight 18-16 win over the Los Angeles Rams on the road in Week 6, but before and after that the defense gave up true avalanches: 45 points against the Detroit Lions and 31 versus the Seattle Seahawks.

To have a chance in Arlington, the Cardinals will need to deliver a much more solid version of themselves than they’ve shown for most of the season.

The key matchup: Dallas' offense against Arizona's defense

If there is a clash of styles that could decide the game, it is the Cowboys' firepower against the fragile visiting defense.

Dallas relies on quarterback Dak Prescott, with a top-tier receiving corps led by CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens , along with tight end Jake Ferguson as a safety valve on short plays. In the running game, Javonte Williams gives the offense the balance it needs to control the tempo.

The Cardinals, who have split carries in the backfield with veterans like James Conner and Tyler Allgeier, rely on tight end Trey McBride and receiver Michael Wilson on offense.

The question mark is under center, with Jacoby Brissett leading an offense that has totaled just 142 points in seven games —the least productive of the two rivals this Sunday—. Arizona will need that attack to sustain possession to protect a defense that cannot afford to be exposed to three-and-outs.

Implications in the overall NFL standings

Although neither of the two is fighting for the top, the game matters. A win would leave Dallas at 4-4 and within striking distance of the Giants in the NFC East, keeping their playoff hopes alive.

For Arizona, a loss would mean falling to 2-6 and virtually saying goodbye to the postseason conversation in an NFC West where the 49ers are firmly in control.

In terms of the overall standings, the Cowboys are ranked 20th in the league and the Cardinals 27th; both need to win to avoid falling behind.

The bottom of the NFC is very crowded: the Cardinals, Tampa Bay Buccaneers, New Orleans Saints, Philadelphia Eagles, Washington Commanders, and Miami Dolphins are fighting not to be buried. For Arizona, every loss carries double the weight when its point differential (-66) is already the most negative in the conference.

Where to watch the Cowboys vs Cardinals game live and what time does it start?

The Week 8 matchup between Dallas and Arizona will be played at AT&T Stadium, home of the Cowboys . Kickoff is scheduled for this Sunday, November 1, at 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time (12:00 p.m. Central Time and 10:00 a.m. Pacific Time).

The game between the Dallas Cowboys and Arizona Cardinals will be broadcast nationwide on Fox and, via streaming, you can watch it on: Fubo, FOX One, Fox Sports, NFL+, DIRECTV, Hulu + Live TV, or Sling TV

Cowboys vs Cardinals Prediction

Dallas comes in with its offense firing and at home , while Arizona carries the worst defense in the conference and a worrying run of results. Everything points to a high-scoring game in which the Cowboys, backed by their passing attack and the heat of Arlington, should come out on top.

Prediction: Cowboys win by a couple of possessions, although McBride and Arizona's offense have enough to keep the score from getting completely out of hand.
