articles.title: The Cowboys legend who made Jerry Jones very happy is enjoying another success away from Dallas
articles.standfirst: Emmitt Smith was inducted to the Florida Gators Hall of Fame on Saturday
articles.summary: Emmitt Smith was inducted to the Florida Gators Hall of Fame on Saturday
articles.body:
Emmitt Smith 's football legacy has earned him a place among the greatest players in NFL history, but another honor has brought his college career back into focus as the former Dallas Cowboys running back was inducted into the Florida Gators Hall of Fame . Smith made an immediate impression after joining Florida in 1987 and as a freshman, he rushed for 1341 yards for the Gators , finishing ninth in the Heisman Trophy voting and establishing himself as one of the country's leading young players before he followed that with 988 yards and nine touchdowns in only nine games during his sophomore season.

His final campaign in 1989 was even more impressive, producing 1599 rushing yards and 14 touchdowns, alongside another Top 10 Heisman finish and across three seasons, Smith accumulated 3928 rushing yards and 36 touchdowns, setting 58 school records. He earned three consecutive First-Team All-SEC selections , was named SEC Player of the Year in 1989 and received unanimous All-American recognition as the Dallas Cowboys selected him 17th overall in the 1990 NFL Draft and Smith went on to become the central figure in their championship teams of the early 1990s. Winning three Super Bowls in four seasons between 1992 and 1995, his individual peak came in 1993, when he claimed the NFL MVP award after recording 1486 rushing yards and nine touchdowns. A year later, he was named MVP of Super Bowl XXVIII , rushing for 132 yards and two touchdowns in Dallas ' victory over the Buffalo Bills .

Smith’s daughters celebrate his Gators Hall of Fame glory

Smith 's best statistical season arrived in 1995, when he produced 1773 rushing yards and a league-leading 25 touchdowns before he continued his career with the Arizona Cardinals after leaving Dallas in 2002, eventually retiring from professional football in 2004. His final numbers remain extraordinary: 18,355 rushing yards and 164 rushing touchdowns across 226 appearances whilst he also recorded 515 receptions for 3224 yards, earning eight Pro Bowls and secured four First-Team All-Pro honors and it was his collegiate foundation that paved the pathway for him to become an elite rusher. Smith entered the College Football Hall of Fame in 2006 and the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2010 and his latest induction adds another distinction to a career defined by college dominance, three NFL championships and a rushing record that continues to stand. The ceremony, held on October 30 at the Chick-fil-A College Football Hall of Fame , recognized four former players as Smith represented Florida alongside former offensive lineman Maurkice Pouncey , whilst Georgia 's inductees were Andre Hastings and Brandon Boykin . The occasion also brought a family celebration as Smith 's daughters Rheagan and Skylar shared messages congratulating their father, with Rheagan posting a photograph of him holding his golden bust from the ceremony. “Congrats Padre! Go Gators,” Rheagan wrote on Instagram whilst her sister Skylar also celebrated the achievement, by adding: “Georgia Florida Hall of Fame 2026 inductees, congrats Pops.”

articles.title: Jerry Jones gets another “No”: Raiders star deals the Cowboys another major blow
articles.standfirst: Maxx Crosby has reportedly made his position known ahead of the November 10 deadline
articles.summary: Maxx Crosby has reportedly made his position known ahead of the November 10 deadline
articles.body:
Jerry Jones ' hopes of bringing another established defensive star to the Dallas Cowboys have suffered a setback, with Maxx Crosby reportedly making it clear that he has no intention of leaving the Las Vegas Raiders .

Crosby has been among the most frequently discussed potential trade targets ahead of the November 10 deadline, with his reputation as one of the NFL's premier pass rushers making him an attractive option for teams seeking defensive reinforcements.

However, ESPN's Adam Schefter reports that the Raiders haven't entertained trade discussions involving the five-time Pro Bowler this season, while the player himself remains firmly committed to the franchise.

"Maxx absolutely does not want to leave Las Vegas under any circumstances," a league source told ESPN. "His hope, though not in his full control, is that he remains a Raider for life."

The revelation significantly reduces the likelihood of a move to Dallas, although there has been no confirmation that the Cowboys have submitted an official offer or directly approached Las Vegas about a potential deal.

Crosby 's position represents a notable turnaround from the uncertainty surrounding his future during the previous season, when questions about his long-term commitment to Las Vegas intensified.

Those concerns appeared to reach a conclusion during the offseason when the Raiders agreed to trade Crosby to the Baltimore Ravens in exchange for two first-round draft picks.

However, the agreement collapsed after Crosby failed his medical examination in Baltimore, leaving him with the organization he had appeared close to departing.

The Raiders now appear determined to retain their defensive leader, despite enduring a difficult stretch of results after opening the 2026 campaign with three consecutive victories.

Las Vegas entered Sunday's meeting with the New York Jets holding a 3-4 record, having suffered four straight defeats following its promising start.

Although another franchise could still make an ambitious offer before the deadline, ESPN reports that neither Crosby nor the Raiders currently has an appetite for reopening negotiations.

What does Crosby's decision mean for Jerry Jones and Dallas?

The situation leaves the Cowboys facing a more complicated path if they intend to make a significant defensive addition before the trade window closes.

Crosby 's ability to disrupt opposing quarterbacks would make him a valuable addition to almost any NFL defense, but his preference to remain in Las Vegas creates an obstacle beyond the potential financial and draft-pick costs of a deal.

The Raiders are also focused on maintaining stability elsewhere, with veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins expected to retain his starting position despite the team's recent struggles.

Cousins has thrown 16 touchdown passes through seven games, while first overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza remains an option for later in the campaign.

Las Vegas faces a demanding schedule against the San Francisco 49ers, Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos and Cleveland Browns before its Week 13 bye.

The Cowboys must now consider whether alternative defensive targets offer a more realistic opportunity, particularly with the deadline approaching.

While nothing is guaranteed in the NFL trade market, Crosby 's reported stance suggests Jones will need an extraordinary change of circumstances to bring the Raiders star to Dallas.

The revelation significantly reduces the likelihood of a move to Dallas, although there has been no confirmation that the Cowboys have submitted an official offer or directly approached Las Vegas about a potential deal.
Crosby 's position represents a notable turnaround from the uncertainty surrounding his future during the previous season, when questions about his long-term commitment to Las Vegas intensified.
Those concerns appeared to reach a conclusion during the offseason when the Raiders agreed to trade Crosby to the Baltimore Ravens in exchange for two first-round draft picks.
However, the agreement collapsed after Crosby failed his medical examination in Baltimore, leaving him with the organization he had appeared close to departing.
The Raiders now appear determined to retain their defensive leader, despite enduring a difficult stretch of results after opening the 2026 campaign with three consecutive victories.
Las Vegas entered Sunday's meeting with the New York Jets holding a 3-4 record, having suffered four straight defeats following its promising start.
Although another franchise could still make an ambitious offer before the deadline, ESPN reports that neither Crosby nor the Raiders currently has an appetite for reopening negotiations.
What does Crosby's decision mean for Jerry Jones and Dallas?
The situation leaves the Cowboys facing a more complicated path if they intend to make a significant defensive addition before the trade window closes.

Crosby 's ability to disrupt opposing quarterbacks would make him a valuable addition to almost any NFL defense, but his preference to remain in Las Vegas creates an obstacle beyond the potential financial and draft-pick costs of a deal.
The Raiders are also focused on maintaining stability elsewhere, with veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins expected to retain his starting position despite the team's recent struggles.
Cousins has thrown 16 touchdown passes through seven games, while first overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza remains an option for later in the campaign.
Las Vegas faces a demanding schedule against the San Francisco 49ers, Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos and Cleveland Browns before its Week 13 bye.
The Cowboys must now consider whether alternative defensive targets offer a more realistic opportunity, particularly with the deadline approaching.
While nothing is guaranteed in the NFL trade market, Crosby 's reported stance suggests Jones will need an extraordinary change of circumstances to bring the Raiders star to Dallas.

articles.title: Jerry Jones, owner of the Dallas Cowboys, on Brian Schottenheimer's future: "That's not in my mind at this time"
articles.standfirst: Despite another disappointing loss, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones insists Brian Schottenheimer's job is not in jeopardy.
articles.summary: Despite another disappointing loss, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones insists Brian Schottenheimer's job is not in jeopardy.
articles.body:
History is repeating itself once again with the Dallas Cowboys , producing results that only bruise the ego of Jerry Jones , who is still trying to return his franchise to the golden years that are now long in the past.

The latest loss to the Arizona Cardinals hit hard, serving as a reminder that it has not been the only setback to strike the team this season.

If blame is to be assigned, Brian Schottenheimer’s name naturally comes up. As the head coach leading the team, he is ultimately the one making many of the decisions in Dallas.

Against this backdrop, Jerry Jones spoke after the loss to the Arizona Cardinals about the immediate future of his head coach, and his response apparently surprised more than a few people.

Jerry Jones addresses Brian Schottenheimer’s future

Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones discussed Brian Schottenheimer’s future as head coach following the painful 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday.

Despite the latest setback, Jones said he is not considering making a change at the coaching position, at least for now.

“I will say that a lot of people let Brian (Schottenheimer) down today.”

We’re not going to get into anything. That’s not in my mind at this time.

The defeat left Dallas with a 3-5 record on the season and once again raised doubts about the team, which has lost three of its last four games and is going through a difficult stretch in the campaign.

articles.title: Dak Prescott’s heartbreak returns after another crushing Cowboys collapse
articles.standfirst: Dak Prescott watched another Cowboys collapse unfold, but the quarterback refuses to point fingers after Dallas wasted a late lead against the Cardinals.
articles.summary: Dak Prescott watched another Cowboys collapse unfold, but the quarterback refuses to point fingers after Dallas wasted a late lead against the Cardinals.
articles.body:
There was a moment that Dallas Cowboys fans surely remember: a 3-5 start to the season that ended with a spectacular turnaround and a playoff berth. That was one of the most exciting campaigns of Dak Prescott ’s career, as Dallas closed the 2018 season with an impressive 7-1 run after acquiring star receiver Amari Cooper and punching a ticket to the postseason.

In that final stretch, the Cowboys defeated the Seattle Seahawks in the Wild Card round before falling to the Los Angeles Rams in the Divisional Round. So with Dallas once again sitting at 3-5 , some might think a similar comeback is still possible.

But that comparison does not appear to convince Prescott, especially after the way the Cowboys let a 24-10 fourth-quarter lead slip away against an Arizona Cardinals team that entered the game at 2-5. Dallas ultimately fell 33-30 in overtime in its own stadium.

Prescott had used the 2018 season as a reference point during the team’s difficult start. However, after such a painful loss in a game they seemed to have under control, the quarterback does not want to rely on stories from the past.

Dak Prescott: “Talk is cheap”

After the game, Prescott dismissed the idea that the Cowboys can simply repeat the 2018 formula and stage an automatic turnaround. The defeat came after a stunning Arizona rally led by backup quarterback Gardner Minshew , who threw three second-half touchdowns, and running back Tyler Allgeier , who piled up 147 yards on just 11 carries .

“At this point, talk is cheap, telling stories is cheap. We have to go write our own story,” Prescott said.

Despite the difficult outlook, the quarterback made clear that he still believes in the team’s chances. For him, it is not the same to fall to contenders like the Green Bay Packers or Baltimore Ravens as it is to lose to a Cardinals team that stole a nearly locked-up victory.

“We still got time,” Prescott said.

Cowboys stand behind Brian Schottenheimer

Despite the results crisis, the Cowboys still have playoff options thanks to an NFC East that remains wide open. However, the idea that a coaching change could give the team a new spark has grown among fans.

Owner Jerry Jones made clear that, for now, he is not considering that possibility.

And Prescott does not believe the solution is to single out Brian Schottenheimer alone.

When asked about the criticism directed at the head coach, the quarterback defended the coaching staff and the entire group:

“It’s all of us. Don’t put the blame on one person. I think that’s weak, I think that’s cowardly. This game is about all 11 of us that touch the field and every person that has a part in it, coaches and support staff. It’s never just one person’s fault.

“Don’t take the easy and cheap way out. This is about us and backing him up and one another up.”

articles.title: Jerry Jones can't take it anymore: Cowboys owner caught on camera cursing after loss
articles.standfirst: Jerry Jones couldn’t hide his frustration after watching the Cowboys suffer another devastating collapse, and his angry reaction inside the owner’s box quickly went viral.
articles.summary: Jerry Jones couldn’t hide his frustration after watching the Cowboys suffer another devastating collapse, and his angry reaction inside the owner’s box quickly went viral.
articles.body:
J erry Jones will not sleep easily Sunday night. The owner, president, and general manager of the Dallas Cowboys exploded in frustration after watching his team suffer yet another collapse at AT&T Stadium . The painful home loss to the Arizona Cardinals revived a familiar nightmare that struck the franchise a year ago: a setback that places their playoff hopes in serious jeopardy.

Halloween may be over, but the Cowboys found a new way to terrify an increasingly desperate fan base. Dallas blew a 14-point fourth-quarter lead and fell 33-30 in overtime , drawing the full fury of Jones. From his suite, the 84-year-old owner slammed the table and reportedly unleashed an expletive, according to Ari Meirov of The 33rd Team.

Although the score remained close for much of the game, Dallas never truly took control. The offense averaged just 2.4 yards per carry and managed only 195 passing yards , while the defense kept the Cardinals in check for three quarters. Everything unraveled in the final period.

The Cowboys missed key tackles on running back Tyler Allgeier and allowed backup quarterback Gardner Minshew II to dismantle their secondary. They even received a second chance when Chad Ryland missed the extra point that would have sealed the game in regulation, but the kicker redeemed himself in overtime with a 42-yard field goal that secured Arizona’s victory.

Despite scoring 30 points, Dallas’ offense also failed to live up to its star power. CeeDee Lamb averaged just 8.3 yards per reception, while George Pickens managed only two catches —though those two grabs totaled 48 yards. While the defense once again found itself under the microscope, the collapse was a shared responsibility.

After the game, Jerry Jones avoided any discussion of potential firings during his traditional postgame press conference . Still, with the Cowboys now sitting at 3-5, an uncomfortable internal conversation is clearly on the horizon. The only reason Dallas remains alive in the playoff race is the continued inconsistency of the NFC East .

Even so, blowing a two-score lead at home against a Cardinals team that entered the game with one of the worst records in the NFL makes it hard to view any remaining matchup as a guaranteed win. In Week 9 , the Cowboys travel to face the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) in a game that could serve as a turning point—or deepen the crisis even further.

articles.title: Mike Tomlin's brutal attack on the Cowboys has Jerry Jones even more worried: “Cut your eyelids off”
articles.standfirst: Pressure grows on head coach Brian Schottenheimer after defeat to the Arizona Cardinals
articles.summary: Pressure grows on head coach Brian Schottenheimer after defeat to the Arizona Cardinals
articles.body:
M ike Tomlin tore into the Dallas Cowboys ' mentality after watching them surrender a 14-point fourth-quarter lead against the Arizona Cardinals , accusing the team of lacking the desire to seize control when the pressure was at its highest. His pointed criticism comes as Jerry Jones faces growing questions over the direction of the franchise as Tomlin , the former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach, described seeing too many players shy away from decisive moments.

Rather than embracing the responsibility of making a winning play, his words followed Dallas ' 33-30 overtime defeat, in which Gardner Minshew threw three touchdowns in the fourth quarter after replacing Jacoby Brissett . “I saw a bunch of blinkers, and what I mean by that, I say if you're a blinker, cut your eyelids off,” Tomlin said. “What I mean is, you gotta relish the thick moments. You gotta want to make the play. “As an individual and as a unit within a team. And watching the end of that game, I didn't see individuals or particular units that wanted to grab the bull by the horns and win the game.” The Cowboys had looked set for victory before Arizona overturned the deficit, leaving Dallas with a 3-5 record after eight games – offering an embarrassing loss against the minnows of the NFC as scrutiny of head coach Brian Schottenheimer grows.

Jerry Jones defends Brian Schottenheimer after Cowboys collapse

Jones , however, was not prepared to place the defeat entirely at Schottenheimer 's door. Speaking after the game, the owner argued that the players had also failed their coach, while acknowledging that the performance had fallen short of what supporters deserved. Jones also recognized how badly Dallas had wasted its opportunity, saying the team had to do better after getting into a position to win. His defense of Schottenheimer suggests the coach will have the chance to address the problems rather than immediately face dismissal. “I will say that a lot of people let Brian Schottenheimer down today,” Jones said. “So, for whatever criticism we might have for Brian, we're all gonna get in line. That was a total, to use a cliché, that was a total team effort out there.” The defensive statistics make that task particularly urgent. Dallas has conceded at least 20 points in every game this season and entered Sunday's contest allowing 373.7 yards per game. The Cowboys have also ranked last in the NFL in rushing yards allowed. Four of their five defeats have been decided by one possession, with the Baltimore Ravens and Arizona Cardinals both finding crucial scores late. The offense has its own shortcomings, too, despite the occasional standout connection between Prescott and CeeDee Lamb . Jones can make changes if he decides Schottenheimer is not the answer, but his public comments indicate that responsibility currently rests across the entire team.

articles.title: The Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders brought their Halloween horror night to AT&T Stadium when no one was expecting it
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys' early kickoff meant the cheerleaders had to sacrifice their Halloween celebrations
articles.summary: The Cowboys' early kickoff meant the cheerleaders had to sacrifice their Halloween celebrations
articles.body:
Halloween night is usually reserved for parties, costumes and celebrations, but the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders had a very different schedule this year.

While fans across the country were dressing up in the squad's blue-and-white uniforms, the real cheerleaders were preparing for an early morning at AT&T Stadium.

That’s because Dallas had a noon local kickoff against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. That start time left little room for a late Halloween celebration.

Several cheerleaders offered a glimpse of their evening through Instagram Stories. Rather than going out and celebrating, they were ironing and steaming their uniforms, making sure every detail was ready for the Week 8 matchup.

Most members of the squad were expected to wake up around 3 or 4 a.m. Hair, makeup, costumes and the rest of their pregame routine all require time and attention. With so much to organize before kickoff, staying out late wasn't an option.

The familiar Halloween costume might have been popular elsewhere, but for the women who wear it professionally, the night was all about getting ready for work.

A Halloween horror show for the Cowboys

The early alarm and abandoned celebrations didn't lead to a cheerful Sunday for Dallas, either. The Cowboys looked set to claim a win against Arizona after building a 24-10 advantage in the fourth quarter.

Dak Prescott's five-yard touchdown run helped extend the lead, and the home team appeared to have the game under control.

Instead, Arizona fought back and eventually secured a 33-30 overtime victory. The collapse was especially startling given Dallas' history of protecting big fourth-quarter leads at home.

Before Sunday, the franchise had never lost a home game after leading by at least 14 points in the final quarter, with its record standing at 202-0-1 in those situations.

The result also made Dallas the first NFL team this season to lose after holding a 14-point fourth-quarter lead. The Cowboys' record fell to 3-5, adding pressure to a season in which their playoff hopes were already complicated by the NFC East standings.

Despite the disappointing result, owner and general manager Jerry Jones made it clear that head coach Brian Schottenheimer wasn't facing an immediate job threat.

"That's not in my mind at this time," Jones said when asked about a possible coaching change.

Schottenheimer said he still believed in his staff and players, while acknowledging how disappointing the defeat was.

"I only know how to do it one way, and that's the work. I'm a worker, I'm a problem solver. I think we got guys in there in that locker room that are problem solvers," Schottenheimer said.

"We have guys in there that want to be great. We got guys that believe in what we're doing as a football team in all three phases, and they're hurting. They're hurting right now, too. And so as a leader, I'm going to stand in front and hit them with the truth."

Prescott also pushed back against the idea of blaming one person, saying responsibility belonged to everyone involved, from the players on the field to the coaches and support staff.

articles.title: ‘My dead mom can coach them better’: Michael Irvin tears into struggling Cowboys
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys legend didn't hold back after Dallas surrendered a late lead against Arizona
articles.summary: The Cowboys legend didn't hold back after Dallas surrendered a late lead against Arizona
articles.body:
Michael Irvin delivered a furious verdict on the Dallas Cowboys following their latest defeat, declaring that even his late mother could do a better job coaching the struggling team.

The Hall of Fame wide receiver made the explosive remark during an appearance on ESPN’s First Take on Monday, a day after Dallas squandered a fourth-quarter lead and suffered a heartbreaking 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals.

Irvin’s outburst came as Stephen A. Smith suggested an unconventional solution to the Cowboys’ problems: bringing ESPN colleague and former NFL head coach Rex Ryan onto the Dallas sideline.

Smith argued that Ryan could make a significant difference with just four days to prepare, considering the disappointing performances the team has produced throughout the season.

Irvin was even less restrained in his comments. He insisted the Cowboys had reached rock bottom, suggesting there was no worse level of performance for the franchise to sink to.

“There is no such thing as lower than this, or worse than this, or not as good as this. They are the worst.” Irvin said. ”My dead mom can coach them better."

The latest defeat offered plenty of reasons for anger. Dallas appeared to have secured the victory after building a 30-24 advantage with just seconds remaining in regulation.

However, Arizona backup quarterback Gardner Minshew sparked a remarkable turnaround after replacing Jacoby Brissett late in the third quarter, helping the Cardinals produce a late touchdown with six seconds left.

Kicker Chad Ryland missed the extra point that could have secured the win, forcing overtime. However, he eventually redeemed himself by converting a 42-yard field goal to complete Arizona’s comeback.

Irvin demands major changes after Cowboys collapse

Irvin had already called for a sweeping overhaul in a video shared through his podcast account, arguing that Dallas needed to dismantle its defensive setup and make significant changes. His animated reaction while watching the final moments demonstrated just how deeply the defeat had affected him.

Arizona running back Tyler Allgeier played a major role in the comeback, recording a spectacular 63-yard touchdown run, another 52-yard carry and a receiving touchdown. Dallas' defense, which had looked considerably better earlier in the contest, struggled to contain the Cardinals after Minshew entered the game.

Former Cowboys quarterback Ben DiNucci also expressed his disappointment, describing the performance as embarrassing.

He questioned the team's effort and argued that established leaders, including Dak Prescott, Quinnen Williams and CeeDee Lamb , needed to take responsibility for the atmosphere inside the locker room.

DiNucci also suggested that the constant attention and distractions surrounding the Cowboys organization could make it difficult for players to remain completely focused on football.

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer is consequently facing growing scrutiny as Dallas searches for answers. His 10-14-1 record since taking charge has added to the pressure, particularly with the Cowboys struggling to establish consistency.

Dallas now faces an important road matchup against the Indianapolis Colts. With the team's playoff hopes becoming increasingly uncertain, the Cowboys desperately need a response.

articles.standfirst: Cowboys face another roster headache as tight-end depth becomes a growing concern
articles.summary: Cowboys face another roster headache as tight-end depth becomes a growing concern
articles.body:
Jake Ferguson’s ankle injury has added another problem to a Dallas Cowboys team already searching for answers after a disappointing Week 8 defeat.

The tight end was forced out of Sunday’s 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals, leaving the club short of options at a position that was already depleted before kickoff.

Ferguson initially injured his ankle during Dallas’ opening possession and headed to the locker room for evaluation. Although he managed to return to the field, his comeback was short-lived.

The veteran aggravated the injury and was eventually ruled out for the remainder of the contest. Subsequent reporting indicated that he had suffered a low-ankle sprain.

His absence was particularly concerning because Luke Schoonmaker was already unavailable after being ruled out with a groin injury.

That left Brevyn Spann-Ford and James Mitchell responsible for handling the tight-end workload against Arizona. Mitchell had also been elevated from the practice squad for his first appearance of the 2026 season.

Cowboys could be forced into the free-agent market

Ferguson’s injury comes during a difficult campaign for the veteran, whose performances have fallen below expectations.

His contribution as a receiver has declined, while his blocking hasn't consistently provided the reliability Dallas needs from the position. Spann-Ford has consequently earned a larger role, even starting ahead of Ferguson in recent games.

Nevertheless, the Cowboys can't afford to overlook their lack of depth. Losing another tight end would leave the offense with limited options, particularly if Schoonmaker's recovery takes longer than expected.

That makes bringing in an experienced free agent a possibility worth exploring. Dallas doesn't necessarily need a headline-grabbing signing, but adding someone capable of contributing as both a blocker and receiver could provide some much-needed stability.

A dependable veteran would also give the coaching staff greater flexibility when putting together offensive packages.

The wider situation makes the decision more pressing. Dallas dropped to 3-5 following its overtime defeat, intensifying questions about the roster and coaching staff.

Linebacker Von Miller defended the coaches afterward, arguing that the players' disappointing performance wasn't a reflection of the preparation and work being done behind the scenes.

“The product that went out there is not a reflection of our coaching staff,” said Miller .

“This is pro sports. This is not parenting. So at the end of the day, the buck has to stop somewhere. Somebody’s going to get the blame.

“But my opinion, this is just me, I don’t know nothing about football. I only played 16 years. We’ve got great coaches. We’ve got a great coaching staff. And that’s not a reflection of how they coach us and get us ready every week.”

However, results ultimately matter in professional football, and the Cowboys' problems can't simply be separated into coaching or personnel issues. If the players aren't executing the game plan, questions inevitably arise about whether the roster has enough quality to compete consistently.

Owner and general manager Jerry Jones has repeatedly backed the team's direction through difficult stretches. But if he believes the coaching staff is doing its job and the players are responsible for the disappointing results, responsibility for improving the roster ultimately falls on him.

articles.title: Trade deadline drama: Cowboys urged to dump Pickens amid coaching buzz
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys may be ready to make a shocking move with George Pickens as questions grow about his future in Dallas.
articles.summary: The Cowboys may be ready to make a shocking move with George Pickens as questions grow about his future in Dallas.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys could be approaching major decisions regarding their roster, and one of the names emerging at the center of the discussion is George Pickens . After another painful loss that raised more questions about the franchise’s direction, some analysts believe Dallas should be willing to listen to offers for its star wide receiver.

The Cowboys dropped to 3-5 after blowing a 14-point fourth-quarter lead and suffering a 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals . The latest setback intensified criticism surrounding the team and sparked debate over Pickens’ true role within the offense.

During an analysis on Pro Football Talk , reporter Mike Florio suggested that a contending team should immediately contact Dallas about the receiver, especially with the name of Mike Tomlin gaining traction as a potential option for the franchise’s future.

“If I’m a contender looking for a receiver, I’m calling the Cowboys about George Pickens. It feels like that’s broken now. If they can get a second-round pick — they gave up a third — you move on and think about the future,” Florio said. “You have Ryan Flournoy, who isn’t George Pickens but good enough. Especially if you’re thinking about Tomlin, you don’t want Pickens around.”

The mention of Tomlin is not a coincidence. The coach worked with Pickens during his time with the Pittsburgh Steelers before the receiver was traded to Dallas, and their relationship featured some moments of tension.

A trade would also allow the Cowboys to regain valuable draft capital. Dallas acquired Pickens in May 2025 in exchange for a 2026 third-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round selection , while receiving a 2027 sixth-round pick from Pittsburgh.

George Pickens’ role in Dallas’ offense raises questions

Pickens’ role once again became a topic of discussion following the loss to Arizona. The receiver finished the game with just two receptions for 48 yards on four targets , while also seeing fewer snaps than other offensive players: 42 snaps, compared to 50 for Ryan Flournoy and 56 for CeeDee Lamb.

Still, Pickens showed his ability to change the course of a game. A 37-yard reception played a key role in setting up Dak Prescott ’s rushing touchdown early in the fourth quarter, a play that extended Dallas’ lead to 24-10.

This season, the receiver has recorded 39 catches for 533 yards and two touchdowns . However, his contract situation is a major factor: he is currently playing under a $27.3 million franchise tag , and a long-term extension cannot be negotiated until after the regular season ends.

Dallas could use the franchise tag on him again next offseason, but if the Cowboys truly view Pickens as part of their future plans, the priority would be reaching a long-term agreement. The biggest question is whether the financial commitment fits the team’s vision.

Mike Tomlin adds more pressure to the Cowboys’ future

The name of Mike Tomlin has resurfaced around Dallas following the collapse against Arizona. During NBC’s Football Night in America, the former Steelers coach questioned the team’s inability to close out games when it has opportunities to take control.

Tomlin has been mentioned as a potential candidate if the Cowboys decide to part ways with Brian Schottenheimer . His track record makes him an appealing option for owner Jerry Jones .

During his 19 seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers , Tomlin recorded 193 regular-season victories, reached the playoffs 13 times , and made two Super Bowl appearances, winning one championship.

Despite the team’s struggles, Jerry Jones said after the loss to Arizona that he was not considering a coaching change at that time, meaning Schottenheimer remains in charge.

Now, Dallas’ biggest decision could involve its roster. The NFL trade deadline is November 10 , leaving the Cowboys with one final game — against a struggling Indianapolis Colts team — before deciding whether to keep Pickens or listen to offers for one of their most talented players.

articles.title: Everything's falling apart in Dallas: Cowboys players are hiding and going silent
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys’ latest collapse was followed by an unusual scene in Dallas.
articles.summary: The Cowboys’ latest collapse was followed by an unusual scene in Dallas.
articles.body:
One day after one of the most embarrassing losses of the season, the Dallas Cowboys found themselves at the center of another controversy after skipping their usual media availability following their defeat to the Arizona Cardinals , a team that earned its first-ever victory at AT&T Stadium .

Are the players hiding? Total silence in Dallas

The majority of the Cowboys’ players had already left the facility before the scheduled media session , leaving the locker room nearly empty when reporters arrived.

“The Cowboys had locker room availability, but the majority of the roster had already left before we got in there. No players were interviewed. I can’t say I remember something like that happening before,” explained Jon Machota of The Athletic .

Later, Joseph Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News reported that the reason was that the players’ internal programs had ended earlier than scheduled, which left very few players available during the time reserved for media access.

However, the situation raised questions given the team’s current struggles. Media availability is a weekly obligation for all NFL teams , and the absence of players came immediately after a particularly painful loss.

The Cowboys blew a 14-point fourth-quarter lead for the first time in franchise history and ultimately lost 33-30 in overtime to a Cardinals team that entered the game with just two wins on the season.

Arizona has also become a surprisingly difficult opponent for Dallas in recent years , adding to the frustration surrounding a franchise that continues searching for consistency while facing increasing questions about its direction.

articles.title: Stephen A. Smith demands Jerry Jones hire Rex Ryan to save the doomed Cowboys
articles.standfirst: Dallas is falling out of contention behind the New York Giants in the NFC East
articles.summary: Dallas is falling out of contention behind the New York Giants in the NFC East
articles.body:
S tephen A. Smith is not the biggest fan of the Dallas Cowboys , but even their latest collapse has prompted him to offer Jerry Jones a solution as the pundit wants Rex Ryan as the new defensive coordinator to fix a unit that has repeatedly let the team down. Dallas ’ 33-30 overtime defeat to the Cardinals left the Cowboys 3-5 and further behind the New York Giants in the NFC East as a two-touchdown lead in the fourth quarter disappeared as Arizona scored late to force overtime and then kicked the winning field goal.

The loss the situation at a Dallas team whose season is slipping away as the Cowboys led by 14 points early in the fourth quarter and looked to be in control, but Gardner Minshew inspired four consecutive scoring possessions to bring the lowly NFC West side level. Running back Tyler Allgeier was central to the turnaround, finishing with 147 rushing yards and 44 receiving yards and his 63-yard touchdown run sparked Arizona ’s comeback, whilst Michael Wilson also caught eight passes for 111 yards, including the game-tying catch. And Smith made his proposal on ESPN’s First Take on Monday, arguing that Ryan should leave his television role and return to the NFL as the Cowboys ’ defensive coordinator following another damaging performance under Christian Parker , who appears to be lacking answers. “He should be the new defensive coordinator for the Dallas Cowboys and come to the rescue for America’s team,” Smith said on First Take as he also urged Jones to contact ESPN immediately, arguing Ryan could make a difference with only four days to prepare for the next game.

Is Ryan a viable candidate for Jerry Jones and the Cowboys?

Chad Ryland missed the extra point after Wilson ’s touchdown, giving Dallas a reprieve, but the Cowboys could not take advantage in overtime and after both teams initially went three-and-out, Arizona moved into range and their kicker converted a 42-yard field goal. Ryan brings a high-profile name and extensive experience, but his time away from coaching is significant as he has not been an NFL head coach since 2015 and has not served as a defensive coordinator since departing the Baltimore Ravens in 2008 to move into broadcasting. Smith ’s suggestion, though, is not an indication that Dallas is preparing to make a change as the Cowboys already have Parker directing the defense, and Jones has not announced plans to replace him even in the wake of growing frustration around the team. Quarterback Dak Prescott has resisted pinning the defeat on one individual, insisting responsibility belongs to everyone involved rejecting the easy and cowardly approach of blaming one person, but it’s hard to ignore the growing pressure as the unit has not stepped up even after bringing aboard Joey Porter Jr. from the Pittsburgh Steelers . The 4-2 Giants sit ahead of Dallas in the NFC East , while the Cowboys ’ 3-5 record leaves them needing a sustained run to get back into the playoff picture as their next opportunity comes against the Indianapolis Colts on November 8. With the defense under scrutiny and the season reaching a critical point, calls for changes are likely to continue and a failure to beat a Colts team that is having a fire sale could represent the tipping point for the Cowboys owner.

articles.title: The $240 Million Ultimatum: An inside look at the rumors threatening to end Dak Prescott's era in Dallas
articles.standfirst: Is Prescott’s time with the Cowboys starting to head to a close?
articles.summary: Is Prescott’s time with the Cowboys starting to head to a close?
articles.body:
Chris Simms has raised fresh questions about Dak Prescott ’s future in Dallas , claiming there are “murmurs” that the Cowboys are losing patience with their $240 million quarterback with his comments arriving as the team’s season threatens to unravel. Speaking Monday, after Dallas surrendered a 14-point fourth-quarter lead in a 33-30 overtime defeat to the Arizona Cardinals and the former NFL quarterback suggested Prescott could be playing to keep his job.

“There’s been some murmurs that,” Simms said. “In Dallas, that they’re a little bit like at the end of their rope with Dak Prescott. Like, it’s like things better turn around or he ain’t gonna be the quarterback there next year. “We’ll see. We’ll see. For what they’re paying him, he’s not one of the top quarterbacks in football. That’s not even debatable, and he’s got some of the best support around him.” The contract makes any separation complicated. Prescott signed a four-year, $240 million extension in 2024, running through 2028, with $231 million guaranteed and a no-trade clause. A release before June 1, 2027 would reportedly leave Dallas with $131 million in dead money, falling to $76 million afterwards. A trade would carry cap charges of $86 million or $31 million, respectively and those financial obstacles mean the reported frustration does not automatically point to an imminent departure. Simms offered no named source for the alleged discontent, and Dallas has not confirmed plans to move on.

Cardinals collapse intensifies pressure on Prescott

The latest defeat has intensified the debate as Dallas fell to 3-5 after surrendering a 14-point fourth-quarter advantage, allowing Arizona to force overtime before Chad Ryland converted a 42-yard field goal for a 33-30 victory. Tyler Allgeier led the comeback with 147 rushing yards and 44 receiving yards, including a 63-yard touchdown run whilst Michael Wilson produced 111 receiving yards. Dallas had an opportunity to escape after Ryland missed the extra point, but could not capitalize in overtime, opening the door to the NFC West side to eventually move into range and secured the victory. Prescott has resisted attempts to blame one individual, insisting responsibility belongs across the organization, and the Cowboys have also missed the playoffs in 2024 and 2025, while their 3-5 start has placed another postseason appearance in doubt. His record and the franchise's continued Super Bowl drought have only increased scrutiny but whether the reported murmurs lead to a genuine change remains uncertain. Dallas faces the Indianapolis Colts on November 8, with their veteran quarterback under pressure to help stop the slide and strengthen his position as the short-term future of the team.

articles.title: Jerry Jones’ brutal George Pickens message puts Dak Prescott and Brian Schottenheimer in the spotlight
articles.standfirst: Jerry Jones is calling for changes after George Pickens’ shocking lack of involvement raised questions about the Cowboys’ offense.
articles.summary: Jerry Jones is calling for changes after George Pickens’ shocking lack of involvement raised questions about the Cowboys’ offense.
articles.body:
It’s become clear that Jerry Jones holds nothing back when it comes to sharing his opinions about the team he owns. The Dallas Cowboys are not in the best of situations despite having several of the best players in the entire NFL , but there’s one player in particular from whom Jones believes Brian Schottenheimer could get more production.

That player is George Pickens , who has taken on a secondary role in this offense even though he has previously shown he has everything needed to take the team to another level.

Jerry Jones holds nothing back when talking about George Pickens

Jerry Jones didn’t mince words when discussing George Pickens’ role in the Dallas Cowboys’ offense. The team’s owner made it clear that the star receiver needs to be more involved in the attack.

“He needs the ball coming his way more,” Jones said during his weekly appearance on 105.3 The Fan .

The comments come after a difficult performance by Dallas in their loss to the Arizona Cardinals . Pickens recorded just two receptions and played only 42 snaps—even fewer than the team’s third receiver, Ryan Flournoy.

Questions about his usage had already been raised, but the controversy grew after Sunday’s game when a video showed Pickens quickly leaving the field and heading to the locker room before the Cardinals’ game-winning field goal had even fully decided the outcome.

For Jones, giving the receiver a bigger role could be one of the keys to getting the Cowboys’ offense back on track.

“There’s a good argument about what we can do differently than what we did the other day. We have to send more balls in that direction,” the Dallas owner explained.

Pickens is playing this season under a one-year franchise tag worth $27.3 million , meaning he could become a free agent at the end of the campaign if the Cowboys do not reach an agreement to extend his contract.

Additionally, his situation makes him a potential trade-deadline target before the NFL’s November 10 cutoff , especially with Dallas going through a difficult stretch and sitting at 3-5 .

articles.title: Cowboys receive brutal reality check amid offensive struggles
articles.standfirst: Dallas has plenty of talent on offense, but one ESPN analyst believes the Cowboys are nowhere near being a Super Bowl-caliber unit.
articles.summary: Dallas has plenty of talent on offense, but one ESPN analyst believes the Cowboys are nowhere near being a Super Bowl-caliber unit.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys continue to search for answers, and their recent 33-30 loss to the Arizona Cardinals has raised serious concerns surrounding the team. While head coach Brian Schottenheimer faces increasing scrutiny over the direction of the franchise, ESPN analyst Dan Orlovsky has pointed to another major problem in Dallas: an offense that, in his opinion, is far from elite.

Dan Orlovsky delivers harsh criticism of the Cowboys' offense

During his appearance on ESPN's NFL Live , Orlovsky questioned why the Cowboys continue to be considered a team with an offense capable of competing for the Super Bowl . Although he acknowledged the individual talent on the roster, he argued that the offensive system has significant shortcomings when measured against the demands of today's NFL.

The former quarterback identified three areas that highlight Dallas' limitations, starting with its inability to handle opposing defenses' blitzes.

“One, good offenses are great against the blitz. They're terrible against the blitz, in all facets,” Orlovsky said.

Orlovsky also criticized the team's lack of formation variety, particularly its limited use of condensed formations and receiver groupings that can create mismatches and confuse opposing defenses.

“Number two, we've talked a ton about getting into strong splits, shrinking your formation, stacks, bunches. They do it the least in the NFL,” Orlovsky continued.

The third weakness he highlighted was Dallas' lack of motion before the snap (pre-snap motion) and at the snap, a strategy increasingly used by the league's most efficient offenses.

“The third thing is motion, pre-snap motion, at-the-snap motion. They're the third-lowest in the NFL, and so for an organization and for people covering the NFL that continue to say, ‘We got a Super Bowl caliber offense.' No, you don't. articles.title: Jerry Jones ‘distances himself’ from Michael Irvin after justifying latest financial decision, complicating player’s return to the Cowboys
articles.standfirst: Irvin's extraordinary criticism of Dallas' coaching has exposed disagreement with Jones
articles.summary: Irvin's extraordinary criticism of Dallas' coaching has exposed disagreement with Jones
articles.body:
Jerry Jones has spent decades defending his decisions as owner of the Dallas Cowboys , but his latest explanation for the franchise's coaching philosophy has placed him on the opposite side of an increasingly heated debate involving one of his most celebrated former players.

Michael Irvin , who helped Dallas win three Super Bowls during the 1990s, has become one of the loudest critics of the team's performances under Brian Schottenheimer , delivering a devastating assessment following Sunday's 33-30 overtime defeat against the Arizona Cardinals .

The Cowboys squandered a 24-10 fourth-quarter advantage before suffering their fifth defeat in eight games, intensifying questions about Schottenheimer's future and Jones' reluctance to make another coaching change.

However, the 84-year-old owner has maintained his support for Schottenheimer , arguing that spending more money on an established head coach doesn't necessarily produce better results.

"There is zero correlation between how much you pay a coach or how many coaches you have as to winning," Jones said during Tuesday's appearance on 105.3 The Fan.

"There is no correlation. And that's a random sample of years and all 32 teams involved. So put that in your hopper and smoke it."

Irvin delivers brutal Cowboys assessment

Jones ' comments came shortly after Irvin publicly questioned whether Schottenheimer should remain in charge following another disappointing defensive collapse.

Speaking on ESPN's First Take, the former Cowboys receiver expressed his frustration in unusually personal terms.

"There is no worse that you can be than what they are right now," Irvin said. "There is no such thing as lower than this or worse than this. They are the worst. Anybody, my dead mom could coach them better."

Fellow analyst Stephen A. Smith also called for change, suggesting Jones should consider former NFL head coach Rex Ryan as a potential replacement.

Jones , however, has indicated that he doesn't intend to dismiss Schottenheimer during the season, despite Dallas recording a 10-14-1 mark under his leadership.

The contrasting positions have highlighted the growing frustration surrounding the Cowboys , who haven't reached an NFC Championship Game since their last Super Bowl-winning campaign in the 1995 season.

Could Irvin's criticism damage chances of Dallas return?

The disagreement arrives amid suggestions from supporters that former Cowboys stars Irvin and Troy Aikman could help restore the franchise's championship culture through organizational roles.

Jones has previously acknowledged the possibility of involving Aikman , although no formal appointment has been announced for either former player.

Irvin 's latest comments could make any potential return more complicated, given his public criticism of a coach whom Jones continues to defend.

With Dallas preparing to face the Indianapolis Colts in Week 9, the immediate challenge remains turning around a season already threatening to slip away.

Jones believes stability and his existing coaching philosophy provide the best path forward, while Irvin 's increasingly forceful criticism suggests he has considerably less patience with the current approach.

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys cheerleader Emily Awbrey “blames” two teammates for her return after being fired: “I hit rock bottom”
articles.standfirst: Awbrey had lost her confidence in her ability to perform, but two close friends have helped her recover
articles.summary: Awbrey had lost her confidence in her ability to perform, but two close friends have helped her recover
articles.body:
E mily Awbrey has two Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders to thank for helping her find the confidence to audition again after being cut in 2025 as the 24-year-old says Faith Ward and Taylor Altieri helped her confront the fear that had threatened to end her dream. Awbrey discussed their influence by explaining that the disappointment of missing out on the squad initially sent her into a difficult period and although she knew she wanted another chance, she struggled to make herself take that step.

“I actually, to be so honest, I think I went lower before I went higher,” Awbrey said to Page Six. “So I got cut and I always knew I wanted to audition again but I kind of just, I got in a bit of a rut where my headspace was more, ‘I’m scared to try again because what if I fail?’ “And they kind of were the ones who lit that fire in me and reminded me that there’s so many people that are supporting me,” she explained. “And truly the only person at that time who was being negative was myself, in my head.” The change began when Awbrey travelled back to Dallas to watch Ward perform as Ward had made the 2025 team, whilst Altieri , a cheerleader since 2023, offered a place to stay during the visit and encouraged her to try again. Altieri also shared a connection with Awbrey beyond cheerleading: both women are from Oregon as their encouragement helped her see another audition as an opportunity rather than a risk she should avoid, and she decided to approach the process differently. “I need to just listen to this and run to it and not be as scared of it,” Awbrey added, as she believed fear had held her back the previous year, and said she did not use traditional therapy to change her mindset at that point. Instead, she described the shift as something she had to make herself, recognizing that she needed to stop allowing self-doubt to dictate whether she pursued the goal, and the renewed determination ultimately carried her back into the audition process. Her second attempt ended with the outcome she had hoped for: Awbrey was named a Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader for the 2026-2027 NFL season, joining the duo on the squad. The three women are now teammates after playing different roles in her journey back.

Cowboys look to bolster running back room

Dallas are looking to add depth at running back after hosting three players for tryouts on Tuesday, including former New York Giants and Cowboys runner Jashaun Corbin as the 26-year-old spent around three and a half weeks with the team during the 2026 preseason. Corbin has the most NFL experience of the three players evaluated, and he also played six regular-season games for the Giants in 2023, recording one rushing yard and three receptions for 12 yards. But has since spent time with several teams, including the Atlanta Falcons , New England Patriots and San Antonio Brahmas . He previously led the UFL with 514 rushing yards in 10 games during the 2025 season. Dallas also worked out Damon Bankston and Blake Watson as the team considers its options before Sunday's Week 9 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts .

articles.title: Michael Irvin says his dead mother could coach the Cowboys better after embarrassing loss
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys legend and three-time Super Bowl champion Michael Irvin delivered a blistering criticism of his former team's coaching staff during ESPN's First Take on November 2, 2026.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys legend and three-time Super Bowl champion Michael Irvin delivered a blistering criticism of his former team's coaching staff during ESPN's First Take on November 2, 2026.

The comments followed the Cowboys' 33-30 overtime defeat to the Arizona Cardinals on November 1. Dallas had led 24-10 in the fourth quarter before surrendering its advantage and losing at home.

During a discussion with Stephen A. Smith about head coach Brian Schottenheimer, Irvin argued that virtually anyone could coach Dallas better, even invoking his deceased mother to emphasize how poorly he believed the team was performing.

Smith suggested that Cowboys owner Jerry Jones should consider bringing in former NFL head coach Rex Ryan. However, Jones indicated after the loss that he wasn't considering an immediate coaching change.

The defeat dropped Dallas to 3-5, intensifying criticism of the team's coaching and defensive performance.

articles.title: Brian Schottenheimer identifies Cowboys’ biggest problem amid frustrating season
articles.standfirst: After falling to 3-5 following another frustrating loss, Brian Schottenheimer revealed what he believes is holding the Cowboys back and took responsibility for the team's struggles.
articles.summary: After falling to 3-5 following another frustrating loss, Brian Schottenheimer revealed what he believes is holding the Cowboys back and took responsibility for the team's struggles.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are still searching for answers after another disappointing result: a 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals that once again exposed the problems of a team that has yet to find consistency.

Dallas enters Week 9 with a 3-5 record and has lost three of its last four games. Now the Cowboys have a chance to change the narrative when they face the Indianapolis Colts — a game that could serve as a turning point to regain confidence and keep their season alive.

But before focusing on their next opponent, the Cowboys must address the main reason for their uneven performance. According to head coach Brian Schottenheimer, the issue is not a lack of effort, but the team’s inability to execute in critical moments.

Brian Schottenheimer identifies the Cowboys’ problem

After the loss to Arizona, Schottenheimer was asked about the team’s attitude through the first half of the season and dismissed the idea that effort is the problem.

“It’s not an effort issue. It’s an execution issue. That starts with me as a head coach,” Schottenheimer said. “I’m responsible for everything that happens here. Our execution has to get cleaner and what we have to do is we have to be able to put some of these close games away that we’ve unfortunately let slip away from us. And that comes down to execution.”

The numbers reflect Dallas’s struggles, especially on defense. The Cowboys head into the matchup against Indianapolis as the NFL ’s worst defense, allowing 385.4 yards per game , and also rank last against the run at 152.8 rushing yards allowed per contest.

The offense, by contrast, has kept the team competitive and ranks 13th in the NFL with an average of 342 total yards per game .

Jerry Jones maintains his support for Schottenheimer

Despite the difficult start, Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones said he has no plans to make a coaching change.

“That’s not in my mind at this time,” Jones said. “This is an indictment of the whole show … This is a criticism of everyone.”

The owner recalled that he has made significant midseason decisions in the past, such as firing Wade Phillips , but made clear he does not see a similar situation with Schottenheimer.

“I’m not proud of it, but I made a change with Wade Phillips there in the middle of the season,” Jones added. “I don’t see that here at all.”

Jones even defended the Dallas coach and insisted the responsibility for the team’s struggles is collective.

“I will say that a lot of people let Brian down today. For whatever criticism we have of Brian, we can all get in line.”

The owner also took some of the blame for the team’s current situation.

“Well, I don’t know,” Jones said. “None of us are getting it done and that should be my concern. So I’m not pointing at Schotty, I’m not pointing to anybody, but none of us have it done. I haven’t been involved in too many games that we should have wanted and we had the opportunities we had to win this game. So that is a big snapshot that we want to put above our mirror.”

A win against the Colts could shift the atmosphere around Dallas and give the team some breathing room amid the pressure. But another loss could increase the doubts surrounding a franchise that needs to respond before its season becomes even more complicated.

articles.title: Maxx Crosby has a message for Jerry Jones as Cowboys trade rumors don't go away
articles.standfirst: Maxx Crosby puts an end to trade rumors and reveals where he wants to continue his NFL career.
articles.summary: Maxx Crosby puts an end to trade rumors and reveals where he wants to continue his NFL career.
articles.body:
L as Vegas Raiders star Maxx Crosby has put an end to speculation about his future with the franchise, making it clear that he has no intention of leaving despite persistent trade rumors. The defensive end reaffirmed his commitment to the team just before the Raiders’ Week 9 visit to the San Francisco 49ers (6-1) .

Amid reports suggesting a possible departure from Las Vegas, Crosby used his media availability on Wednesday to express his desire to stay with the Raiders.

“I love being a Raider, I’ve said that about a million times, this is where I want to be.”

The comments come after Las Vegas (4-4) secured an important 38-33 victory over the New York Jets in Week 8 , snapping a four-game losing streak against the Kansas City Chiefs, Buffalo Bills, New England Patriots, and Los Angeles Rams.

Crosby remains one of the cornerstones of the Raiders’ defense. Through eight games in the 2026 season , he has recorded 22 tackles, three sacks, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery, and one pass defended.

In the win over the Jets, the edge rusher contributed four tackles and a sack, helping Las Vegas return to a .500 record before facing one of the toughest tests on its schedule.

Maxx Crosby clarifies his future with the Raiders after a turbulent offseason

Crosby’s remarks carry extra weight given what happened during the offseason, when his continued presence in Las Vegas was nearly ruled out following a trade agreement with the Baltimore Ravens .

The Raiders had agreed to send the defensive end to Baltimore in exchange for two first-round draft picks, including the No. 14 overall selection in 2026 and another in 2027 .

However, the Ravens backed out of the deal after concerns arose about Crosby’s knee — which had undergone surgery — during his medical examinations.

The collapsed trade fueled doubts about the edge rusher’s future, especially after Crosby himself shared some unusual details about his visit to Baltimore.

On an episode of his show The Rush With Maxx Crosby , he described an awkward meeting with Ravens head coach Jesse Minter and revealed that he never even got the chance to meet with the team’s general manager.

In the end, Crosby remained in Las Vegas to begin the 2026 season and is once again publicly stating his desire to stay with the Raiders.

The franchise, meanwhile, is trying to build a more competitive roster under head coach Klint Kubiak after a disappointing 3-14 campaign in 2025 .

Sitting at 4-4 and having regained some confidence with the win over the Jets, the Raiders will look to make another statement when they visit San Francisco. In the meantime, Crosby appears to know exactly where he wants to continue his career: Las Vegas.

articles.title: Cowboys legend joins Michael Irvin and suggests a surprising replacement for Brian Schottenheimer to Jerry Jones: “I can see it”
articles.standfirst: Dez Bryant has identified Jason Witten as his preferred candidate to lead Dallas if Jerry Jones decides to make a coaching change
articles.summary: Dez Bryant has identified Jason Witten as his preferred candidate to lead Dallas if Jerry Jones decides to make a coaching change
articles.body:
The pressure on Brian Schottenheimer is increasing after the Dallas Cowboys slipped to a 3-5 record with a painful overtime defeat against the Arizona Cardinals .

While owner Jerry Jones has insisted that dismissing his head coach is not currently under consideration, former Cowboys wide receiver Dez Bryant has already suggested an alternative.

Bryant believes Jason Witten could be the man to take charge in Dallas if the franchise eventually decides to move on from Schottenheimer.

His recommendation comes after Hall of Fame receiver Michael Irvin also publicly criticised the team's direction following Sunday's 33-30 defeat.

Taking to X on November 5, Bryant made his preference clear, backing his former teammate for the position.

“I’m just saying… if anything were to happen in Dallas…Jason Witten should be the next head coach of the Dallas Cowboys ,” Bryant wrote. “I can see it..and I’d love that.”

Bryant knows Witten particularly well after sharing the Cowboys locker room with him for eight seasons between 2010 and 2017.

The pair were important figures in Dallas' offence, building a strong relationship during a period when the franchise regularly relied on their contributions.

Witten spent 16 seasons with the Cowboys across two spells, making 255 appearances and earning 11 Pro Bowl selections.

He finished his NFL career with 1,228 receptions for 13,046 yards and 74 touchdowns, establishing himself as one of the most productive tight ends in league history.

His leadership and experience are among the qualities that could make him attractive to Bryant , although moving directly from college coaching into an NFL head-coaching position would represent a significant step.

Witten's coaching opportunity at Oklahoma could strengthen his case

Witten has already started building a coaching career since retiring from professional football.

He became head coach at Liberty Christian School in Texas in 2021, guiding the programme to consecutive state championships in 2023 and 2024 and recording a 26-1 record across those two seasons.

In January 2026, he joined Oklahoma as tight ends coach, taking his first position in college football. He has since received a major promotion following the dismissal of offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle on November 2.

Sooners head coach Brent Venables appointed Witten interim offensive coordinator and play-caller for the remainder of the season.

“The greatest teaching tool for me was coaching high school because it really taught me, coming from the NFL, that they don’t learn like I do,” Witten previously explained.

“I learned they don’t have the same expectation. So how do I impact, how do I reach them, how do I get that?”

Venables also explained the responsibility being handed to the former Cowboys star.

“Beginning today, he [Witten] will lead our offensive staff in preparing a clear and focused plan that gives our players the best opportunity to execute with confidence,” he said.

Meanwhile, Dallas' immediate priority remains recovering from its collapse against Arizona. The Cowboys surrendered a 14-point fourth-quarter advantage before losing 33-30 in overtime, falling to 3-5.

Jones subsequently defended the coaching staff, saying a change was not something he was considering at that moment.

Witten's new responsibilities at Oklahoma will provide an opportunity to demonstrate his coaching ability, but Bryant's suggestion remains a hypothetical one.

For now, Schottenheimer retains the Cowboys job, while the former tight end has an important challenge ahead of him in Norman.

He finished his NFL career with 1,228 receptions for 13,046 yards and 74 touchdowns, establishing himself as one of the most productive tight ends in league history.

His leadership and experience are among the qualities that could make him attractive to Bryant , although moving directly from college coaching into an NFL head-coaching position would represent a significant step.
Witten's coaching opportunity at Oklahoma could strengthen his case
Witten has already started building a coaching career since retiring from professional football.
He became head coach at Liberty Christian School in Texas in 2021, guiding the programme to consecutive state championships in 2023 and 2024 and recording a 26-1 record across those two seasons.

In January 2026, he joined Oklahoma as tight ends coach, taking his first position in college football. He has since received a major promotion following the dismissal of offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle on November 2.
Sooners head coach Brent Venables appointed Witten interim offensive coordinator and play-caller for the remainder of the season.
“The greatest teaching tool for me was coaching high school because it really taught me, coming from the NFL, that they don’t learn like I do,” Witten previously explained.
“I learned they don’t have the same expectation. So how do I impact, how do I reach them, how do I get that?”
Venables also explained the responsibility being handed to the former Cowboys star.
“Beginning today, he [Witten] will lead our offensive staff in preparing a clear and focused plan that gives our players the best opportunity to execute with confidence,” he said.

Meanwhile, Dallas' immediate priority remains recovering from its collapse against Arizona. The Cowboys surrendered a 14-point fourth-quarter advantage before losing 33-30 in overtime, falling to 3-5.
Jones subsequently defended the coaching staff, saying a change was not something he was considering at that moment.
Witten's new responsibilities at Oklahoma will provide an opportunity to demonstrate his coaching ability, but Bryant's suggestion remains a hypothetical one.
For now, Schottenheimer retains the Cowboys job, while the former tight end has an important challenge ahead of him in Norman.

articles.title: From ‘The Bachelor’ to second DWI: Former Cowboys cheerleader Melissa Rycroft seeks help after crashing into ambulance on Halloween
articles.standfirst: The reality tv star has spoken publicly about difficulties and impact on her family after another troubling incident
articles.summary: The reality tv star has spoken publicly about difficulties and impact on her family after another troubling incident
articles.body:
Melissa Rycroft spent years building a television career after rising to fame as a Dallas Cowboys cheerleader, but the former Bachelor contestant is now facing another legal controversy that has prompted a deeply personal admission about her life away from the cameras.

The 43-year-old was arrested following a Halloween collision involving an ambulance in Southlake, Texas, marking her second driving while intoxicated case in just over a year.

Rather than remaining silent about the latest incident, Rycroft addressed her followers on Instagram on November 3, acknowledging the distress her circumstances have caused those closest to her.

"First, please know how deeply ashamed and embarrassed I am, especially knowing how much this has affected my friends and family," she wrote.

The television personality explained that she had been dealing with private difficulties for some time, despite maintaining a positive public appearance.

"I've been struggling with my mental health for quite some time now. It has completely overwhelmed me," Rycroft admitted.

Her statement came just months after she pleaded guilty to an earlier DWI offense, adding another complication to a legal situation that remains unresolved.

Melissa Rycroft faces second DWI charge

According to the Southlake Police Department, officers responded to a reported collision shortly before 6 p.m. on October 31 involving a Southlake Fire Department ambulance.

Investigators alleged that another vehicle struck the ambulance while it was stopped at a stop sign before leaving the scene. Police subsequently located the vehicle and identified Rycroft as its driver.

No injuries were reported, although the former NFL cheerleader was charged with a second DWI offense, driving with an invalid license and an accident involving property damage exceeding $200.

The arrest followed a separate incident in September 2025, when Rycroft crashed her Cadillac Escalade into a tree and was arrested on suspicion of intoxicated driving.

She pleaded guilty in August 2026 and received 20 months of probation, alongside additional financial penalties and court requirements.

Admission of need for professional help

Rycroft first attracted national attention through the 13th season of The Bachelor before becoming a familiar television personality through Dancing With the Stars, winning the competition's all-star season in 2012.

She shares three children with her husband, Tye Strickland , and emphasized that her family's support had become particularly important during her recent difficulties.

"No excuses at all, but I'm finally admitting that I need help. I've fought this for a long time on my own, and it's time to admit that I can't do it anymore," she wrote.

Rycroft confirmed that she was receiving professional care and expressed her determination to regain a sense of stability.

"I'm ready to feel like myself again, for me and for my family. They have stood by me through all of this, and they deserve honesty," she added.

Her decision to speak publicly marks a significant moment for the former reality star, although her personal statement does not resolve the criminal allegations she now faces.

articles.title: CeeDee Lamb rips Cowboys fans over George Pickens trade calls
articles.standfirst: Amid trade rumors surrounding George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb made his stance clear: the Cowboys’ offense is better with both receivers on the field.
articles.summary: Amid trade rumors surrounding George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb made his stance clear: the Cowboys’ offense is better with both receivers on the field.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have found a new dynamic in their receiving corps, with CeeDee Lamb reclaiming the undisputed WR1 role and George Pickens establishing himself as the offense’s clear No. 2 threat.

Both receivers have delivered strong performances and are on pace to surpass 1,000 receiving yards this season. Yet not everyone in the Dallas fan base is convinced that Pickens should remain with the team long-term.

With the Cowboys sitting at 3-5 , a defense ranking among the worst in the NFL , and limited realistic chances of contending for a championship, some fans believe the franchise should capitalize on Pickens’ value and explore a trade before his contract expires this summer.

The thinking is to sell high on a receiver acquired from the Pittsburgh Steelers who could become a significant asset on the trade market.

CeeDee Lamb backs George Pickens

However, one of the most important voices in the locker room disagrees. CeeDee Lamb came to Pickens’ defense and questioned why some fans want to see him leave Dallas.

Dallas Morning News reporter Calvin Watkins shared Lamb’s comments on the trade rumors:

“I don’t know why that’s the thing, but come on man. Everything that I’ve been able to accomplish has been because of him and what he’s done the year before and vice versa.”

While Lamb’s statement may sound exaggerated — especially since the receiver had already built a standout career before Pickens arrived — there is a valid point behind his argument.

Pickens’ presence has allowed Lamb to face fewer double teams and prevented opposing defenses from concentrating all their resources on stopping him. With another elite threat on the field, the seventh-year receiver has more space to create explosive plays.

Should the Cowboys re-sign or trade Pickens?

The numbers partially support Pickens’ impact on the offense. In 2024 , Lamb’s last season before the former Steelers receiver arrived, he averaged 79.6 yards per game — a lower figure than he is posting in 2026.

That comparison needs context, of course, since Cooper Rush started a large portion of that season due to Dak Prescott ’s injuries.

Still, Pickens continues to carry some questions related to his behavior and maturity. While those issues have not been a significant factor since he joined Dallas, uncertainty remains about whether they could resurface after a contract extension.

If the Cowboys received an offer approaching a second-round draft pick for Pickens , it would be a difficult decision to turn down. The receiver was originally selected in that same round by Pittsburgh, and Dallas already used a 2028 second-round pick to acquire Joey Porter Jr.

The franchise will have to decide whether the Lamb-Pickens duo can develop into one of the NFL’s best receiving combinations or whether this is the ideal time to cash in on Pickens’ value before committing to a long-term investment.
