articles.title: Dak Prescott makes feelings clear on George Pickens’ future with Cowboys
articles.standfirst: As trade speculation continues to swirl around George Pickens, Dak Prescott delivered a strong public defense of his Cowboys teammate.
articles.summary: As trade speculation continues to swirl around George Pickens, Dak Prescott delivered a strong public defense of his Cowboys teammate.
articles.body:
As the Dallas Cowboys try to move past a difficult start to the season marked by injuries and inconsistency, Dak Prescott has put an end to one of the debates surrounding the team: the rumors of a possible trade involving George Pickens.

The quarterback was firm in rejecting the idea that Dallas should part ways with the receiver and made clear that he considers Pickens an important piece both in the locker room and in the offense.

“People say a lot of things I don’t believe, so I’m not listening to that one, either. George is a great teammate. And I say that in the sense of, he’s gonna do whatever is asked, he’s gonna do whatever is called. If it’s to go block, if it’s to just go run a guy off, he’s gonna do that. He believes in just doing the right thing, and the ball will come his way at times. And so, that’s not on George.”

Prescott’s comments come at a time when some fans have called for the Cowboys to capitalize on Pickens’ value on the trade market before his contract expires.

Will the Cowboys re-sign George Pickens?

Despite the speculation, not everyone believes Pickens’ time in Dallas is nearing an end.

Fort Worth Star-Telegram reporter Nick Harris said on the House of Haymaker podcast that he expects the franchise to reach agreements to extend the contracts of both George Pickens and cornerback Joey Porter Jr.

“I think it will be a long-term extension (for Pickens),” Harris said. “And Porter gets the tag. I think there’s already kind of been foundations to that conversation being had with Porter. Whether Porter knows it or not, I think the foundations of that conversation have already started.”

Prescott has not been the only one to publicly defend the receiver.

Days earlier, CeeDee Lamb questioned the fans pushing for a Pickens trade and said his teammate’s presence has been key to his own success in the offense.

“I don’t know why that’s the thing, but come on, man. Everything that I’ve been able to accomplish has been because of him. And what he’s done the year before and vice versa.”

With the trade deadline approaching, George Pickens’ future continues to generate debate. However, both Prescott and Lamb have made clear that, inside the locker room, the receiver still has the full support of the Cowboys’ key figures.

articles.title: “Execute them on the field!” The frenzied reaction to epic Dallas Cowboys collapse
articles.standfirst: Dallas' heartbreaking overtime loss prompted an extraordinary reaction on ESPN's First Take
articles.summary: Dallas' heartbreaking overtime loss prompted an extraordinary reaction on ESPN's First Take
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys ' dramatic collapse against the Arizona Cardinals has left the franchise facing serious questions about its defense, but Skip Bayless has now created an entirely different controversy with his extraordinary reaction to the defeat.

Dallas appeared to be heading toward a much-needed victory on Sunday after establishing a 24-10 lead, only for Arizona to stage a remarkable comeback and secure a 33-30 overtime win at AT&T Stadium.

The Cowboys surrendered four consecutive touchdown drives during the closing stages, exposing defensive problems that have troubled Brian Schottenheimer 's team throughout the season.

Those failures dominated the discussion when Bayless returned to ESPN's First Take on Thursday alongside longtime broadcasting partner Stephen A. Smith .

However, the veteran commentator went considerably further than criticizing missed tackles or questionable defensive decisions, making a remark that quickly attracted widespread condemnation.

Bayless , a passionate Cowboys supporter known for his emotional reactions to Dallas defeats, expressed his frustration by suggesting he wanted several players executed during the game.

The remark was apparently intended as an exaggerated joke, but it immediately overshadowed the football discussion and prompted a direct response from one of the team's most prominent defensive players.

Bayless ' comments followed a Wednesday interview in which defensive tackle Quinnen Williams repeatedly emphasized the importance of executing assignments more effectively.

"I think the biggest thing is execute," Williams told reporters. "We gotta execute. We haven't been executing this whole season."

Williams acknowledged that Dallas had performed well defensively during the opening three quarters before allowing Arizona to take control.

"We executed for three quarters, and didn't execute that last quarter, and the film says it all," he explained.

Bayless subsequently seized upon the repeated use of the word when discussing the Cowboys' latest disappointment.

"Quinnen Williams, in a five-minute interview, used the word 'execute' 32 times in five minutes," Bayless said on First Take.

"And I must tell you that during Sunday's collapse against the Arizona freakin' Cardinals, I wanted to execute several of my players during the game. Execute them on the field. I wanted them to be executed."

The comments quickly circulated across social media, where viewers questioned whether such language was appropriate during a national television broadcast.

Dallas Cowboys face growing pressure

Williams was among those unimpressed by the remarks, confronting Bayless directly in a message posted on X later Thursday.

"It's extremely crazy to say you wanted players on defense to be executed. You got to do better my guy," Williams wrote.

The exchange added another distraction for a Cowboys team struggling to establish consistency as the NFL season approaches its midpoint.

Dallas has fallen to 3-5, leaving Schottenheimer under increasing pressure to address a defense that has repeatedly failed to protect leads.

Arizona's comeback was particularly damaging because the Cowboys had appeared in control before Gardner Minshew helped revive the Cardinals ' offense.

Chad Ryland eventually completed the turnaround with a 42-yard field goal in overtime, condemning Dallas to another defeat that could prove costly in the playoff race.

The Cowboys now face the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, with an opportunity to respond before their postseason ambitions suffer further damage.

Bayless may have intended his comments as provocative television humor, but Williams ' response demonstrated that the players involved saw little amusement in his choice of words.

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys and Jerry Jones could benefit from Texas election results
articles.standfirst: Texas is set to look a lot different these next few years.
articles.summary: Texas is set to look a lot different these next few years.
articles.body:
Tuesday's midterm election results have polarized the country, sparking major change within the government. Texas was one of the states that saw surprising results, and one of those results could end up playing a role in the Dallas Cowboys ' financial future under owner Jerry Jones .

In the race for Lieutenant Governor of Texas , Democrat Vikki Goodwin handily beat out Republican Dan Patrick . Along with Gina Hinojosa defeating Greg Abbott , there's now renewed hope that sports betting could soon become legal in Texas.

Sports betting is still illegal in Texas and 10 other states in the U.S.

Texas is one of 11 states where sports betting is still not legal: Alabama, Alaska, California, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Minnesota, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Texas, and Utah .

Patrick and Abbott were notoriously against sports gambling, but they are now no longer obstacles. It's not that clear-cut, as there are still many hoops to clear , but Marc Engel of Fort Worth Star-Telegram has explained why sports betting could once again be on the discussion table for Texas.

For the first time, a Texan can envision a future with legalized gambling possible within its borders. It does not mean it’s imminent. In a September interview with Fox 7 Austin, Goodwin said she is open to putting legalized gambling on a ballot for voters. Her win does not mean this topic will automatically flip in Austin. ​ ​The Democrats took control over the Texas House, but the Republicans still have the Texas Senate. Gambling requires a constitutional amendment approved by two-thirds vote of both chambers, and a statewide vote. Hinojosa’s stance on this is murkier. In her campaign for the governor’s office, she didn’t offer anything concrete about gambling. Her only real record on this is from 2023, when she was a state representative, and she voted against the sports betting constitutional amendment.

While nothing is set in stone, at all, there's at least some hope for sports fans who have been begging to be able to bet on games. If sports betting becomes legal in Texas, it will only grow the Cowboys' value, due to potential partnership deals and more ways of generating revenue through betting.

articles.title: Jerry Jones boasts of his wealth outside the Cowboys: “I have five wells going right now that cost more than any coach to drill the wells”
articles.standfirst: The Dallas Cowboys owner has hit back at suggestions that he is unwilling to pay top dollar for an elite head coach
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys owner has hit back at suggestions that he is unwilling to pay top dollar for an elite head coach
articles.body:
J erry Jones has made it clear that he does not believe money should prevent him from making a major investment, whether in the oil industry or in the future of the Dallas Cowboys .

The 84-year-old owner sparked fresh discussion about his approach to coaching salaries after appearing on 105.3 The Fan on Friday, November 6.

Facing criticism over the Cowboys ' spending on their coaching staff, Jones insisted he had previously pursued successful NFL coaches and was prepared to offer them significant contracts.

He then used his business interests outside football to make his point, revealing that he currently has five oil wells being drilled, with each project costing more than an NFL head coach's salary.

"My point is financial. Once you have decided the direction you want to go, financial is not a deterrent," Jones said.

The comments followed an earlier appearance on the same radio station in which Jones argued that there was no direct relationship between how much an organization pays its head coach and how successful it becomes.

That position attracted criticism, particularly given the Cowboys ' recent results and the reported compensation of their current head coach, Brian Schottenheimer .

Jones was determined to challenge the suggestion that he has avoided pursuing established coaching talent because of the financial commitment involved.

"Well, the facts are, I have been out there and I have been trying to lure very successful coaches away from the teams they were on and knew full well that I was going to pay them for all their success," Jones said. "So that has been done. No one knows that, but I do."

He also dismissed the criticism of his willingness to spend as "absolutely ridiculous," arguing that every major coaching appointment involves uncertainty.

"The fundamental issue of me not paying money for something that has a chance to be as wonderful as a Super Bowl or a successful team is ridiculous," he added.

Jones turns to his oil business to defend his spending decisions

The most striking part of the discussion came when Jones compared the financial decisions involved in running the Cowboys with his investments in energy.

"I make decisions every day that put hiring of coaches' financial situation pale, in comparison to it. And I drill wells. I have five wells going right now that cost more than any coach to drill the wells," Jones explained.

He added that the drilling projects would each require another three or four months to finish.

Oil and gas have been an important part of Jones ' business career for decades. He began investing in the industry long before becoming one of the most recognizable owners in professional sports, purchasing the Cowboys in 1989 for $150 million.

His involvement in the energy sector has continued through Comstock Resources, where he became the controlling shareholder following a major investment deal in 2018.

His business interests have therefore extended well beyond the football operation that made him a household name.

Jones also reinforced his personal philosophy about spending, saying: "Not one time in my life, if I wanted to do it, I let money stand in the way of doing it. That's stood true since the day I walked into the Dallas Cowboys ."

However, the debate is not simply about whether Jones has the resources to pay an expensive coach. It is also about whether he believes doing so would make a meaningful difference to the team's results.

Schottenheimer's annual salary has been estimated at between $5 million and $8 million, although NFL coaching contracts are not publicly disclosed.

That figure is considerably below the reported $20 million annual earnings of coaches such as Andy Reid , John Harbaugh and Sean Payton .

The difference has become particularly noticeable as the Cowboys continue to search for a way back to championship contention.

Six of the previous 10 Super Bowl-winning teams had coaches considered among the league's highest-paid, although that does not establish that salary alone produces success.

Dallas entered Week 9 with a 3-5 record, following a painful 33-30 overtime defeat against the Arizona Cardinals .

The result increased pressure on Jones and the coaching staff, with supporters questioning whether the organization is making the right decisions to compete at the highest level.

Jones , however, has continued to defend the team's direction rather than suggest that a major coaching change is imminent.

The Cowboys ' next opportunity to respond comes against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, November 8. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET, with the game airing on FOX and available to stream through FOX One.

For Jones , the message is that financial limitations are not responsible for Dallas' coaching decisions.

Whether his willingness to invest in football matches the ambition he demonstrates in his oil business, however, remains a question Cowboys supporters will continue to ask.

The 84-year-old owner sparked fresh discussion about his approach to coaching salaries after appearing on 105.3 The Fan on Friday, November 6.
Facing criticism over the Cowboys ' spending on their coaching staff, Jones insisted he had previously pursued successful NFL coaches and was prepared to offer them significant contracts.
He then used his business interests outside football to make his point, revealing that he currently has five oil wells being drilled, with each project costing more than an NFL head coach's salary.
"My point is financial. Once you have decided the direction you want to go, financial is not a deterrent," Jones said.

The comments followed an earlier appearance on the same radio station in which Jones argued that there was no direct relationship between how much an organization pays its head coach and how successful it becomes.
That position attracted criticism, particularly given the Cowboys ' recent results and the reported compensation of their current head coach, Brian Schottenheimer .
Jones was determined to challenge the suggestion that he has avoided pursuing established coaching talent because of the financial commitment involved.

"Well, the facts are, I have been out there and I have been trying to lure very successful coaches away from the teams they were on and knew full well that I was going to pay them for all their success," Jones said. "So that has been done. No one knows that, but I do."
He also dismissed the criticism of his willingness to spend as "absolutely ridiculous," arguing that every major coaching appointment involves uncertainty.
"The fundamental issue of me not paying money for something that has a chance to be as wonderful as a Super Bowl or a successful team is ridiculous," he added.
Jones turns to his oil business to defend his spending decisions
The most striking part of the discussion came when Jones compared the financial decisions involved in running the Cowboys with his investments in energy.

"I make decisions every day that put hiring of coaches' financial situation pale, in comparison to it. And I drill wells. I have five wells going right now that cost more than any coach to drill the wells," Jones explained.
He added that the drilling projects would each require another three or four months to finish.

Oil and gas have been an important part of Jones ' business career for decades. He began investing in the industry long before becoming one of the most recognizable owners in professional sports, purchasing the Cowboys in 1989 for $150 million.
His involvement in the energy sector has continued through Comstock Resources, where he became the controlling shareholder following a major investment deal in 2018.
His business interests have therefore extended well beyond the football operation that made him a household name.

Jones also reinforced his personal philosophy about spending, saying: "Not one time in my life, if I wanted to do it, I let money stand in the way of doing it. That's stood true since the day I walked into the Dallas Cowboys ."

However, the debate is not simply about whether Jones has the resources to pay an expensive coach. It is also about whether he believes doing so would make a meaningful difference to the team's results.
Schottenheimer's annual salary has been estimated at between $5 million and $8 million, although NFL coaching contracts are not publicly disclosed.
That figure is considerably below the reported $20 million annual earnings of coaches such as Andy Reid , John Harbaugh and Sean Payton .
The difference has become particularly noticeable as the Cowboys continue to search for a way back to championship contention.
Six of the previous 10 Super Bowl-winning teams had coaches considered among the league's highest-paid, although that does not establish that salary alone produces success.
Dallas entered Week 9 with a 3-5 record, following a painful 33-30 overtime defeat against the Arizona Cardinals .
The result increased pressure on Jones and the coaching staff, with supporters questioning whether the organization is making the right decisions to compete at the highest level.
Jones , however, has continued to defend the team's direction rather than suggest that a major coaching change is imminent.

The Cowboys ' next opportunity to respond comes against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, November 8. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET, with the game airing on FOX and available to stream through FOX One.
For Jones , the message is that financial limitations are not responsible for Dallas' coaching decisions.
Whether his willingness to invest in football matches the ambition he demonstrates in his oil business, however, remains a question Cowboys supporters will continue to ask.

articles.title: CeeDee Lamb and Dak Prescott put brakes on potential trade involving George Pickens, as Jerry Jones clearly states his plans
articles.standfirst: The Dallas quarterback and CeeDee Lamb want their teammate to remain with the franchise
articles.summary: The Dallas quarterback and CeeDee Lamb want their teammate to remain with the franchise
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys may be running out of time to rescue their season, but CeeDee Lamb and Dak Prescott believe trading George Pickens would only make their situation more difficult.

With the November 10 NFL trade deadline approaching, questions have emerged about whether Dallas should consider moving its talented wide receiver rather than risk losing him in free agency next year.

Pickens is playing under the franchise tag, leaving the Cowboys facing another expensive contract decision after already committing substantial money to Prescott and Lamb.

However, neither player believes breaking up one of the NFL's most productive receiving partnerships would solve the problems that have contributed to Dallas ' disappointing 3-5 start.

Lamb appeared genuinely surprised when asked Thursday about suggestions that the franchise should consider trading Pickens .

"I don't know why it's a thing," Lamb said. "Come on, man. "Everything I've been able to accomplish has been because of him and what he's done the year before, and vice versa. Everything I've accomplished the year prior to that, he exposed them."

His comments highlighted the importance of having another dangerous receiving option capable of drawing defensive attention away from him.

Prescott delivers strong defense of Pickens

Prescott was equally dismissive when questioned about the possibility of losing Pickens before the deadline.

"People say a lot of things I don't believe," Prescott responded. "So I'm not listening to that one, either."

The quarterback also defended Pickens ' attitude, describing a player willing to contribute even when the offense does not specifically involve him.

"George is a great teammate," Prescott said. "And I say that in the sense of, he's gonna do whatever is asked, he's gonna do whatever is called."

The statistics support the importance of both receivers, with Lamb recording 709 yards and six touchdowns this season while Pickens has contributed 533 yards and two scores.

Pickens was particularly productive last year, finishing with 1,429 receiving yards and nine touchdowns during his first season in Dallas.

However, retaining him beyond 2026 could prove expensive, particularly with Prescott earning an average of $60 million annually and Lamb already holding a contract worth $34 million per season.

Jerry Jones reveals Cowboys trade deadline approach

Despite those financial considerations, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has indicated that his immediate priority remains improving the team's chances of winning.

"We certainly are gonna take any opportunity to improve our team," Jones said during a recent appearance on 105.3 The Fan.

However, when questioned again Tuesday about potential moves, the owner adopted a more cautious position.

"At this particular time, I don't see anything," Jones said.

Executive vice president Stephen Jones has similarly rejected the suggestion that Dallas should abandon its playoff ambitions following Sunday's damaging overtime defeat against the Arizona Cardinals.

"We think we're close," Stephen Jones said. "We think we can get this ship righted and that we can have success."

The Cowboys have already traded away several draft selections, limiting their flexibility to pursue another significant addition before Tuesday.

With Indianapolis awaiting them Sunday, Dallas faces an important test of whether its confidence is justified.

Although Pickens ' long-term future remains uncertain, the message from his quarterback, fellow receiver and the Cowboys ' leadership suggests a trade is unlikely before the deadline.

articles.title: The Dallas Cowboys defense gets even worse as team makes painful move with rising starter
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys’ 2026 season might be dead in the water following their brutal loss in Week 8.
articles.summary: The Cowboys’ 2026 season might be dead in the water following their brutal loss in Week 8.
articles.body:
When Jerry Jones and the Dallas Cowboys front office made the quick decision to fire Matt Eberflus after just one season as the team’s defensive coordinator, they were making a statement that they believed he was at fault for fielding one of the worst defenses in franchise history.

Over the offseason, though, the front office made tons of moves to try to improve that defense, bringing in new players both through the draft and free agency. They also brought in 34-year-old defensive coordinator Christian Parker , who was previously the defensive backs coach for the Philadelphia Eagles .

None of that has made any difference. The Cowboys defense remains, arguably, the worst defense in the entire NFL. That notion was only amplified last week, when they let journeyman backup quarterback Gardner Minshew come on in a relief appearance and throw all over them in a shocking 33-30 Arizona Cardinals win in the Cowboys’ home.

Dallas Cowboys place Malachi Lawrence on IR

Now, heading into Week 9, the defense is set to get even worse. The team reportedly placed rookie outside linebacker Malachi Lawrence on Injured Reserve on Saturday, one day before their game against the Indianapolis Colts . Lawrence suffered a high-ankle sprain in the team’s loss to the Cardinals.

Lawrence had worked his way into a starting role in his first season with Dallas. Along with fellow rookie Caleb Downs , who was also injured during the Cardinals game, the two first-year players have been the only semblances of hope for the defense. Downs is expected to play in Week 9 , at least.

Lawrence will miss at least the next four games: at Colts, vs. San Francisco 49ers, vs. Tennessee Titans, vs. Philadelphia Eagles . There’s no telling whether the Cowboys will still be in playoff contention by the time Lawrence returns.

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys vs Indianapolis Colts: Where to watch, game time, and prediction for the NFL Week 9 matchup
articles.standfirst: Two struggling teams meet at Lucas Oil Stadium in Week 9
articles.summary: Two struggling teams meet at Lucas Oil Stadium in Week 9
articles.body:
The NFL reaches Week 9 with a matchup between two historic franchises that, at this point in the schedule, share an uncomfortable reality: their margin for error ran out a while ago.

Both teams carry losing records and need to pile up wins however they can to avoid being buried in the playoff race. What is at stake here is not guaranteed brilliance or spectacle, but sporting survival.

Standings overview in the NFL table

The context leaves no room for doubt about the urgency. T he Colts stand at 2 wins and 6 losses , which places them 28th in the league standings overall and in third place in the AFC South, behind Jacksonville and Houston.

Their point differential is alarming: 161 points for and 222 against, the worst defensive mark among the teams in their division and one of the most concerning in the entire AFC.

The Cowboys, meanwhile, come in with 3 wins and 5 losses, ranking 23rd overall and sitting second in the NFC East, behind the New York Giants.

Their offense has been more productive —219 points scored, the second-best total in their conference —, but their defense is also bleeding: 213 points allowed leave them with a differential of just +6. In Dallas they know how to score; the problem has been stopping the opponent.

The contrast is clear: the Cowboys have firepower but leaks at the back, while the Colts are limping on both sides of the ball. That dynamic sets the tone for the game.

Where to watch the Cowboys vs Colts and what time does it start?

The Colts host Dallas on Sunday, November 8, 2026, with kickoff at 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time (12:00 p.m. Central Time and 10:00 a.m. Pacific Time), at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, an indoor venue with a capacity of about 70,000 fans.

The Cowboys at Indianapolis will be broadcast nationally on Fox in the United States; while via streaming you can watch it on NFL+, YouTube TV, Hulu + Live TV, or Sling TV.

The key point: Dallas offense vs. Indianapolis defense

If there is one matchup that will decide the game, it is the one that will measure the Cowboys' offensive firepower against the Colts' fragile secondary. Dallas has averaged more than 27 points per game over eight contests, and Indianapolis has allowed nearly 28 per outing. On paper, it is fertile ground for the visitors.

The Cowboys' helmsman is Dak Prescott, a 33-year-old quarterback who leads an offense with top-tier weapons. His star receiver, CeeDee Lamb, is one of the most feared in the league, and the arrival of George Pickens gives Prescott a second vertical target capable of punishing any lapse.

Tight end Jake Ferguson rounds out a group of receivers that can put pressure on an Indianapolis secondary that has conceded too much.

On the home side, the challenge will be to sustain the offensive pace. At quarterback, the Colts have Daniel Jones and Anthony Richardson Sr. , while the heart of the attack remains running back Jonathan Taylor, a key piece in controlling the clock and keeping Dallas's offense off the field.

If Indianapolis wants to compete, it needs Taylor to carry the ball consistently and rookie tight end Tyler Warren to keep contributing in the passing game. Veteran receiver Keenan Allen adds experience to a group that needs sustained plays more than isolated deep shots.

For both, the math is tight. The Colts, at 2-6, depend on an almost perfect run in the second half of the schedule to dream of January, and they must also make up ground on two direct rivals in their own division. A loss here would leave them practically out of air.

The Cowboys, at 3-5, retain a more tangible hope: they are only one step behind the Giants in the NFC East and a victory would keep them within striking distance in a division no one has dominated. For Dallas, winning in Indianapolis is not a luxury, it is an obligation if they want to remain in the postseason conversation.

Cowboys vs Colts prediction: Who is favored to win?

Everything points to a high-scoring game. The Cowboys' offense has the weapons to punish a Colts defense that has been Indianapolis' biggest weakness all season.

If Jonathan Taylor manages to maintain control of the clock and the home team shortens possessions, the score could tighten; but if Dallas plays at its natural pace, Prescott and company have what it takes to come away with the win.

The forecast leans toward the Cowboys, although Indianapolis, playing at home and fueled by urgency, has what it takes to make it uncomfortable.

articles.title: Dak Prescott's spot-on speech drives Stephen A. Smith up the wall: “They're so comfortable that losing doesn't hurt them enough”
articles.standfirst: The ESPN analyst questioned the Dallas Cowboys quarterback’s public stance after he acknowledged his doubts about the team’s offensive identity.
articles.summary: The ESPN analyst questioned the Dallas Cowboys quarterback’s public stance after he acknowledged his doubts about the team’s offensive identity.
articles.body:
Dak Prescott once again found himself at the center of criticism for the way he publicly addresses the Dallas Cowboys’ problems. This time, his comments on the team’s offensive identity angered Stephen A. Smith, who questioned the quarterback’s attitude and felt that his remarks conveyed too much calm in the face of poor results.

The controversy began after Prescott was asked about the nature of Dallas’s offense. The quarterback responded with a mix of sincerity and a touch of irony: “Yeah, sure. I mean, is it an identity we’re proud of? I don’t know.” That answer failed to convince the ESPN analyst, especially given the franchise’s current struggles, with a 3-5 record heading into Week 9 of the season.

Stephen A. Smith Questions Prescott’s Attitude

During his appearance on “First Take,” Smith made it clear that his criticism isn’t related to the quarterback’s footballing ability. He acknowledged that Prescott is a great player and has enough talent to compete at the highest level, but pointed out that his priority seems to be giving politically correct answers and maintaining a controlled image in front of the media.

What really bothers me about Dak Prescott is that he’s a great player. He knows how to play; he’s no slouch. But his priority always seems to be saying the right thing and coming across as flawless

The analyst believes Dallas needs a different kind of reaction from its key leaders. In his opinion, Prescott should show more anger when the team isn’t performing, publicly call out his teammates when necessary, and make it clear that the current performance isn’t living up to the franchise’s expectations.

Sometimes I’d like to see him angry. I’d like to see him upset with his teammates. We’re talking about a player who makes $60 million a year and has earned $337 million over the past seven years. I want to see him a little more indignant

His criticism was even more scathing when he addressed the Cowboys’ competitive culture. “They’re living the good life in Dallas. That’s why they’re so bad: because they’re too comfortable. They’re so comfortable that losing doesn’t hurt them enough,” he said, in one of the harshest remarks of his commentary.

Smith also cited the Kansas City Chiefs as an example of a different reaction to losses. The commentator believes that players like Patrick Mahomes publicly express greater demand and frustration when results aren’t there—an attitude he feels is missing in the Dallas locker room.

The criticism comes during a difficult season for the Cowboys. The team, led by Brian Schottenheimer, has alternated between strong offensive moments and inconsistent performances and losses that have complicated their situation in the NFC East. The 33–30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals was one of the latest setbacks for a franchise that needs to improve its results.

Furthermore, Prescott isn’t the only one who has faced questions about the team’s situation. Doubts about the effort of some players, the coaching staff’s ability to respond, and a lack of consistency have fueled the debate over Dallas’s competitive culture. Now, with a 3-5 record , the Cowboys head into their next game against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 9 needing to deliver a response on the field as well.

articles.title: Jerry Jones in surprise Kanye West meeting that raises questions before Cowboys beat Colts
articles.standfirst: A surprise encounter at AT&T Stadium has attracted attention
articles.summary: A surprise encounter at AT&T Stadium has attracted attention
articles.body:
Jerry Jones has built a reputation for turning the Dallas Cowboys into far more than a football franchise, and his latest high-profile encounter has raised questions about another potential business opportunity involving one of music's biggest names.

The Cowboys owner reportedly met Kanye West , known professionally as Ye, during the rapper's concert at AT&T Stadium on Saturday, November 7, shortly before Dallas faced the Indianapolis Colts .

The unexpected meeting was revealed by longtime Cowboys reporter Clarence Hill Jr. , who shared the development on social media.

"Jerry Jones met with Kanye West before the show tonight @ATTStadium," Hill wrote on X.

The encounter has prompted speculation about a possible commercial relationship, and the timing attracted additional attention because the Cowboys were entering an important period of their season, with their playoff hopes under pressure and the NFL trade deadline approaching.

West performed at AT&T Stadium in Arlington as part of his 2026 stadium tour, which has included major appearances across the United States and internationally.

The November 7 concert was among the largest events on the rapper's schedule, bringing another major entertainment production to the Cowboys ' home venue.

Jones has consistently emphasized the commercial potential of AT&T Stadium, which regularly hosts concerts, boxing events and other entertainment attractions beyond NFL games.

The meeting therefore created an intriguing connection between two prominent figures whose business interests extend well beyond their original industries.

West , who grew up in Chicago, has historically been associated with the Chicago Bears rather than Dallas, making his appearance alongside Jones particularly unexpected.

Jones faces major Cowboys decision after Colts victory

While speculation surrounded his meeting with West , Jones also had more immediate concerns involving the direction of his football team.

Dallas entered Sunday's game against Indianapolis with a 3-5 record following a disappointing overtime defeat to the Arizona Cardinals .

The Cowboys responded with a 27-23 victory over the Colts , improving to 4-5 and giving their postseason ambitions a much-needed boost.

Before the game, Jones had already rejected suggestions that another defeat would automatically prompt Dallas to trade away established players.

Speaking on 105.3 The Fan, the Cowboys owner insisted that the roster possessed greater potential than its results had demonstrated.

"I really believe that we have a team that the work we've done over certainly the last 18 months or the last year in this year has real potential to play better than it's playing now," Jones said.

He also emphasized his preference for strengthening the current squad rather than beginning another rebuilding process.

"I'd be a lot more likely to be adding to this direction than taking away from it," Jones explained.

With the November 10 trade deadline approaching, Jones faces important decisions about whether to invest further resources in Dallas' playoff pursuit.

His meeting with West provided an unexpected distraction during a crucial weekend, although any suggestion of a new business deal remains unconfirmed.

Before the game, Jones had already rejected suggestions that another defeat would automatically prompt Dallas to trade away established players.
Speaking on 105.3 The Fan, the Cowboys owner insisted that the roster possessed greater potential than its results had demonstrated.
"I really believe that we have a team that the work we've done over certainly the last 18 months or the last year in this year has real potential to play better than it's playing now," Jones said.
He also emphasized his preference for strengthening the current squad rather than beginning another rebuilding process.
"I'd be a lot more likely to be adding to this direction than taking away from it," Jones explained.
With the November 10 trade deadline approaching, Jones faces important decisions about whether to invest further resources in Dallas' playoff pursuit.
His meeting with West provided an unexpected distraction during a crucial weekend, although any suggestion of a new business deal remains unconfirmed.

articles.title: Dak Prescott shares a special moment with a young fan before Cowboys-Colts game
articles.standfirst: The quarterback had a memorable encounter before leading Dallas to a much-needed win.
articles.summary: The quarterback had a memorable encounter before leading Dallas to a much-needed win.
articles.body:
Some coincidences seem destined to become unforgettable memories. Before facing the Indianapolis Colts, Dak Prescott met a young fan named Rayne Dakota, whose first and middle names were chosen in his honor . The quarterback took a moment to greet the boy and sign a keepsake, a gesture that will likely stay with him for years to come.

But there was another reason for Cowboys fans to celebrate that day. After the heartwarming encounter, Prescott took the field and led Dallas to a victory the team desperately needed .

Dak Prescott delivers on the field as the Cowboys defeat Indianapolis

It wasn't an easy start for Dallas. Brandon Aubrey opened the scoring with a 45-yard field goal , but a Prescott fumble allowed Indianapolis to take the lead on a touchdown by rookie Seth McGowan.

Dallas found its answer before halftime. Facing fourth down, Prescott connected with Jake Ferguson for a 10-yard touchdown. The quarterback later found CeeDee Lamb with a deep pass to extend the lead to 17-7 and give the visiting offense a much-needed boost .

Indianapolis kept applying pressure and managed to close the gap in the second half, but the Cowboys held their ground and protected their lead to secure a win they had to fight for until the final moments.

Prescott finished with 21 completions on 34 attempts for 335 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions . Lamb also delivered an impressive performance, recording 155 receiving yards, although he lost a fumble on a play in which he had gained 48 yards.

The final score was 27-23, and the result meant more to Dallas than just another win . After several weeks of taking their fans from excitement to frustration, the Cowboys finally gave them another reason to celebrate. Their season has been marked by inconsistent results: just when it seems the team is finding its footing, a loss gets in the way. Then a victory comes along and brings hope back.

Dallas remains second in the NFC East despite its ups and downs

That mix of wins and losses has kept Dallas from finding the consistency it needs, but the team is still very much in the race. With a 4-5 record, the Cowboys sit second in the NFC East, behind the New York Giants, who have five wins, two losses and one tie .

The gap still gives Dallas a chance to close in on the division lead. However, to make that happen, the Cowboys will need to build on victories like the one against Indianapolis and avoid letting a positive result be overshadowed by another setback the following week.

articles.title: Brian Schottenheimer explains why George Pickens didn't play against the Colts amid trade rumors
articles.standfirst: The receiver was unexpectedly ruled out against the Colts
articles.summary: The receiver was unexpectedly ruled out against the Colts
articles.body:
George Pickens ' unexpected absence from the Dallas Cowboys ' victory over the Indianapolis Colts raised immediate questions about his future, but head coach Brian Schottenheimer has offered a straightforward explanation for the receiver's controversial omission.

With the NFL trade deadline approaching on November 10, speculation intensified when Pickens was declared inactive shortly before Sunday's game, despite having participated in practice throughout the week.

The 25-year-old has been dealing with shoulder and hamstring injuries, limiting his playing time in recent weeks and raising concerns about his ability to contribute at full strength.

However, the timing of his absence prompted suggestions that Dallas could be protecting the receiver ahead of a potential trade, particularly with his contract situation remaining unresolved beyond this season.

Following the Cowboys ' dramatic 27-23 victory in Indianapolis, Schottenheimer dismissed the uncertainty surrounding the decision by explaining that Pickens had simply failed to recover sufficiently from his injuries.

"It's more the hamstring," Schottenheimer said when asked about the issue that ultimately prevented the receiver from taking the field.

Why was Pickens was ruled out against the Colts?

Pickens had been listed as questionable after participating on a limited basis in all three practices leading up to Sunday's game.

Although there was optimism that he could play, the receiver experienced discomfort after attempting to increase his workload, leaving the coaching staff unwilling to take unnecessary risks.

"He tried to go," Schottenheimer told reporters. "I mean, he wanted to play. He loves football. He tried to play, and unfortunately, just ran out of time."

The Cowboys were also without cornerback Joey Porter Jr. and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown , with both players unable to overcome injuries before kickoff.

Schottenheimer explained that the team had assessed all three players late in the week before ultimately deciding they were not healthy enough to participate.

"Friday they did some stuff, and then Saturday a little bit sore," he said. "We weren't sure, but again, at the end of the day, just they weren't able to go."

The coach expressed hope that the injured players could return for next Sunday's meeting with the San Francisco 49ers , although their availability will depend on further evaluations.

Cowboys overcome Pickens absence

Despite missing one of their leading offensive weapons, Dallas produced an impressive passing performance against Indianapolis, with quarterback Dak Prescott throwing for 335 yards and two touchdowns.

CeeDee Lamb shouldered much of the responsibility, recording 10 receptions for 195 yards and a touchdown as the Cowboys adjusted their offensive formations.

Ryan Flournoy also delivered a crucial contribution, catching a 46-yard pass on Dallas' final scoring drive before Javonte Williams completed the comeback with a one-yard touchdown run.

The victory improved the Cowboys ' record to 4-5, strengthening their position ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline.

Pickens' future nevertheless remains a significant question because his current contract expires after the season, potentially creating a difficult financial decision for the organization.

However, Schottenheimer 's explanation provides no indication that the receiver's absence was connected to trade negotiations.

With Dallas preparing to host San Francisco, the immediate priority remains getting Pickens healthy enough to return rather than speculating about a departure that has not been announced.

articles.title: George Pickens’ status vs. 49ers takes another twist after Stephen Jones’ latest update
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys escaped Indianapolis with a crucial win, but their biggest concern now is the health of George Pickens.
articles.summary: The Cowboys escaped Indianapolis with a crucial win, but their biggest concern now is the health of George Pickens.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys survived a difficult road trip to Indianapolis and defeated the Colts 27-22 in Week 9 , powered by another strong performance from Dak Prescott , who threw for 335 yards. The win came despite Dallas committing 14 penalties for 153 yards and missing two key starters: George Pickens and Joey Porter Jr.

Now, with a matchup against the San Francisco 49ers on the horizon, Dallas’s main concern is getting both players back. Facing one of the NFL’s top teams without their star receiver and one of their key defensive pieces would significantly hurt the Cowboys’ chances.

Stephen Jones does not guarantee George Pickens’s return

Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones acknowledged Monday on 105.3 The Fan that there is still no certainty about the availability of George Pickens or Joey Porter Jr. for the Week 10 game.

Both players were listed as questionable before the Colts game but ultimately sat out—Pickens with a hamstring injury and Porter Jr. with an ankle issue.

When asked whether the decision could come as late as the end of the week, Jones made clear that everything will depend on their progress:

It’s probably a fair summary of it. I think we just have to get them out there, get them going again, and see how they’re coming along. Obviously, two great players like that you want them on the field. Certainly, can do a lot to help you win a football game. We’ll just have to see how the week goes. We’re not the only team that is fighting through injuries, so that’s just part of the game we play. We’re certainly going to have to really see what our injury situation is this week. We’re going to have some challenges.

CeeDee Lamb and Ryan Flournoy stepped up

Despite Pickens’s absence, Dallas’s passing attack responded. CeeDee Lamb had a standout performance with 195 receiving yards , while Ryan Flournoy took on a larger role in the offense.

Though he caught only two passes, one of them was a 46-yard reception that set up the Cowboys’ game-winning touchdown.

Prescott did not hold back in praising his teammate:

“That’s the standard he sets for himself, that we have, and the expectation. Flo is a guy that I can’t say enough about and I try to every time tell you guys what he means to me and what he means to this offense. So when I got an opportunity like that, with a minute left, I got Flo man-to-man … I am going to attack with the utmost trust and Flo showed you why I have that.”

The Cowboys will host the 49ers this Sunday at AT&T Stadium in a critical game for their playoff hopes. With Pickens and Porter Jr. still recovering, Dallas will closely monitor both players’ progress throughout the week.

articles.title: Cowboys coach confronts injured starter after ‘unacceptable’ mistake
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys avoided disaster against the Colts, but one controversial moment pushed Brian Schottenheimer to deliver a strong message to the team.
articles.summary: The Cowboys avoided disaster against the Colts, but one controversial moment pushed Brian Schottenheimer to deliver a strong message to the team.
articles.body:
The controversial play involving DeMarvion Overshown has become the latest example of the concentration and discipline problems that have plagued the Dallas Cowboys this season.

The linebacker, who is currently sidelined with back and hamstring injuries, was dressed in civilian clothes when he ran onto the field in Indianapolis to celebrate with his teammates after a Colts fumble in the fourth quarter .

Although Overshown’s reaction was driven by the emotion of the moment, his decision drew criticism both inside and outside the organization. It resulted in a 15-yard penalty and added to an already messy disciplinary afternoon for Dallas, which committed 14 penalties in its 27-23 victory .

According to reports, the linebacker apologized to his teammates on Monday for an action coaches viewed as a lapse in concentration that cannot be repeated.

Brian Schottenheimer puts the Overshown issue to rest

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer said the situation has been handled. He spoke with Overshown one-on-one before addressing the full team.

“Addressed it 1-on-1 with D-Mo first. Addressed it with the football team. Totally unacceptable and it won’t happen again. … He understands that was unacceptable and can’t happen. Our meeting was very straightforward.”

Beyond the Overshown incident, Schottenheimer expressed frustration with the volume of penalties Dallas committed against Indianapolis, though he called the performance an outlier.

The coach said the team reviewed all 14 penalties during Monday’s meeting and made clear the standard was not met.

“We actually watched all 14 of them in the team meeting, we pointed it out. Sloppy. Not good enough. I think there were two pre-snap, which is a positive. I think we were averaging seven a game, so we were twice the average. Not good enough at all. We showed all the penalties from the PIs to the holdings. … Sloppy fundamentals.”

Schottenheimer also warned that these kinds of mistakes could prove costly if the team fails to correct them.

“Yesterday was the outlier and that was why that game came down the way it came down. That game should have been where we win by a couple touchdowns maybe, but we let them hang around, we put ourselves behind the sticks on offense a bunch. Explained to the guys, if we don’t clean that up, it is going to hurt our ability to do what we want to do.”

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys inactive player gets penalized without even playing
articles.standfirst: Dallas celebrated a win over the Colts, but an inactive player ended up getting the team into trouble.
articles.summary: Dallas celebrated a win over the Colts, but an inactive player ended up getting the team into trouble.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys got the win they desperately needed, defeating the Indianapolis Colts 27-23 in Week 9 of the NFL season . However, in a game that remained close until the final moments, one celebration turned into a headache for Dallas.

Cowboys player gets penalized without even playing

It all happened in the fourth quarter. Quinnen Williams forced a fumble by Jonathan Taylor, and Shemar James recovered the ball for the Cowboys. The defense rushed to celebrate the play, and DeMarvion Overshown wanted to join in on the excitement .

The linebacker, who was inactive for the game, left the sideline and stepped onto the field wearing blue sweatpants and a beanie. His enthusiasm, however, ended up costing Dallas.

Why were the Cowboys penalized?

Referee Clay Martin called a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty after spotting Overshown on the field without wearing his uniform . It was a costly mistake that the Cowboys had to deal with at a crucial point in the game.

Dallas failed to make progress on its next possession and was forced to punt. Indianapolis took advantage, moving closer on the scoreboard before eventually tying the game at 20-20 with a 59-yard field goal.

What seemed like an innocent celebration ended up creating a problem for the Cowboys, giving their opponents another opportunity to stay in the game.

Dallas will return to action on Sunday, November 15, when it takes on the San Francisco 49ers . Following this win, the team will look to build on its momentum and put behind the inconsistency it showed early in the season, when wins and losses seemed to alternate week after week.

articles.title: Pat McAfee gives Cowboys legend Tony Romo a surprise TV opportunity after CBS exit
articles.standfirst: The former Dallas quarterback made his first major television appearance since leaving CBS Sports
articles.summary: The former Dallas quarterback made his first major television appearance since leaving CBS Sports
articles.body:
T ony Romo has found an unexpected route back onto NFL television, thanks to Pat McAfee .

The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback made a surprise appearance on ESPN2 during Monday night's Buffalo Bills versus Minnesota Vikings game, offering fans their first major glimpse of him behind a microphone since his departure from CBS Sports.

McAfee introduced Romo during the second quarter of the Week 9 matchup, giving him the playful title of "quarterback specialist" and immediately bringing some familiar personality back to the broadcast.

“U.S. Bank Stadium has been a problem for this Buffalo Bills team. They’re not the only one. Ladies and gentlemen, joining us now, he’s our quarterback expert. Sorry about it, Orlovsky. Tony Romo , how are you, brother?” said McAfee .

Romo responded in good spirits, acknowledging ESPN analyst Dan Orlovsky , who was also involved in the coverage.

“I’m doing good, and I’m sorry, Dan, that they gave me the quarterback specialist here, but you know that I think you’re a great quarterback guru. You know that,” Romo said.

The exchange quickly moved into football analysis. Romo discussed Minnesota's offensive difficulties against Buffalo's defense, highlighting the pressure facing quarterback Carson Wentz and the challenge of getting the ball to star receiver Justin Jefferson .

He also delivered a familiar piece of entertainment by imitating a quarterback's pre-snap cadence: “White eighty! Get the ball to Jefferson!”

The brief appearance ended with McAfee making his appreciation for the former Cowboys star clear.

“We miss the hell out of you this season,” McAfee told him before signing off.

Could ESPN offer Romo a permanent broadcasting opportunity?

Although Monday's appearance was only a guest segment, it arrived at an interesting moment for ESPN's NFL coverage. Troy Aikman 's future with the network is uncertain, with his current contract approaching its expiration after the 2026 season.

Aikman has acknowledged that he will become a free agent following the Super Bowl, while his broadcasting partner Joe Buck has already secured a new six-year agreement with ESPN. Reports have also highlighted differences between Aikman's contract situation and Buck's new deal.

That uncertainty has naturally encouraged speculation about possible replacements. Romo's appearance prompted some fans to suggest that ESPN could be testing him as a potential successor, although there has been no official announcement connecting the former quarterback to Aikman's position.

For now, McAfee's invitation should be viewed as an opportunity to return to television rather than confirmation of a new job.

Romo's absence began after his July 2026 arrest in Wisconsin for operating while intoxicated. CBS subsequently placed him on leave, and the network announced on October 2 that both parties had mutually agreed to part ways.

He had spent nine seasons as CBS's lead NFL analyst alongside Jim Nantz , with J.J. Watt subsequently taking over the role.

Romo had previously addressed his departure with a statement reflecting on his time at the network: “I’m proud of what I accomplished at CBS Sports over the last nine years. I approached my role as a game analyst the way I’ve approached everything in my life, with a desire to win and be the best that I can be.”

A familiar voice that NFL fans have missed

Romo's broadcasting reputation was built on his ability to anticipate plays before they developed. After retiring from professional football in 2017, he quickly became one of the most recognizable analysts in the sport.

His chemistry with Nantz and his willingness to predict offensive decisions helped distinguish him from more traditional commentators.

His performance during the 2019 AFC Championship Game between the Kansas City Chiefs and New England Patriots remains one of the most celebrated examples of his ability to read the action.

His departure from CBS therefore left a significant gap, even as the network moved forward with Watt .

McAfee's appearance offered Romo a relatively relaxed environment to demonstrate his football knowledge without having to address his recent legal difficulties. It also gave viewers a reminder of the personality that made him such a popular broadcaster.

Whether this leads to further ESPN appearances, a permanent role or another opportunity elsewhere remains unknown. Jerry Jones and the Cowboys have not announced any new broadcasting position for their former quarterback.

For now, McAfee has given Romo a welcome opportunity to reconnect with NFL audiences. The surprise cameo may not represent a permanent return, but it has certainly restarted the conversation about what comes next for the former Cowboys star.

His departure from CBS therefore left a significant gap, even as the network moved forward with Watt .

McAfee's appearance offered Romo a relatively relaxed environment to demonstrate his football knowledge without having to address his recent legal difficulties. It also gave viewers a reminder of the personality that made him such a popular broadcaster.

Whether this leads to further ESPN appearances, a permanent role or another opportunity elsewhere remains unknown. Jerry Jones and the Cowboys have not announced any new broadcasting position for their former quarterback.

For now, McAfee has given Romo a welcome opportunity to reconnect with NFL audiences. The surprise cameo may not represent a permanent return, but it has certainly restarted the conversation about what comes next for the former Cowboys star.

articles.title: Jerry Jones signals Cowboys could make a deadline move without making a major push
articles.standfirst: On Sunday, the Cowboys will look to string together their first winning streak of the season
articles.summary: On Sunday, the Cowboys will look to string together their first winning streak of the season
articles.body:
It has been another frustrating campaign for the Dallas Cowboys , who currently sit at 4-5 while burdened by a porous defense that continually struggles to contain opposing offenses.

Failing to reach the postseason for a third consecutive season would almost certainly trigger widespread coaching changes in Dallas, likely beginning with head coach Brian Schottenheimer .

Beyond the coaching staff, questions linger regarding Jerry Jones ’ long-term commitment to starting quarterback Dak Prescott , including whether the front office might eventually consider listening to trade offers for him.

The franchise’s playoff drought in the late rounds remains a glaring issue; since 2010 , every single NFC franchise has reached the NFC Championship Game at least once, except for the Cowboys, who last appeared in the conference title game during their 1995 Super Bowl championship run .

Jerry Jones Hints at Potential Dallas Cowboys Trade Deadline Move

As the 2026 NFL regular season enters its second half, Dallas recognizes that its clearest path to a postseason berth lies in capturing the NFC East title, currently led by the New York Giants holding a 5-2-1 record.

That reality has fueled intense speculation over whether the Cowboys will make a dramatic splash before the trade deadline to patch up significant defensive vulnerabilities.

While the front office previously acquired All-Pro defensive tackle Quinnen Williams and traded for cornerback Joey Porter Jr. , the roster still suffers from an overall talent deficit on the defensive side of the ball.

Addressing the team’s plans, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones offered a nuanced update during a radio appearance.

Jones advised fans to “don’t count out” a potential deadline deal, though he tempered expectations with a humorous caveat: “You know that old country song? When that phone’s not ringing, that’s me calling. It’s really not ringing … but don’t count it out. A lot of things happen on that last day. But I don’t look for us to make a significant trade today.”

Adding defensive reinforcements would be a critical boost for Dallas as they navigate a challenging second-half schedule. The Cowboys still face home matchups against the San Francisco 49ers, Jacksonville Jaguars , and division-leading Giants, alongside tough road trips to confront the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams .

Whether Jones pulls off a late-minute transaction or stands pat, the Cowboys need immediate defensive improvements if they hope to salvage their season and make a push for the playoffs.

articles.title: Jake Ferguson earns Haley’s praise for something he did away from the football field
articles.standfirst: Four words were all it took for his wife to make her feelings clear.
articles.summary: Four words were all it took for his wife to make her feelings clear.
articles.body:
There are things that make you proud of your partner that have nothing to do with their professional achievements. Jake Ferguson has just received recognition that shines a spotlight on that side of him, and Haley Cavinder was quick to let him know just how proud she is .

The Dallas Cowboys tight end’s wife shared a selfie with Jake on her Instagram Stories. Over the photo, she wrote four simple words: “proud of you always.” She also tagged the National Medal of Honor Museum , offering a clue about what prompted her heartfelt message.

Ferguson was selected by Dallas as the team’s nominee for the 2026 NFL Salute to Service Award . Announced on November 5, the nomination recognizes players, coaches and members of NFL organizations who demonstrate a strong commitment to supporting military members, veterans and their families.

A commitment that goes far beyond a nomination

So, what has Jake done to earn this recognition? His connection to the cause runs through the National Medal of Honor Museum in Arlington, Texas, where he serves as an ambassador . Through his involvement, he takes part in activities that help share the stories of the men and women who received the Medal of Honor.

One of those initiatives is Character Playbook, an educational program for students in Arlington ISD. Through the program, young people learn about the experiences of these service members while exploring leadership, resilience and civic responsibility. Ferguson has also had the opportunity to spend time with veterans and their families, as well as Medal of Honor recipients, including Jim McCloughan.

Another sign that his support goes beyond those personal encounters is his involvement in My Cause My Cleats. The tight end chose the museum as his charitable cause and wears custom-designed cleats to help raise awareness of its mission . Proceeds from auctions of the footwear also help fund the institution’s work.

Jake has also teamed up with Black Rifle Coffee Company on fundraising campaigns aimed at helping veterans eliminate their medical debt.

That is what makes the Cowboys’ recognition especially meaningful: it shines a light on a side of Ferguson that deserves to be celebrated, and one Haley was more than happy to applaud.

articles.title: The reason Jerry Jones has never considered trading Dak Prescott lies in his “controversial” contract
articles.standfirst: Jones may not have permission to move the Dallas Cowboys star elsewhere
articles.summary: Jones may not have permission to move the Dallas Cowboys star elsewhere
articles.body:
J erry Jones has made it clear that Dak Prescott is not available for trade, regardless of the Dallas Cowboys ' struggles this season – however, the owner's explanation goes beyond his confidence in the quarterback, with the terms of the NFL player’s lucrative contract. Jones currently holds significant control over his future in Dallas and admitted that letting the veteran leave the franchise has never been a viable option as he opened up on 105.3 The Fan ahead of the NFL trade deadline on November 10.

The 84-year-old was asked whether another franchise had ever contacted the Cowboys about acquiring Prescott and his response suggested that moving the quarterback had never been a serious consideration. "No. No, not really,” Jones said. “We've always, let's say for two-thirds of his contract and two-thirds of time with us, we've had him in a position where it wouldn't make any sense to trade him.” That position became particularly clear when Dallas negotiated Prescott 's latest extension as just before the 2024 regular season, the Cowboys handed their quarterback a four-year contract worth $240 million and made him the NFL 's highest-paid player at the time. The agreement included an average annual value of $60 million and $231 million in total guarantees but more significantly, it contained no-trade, no-franchise-tag and no-transition clauses. Consequently, Dallas cannot simply negotiate a deal with another team and send Prescott elsewhere without first obtaining his approval as the paperwork reflects the Cowboys ' longstanding commitment, even during periods when uncertainty surrounded his future.

Jones backs Prescott despite Cowboys woes

The subsequent $240 million agreement reinforced that stance as although Prescott 's previous contract situation created the possibility of him reaching free agency, Jones never publicly suggested that the franchise was prepared to move on from its starting quarterback. And the commitment has remained in place despite another challenging campaign as Dallas entered Week 9 with a 3-5 record but managed to claim another victory after edging out the Indianapolis Colts 27-23, a win that required Prescott to help rescue the team from another potential late-game collapse. The quarterback completed 21 of 34 passes for 335 yards and two touchdowns, including a crucial 46-yard connection with Ryan Flournoy during the final stages whilst three plays later, running back Javonte Williams scored the decisive touchdown with 1:08 remaining. CeeDee Lamb also delivered an outstanding performance, catching 10 passes for 195 yards. However, Dallas ' 14 penalties for 153 yards demonstrated that the victory was far from convincing. Yet despite the penalties, Prescott 's individual numbers remain productive in the 2026 NFL season and with his contract giving him substantial control over any potential move, Dallas remains firmly committed to the player it made one of the league's highest-paid quarterbacks.

articles.title: Latest comment by Shannon Sharpe on CeeDee Lamb triggers fan reaction: “The Cowboy hate is real”
articles.standfirst: Sharpe's assessment of the NFL's best receivers has reopened an old argument
articles.summary: Sharpe's assessment of the NFL's best receivers has reopened an old argument
articles.body:
CeeDee Lamb delivered the kind of performance that typically strengthens a receiver's reputation among the NFL 's elite, but his latest display has done little to convince Shannon Sharpe that the Dallas Cowboys star belongs among the league's three best players at his position.

Lamb recorded 10 catches for 195 yards and a touchdown during Dallas' 27-23 victory over the Indianapolis Colts , helping his team secure an important win. However, the former NFL tight end sparked controversy by suggesting several other receivers remain ahead of him.

Speaking on his Nightcap podcast, Sharpe identified Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Ja'Marr Chase as superior options before adding Puka Nacua to the conversation, effectively moving Lamb outside his top three when everyone is healthy.

The assessment quickly generated criticism from Cowboys supporters, many of whom believe Sharpe has consistently underestimated their leading receiver despite his production and importance to the Dallas offense.

“So you saying CeeDee better than Chase and JSN? Because normally that's who we mention,” Sharpe explained. "I will put JSN based on what he's done the last two years… Prior of last year he had a hundred catch season. "And then we know he was offensive player of the year… But I go JSN, Chase, I put CeeDee 3rd… Hold on. If Puka’s fully healthy, I'm not so sure. I'll take Puka over CeeDee.”

His comments prompted an immediate response on social media, where supporters questioned why Lamb 's achievements appeared insufficient to secure a higher ranking.

“Production matters until it comes to ceedee lmao,” one fan wrote on X, suggesting the Cowboys receiver was being judged differently from his peers. Another declared, “The cowboy hate is real,” while a third added, “CeeDee disrespect is wild”.

Not everyone agreed with the criticism, however. One fan defended Sharpe's position, responding, “Having him top 4 is not hate sir”.

The disagreement also revived memories of Sharpe 's previous assessment on Undisputed, when he argued that Lamb didn't deserve a place among the NFL's 10 best receivers.

Lamb looks to silence critics

While the debate continues, Lamb has more immediate concerns surrounding Dallas' performances and his own mistakes during the victory over Indianapolis.

Despite his impressive receiving numbers, the Cowboys star committed three penalties and lost a fourth-quarter fumble, mistakes that threatened to complicate an otherwise productive afternoon.

The receiver acknowledged those errors afterward, focusing on the improvements required rather than celebrating his individual statistics.

Dallas now prepares to host the San Francisco 49ers on November 15, with Lamb expected to play another significant role as the Cowboys attempt to build momentum.

Sharpe 's ranking remains a matter of personal opinion, but another commanding performance would give Lamb 's supporters further ammunition in a debate that has become increasingly heated.

articles.title: The Cowboys have a serious problem with Brandon Aubrey: What is it?
articles.standfirst: The Dallas kicker's struggles from long distance are creating an uncomfortable dilemma for head coach Brian Schottenheimer
articles.summary: The Dallas kicker's struggles from long distance are creating an uncomfortable dilemma for head coach Brian Schottenheimer
articles.body:
B randon Aubrey has established himself as one of the NFL's most reliable kickers since arriving in Dallas in 2023.

However, his performances from beyond 50 yards have become a growing concern during the 2026 season, and the problem could force the Cowboys to reconsider how they approach fourth downs.

Through nine games, Aubrey has converted just three of eight attempts from at least 50 yards, a 37.5% success rate.

The numbers are particularly striking for a kicker who has previously made a reputation for delivering from distances that many others would consider difficult.

According to NFL statistics, Aubrey has connected on two of four attempts between 50 and 59 yards and just one of four from 60 yards or further. By comparison, he has been perfect on attempts from 20 to 49 yards this season.

That distinction matters because Dallas has frequently trusted its kicker to attempt long-range field goals rather than push for a first down or touchdown.

The concern is not necessarily that Aubrey has suddenly become a poor kicker. Even the best players miss difficult attempts, particularly from beyond 50 yards.

Instead, the bigger question is whether Schottenheimer should continue making decisions based on the assumption that his kicker can reliably convert from almost anywhere on the field.

One Cowboys supporter highlighted the issue on social media, writing: “Meanwhile Schotty calls the game like he’s automatic from 70.”

Another fan argued that Dallas should be more willing to keep its offense on the field in certain situations: “Anything 4th & 2 or less from the opponents 35-45 yard line should be an automatic go for it. Dal 45 to opp 45 is situational go for it or punt.”

Why Schottenheimer may need to change his approach

Dallas has enough offensive talent to make opponents uncomfortable without relying so heavily on its kicker.

Quarterback Dak Prescott has continued to lead a productive attack, while the Cowboys have averaged 27.3 points per game through their first nine contests, ranking among the league's better scoring offenses.

That makes the decision to settle for a long field goal particularly important. When the offense reaches the opponent's 35-yard line, for example, a 53-yard attempt might appear attractive because of Aubrey's powerful leg.

But if his recent conversion rate from that distance is taken into account, going for a manageable fourth down could offer a better opportunity.

There is also a broader issue with Dallas' dependence on Aubrey. His ability to make extraordinary kicks has helped give the coaching staff confidence in situations where other teams might punt or attempt to convert. However, that reputation should not automatically dictate every decision.

Aubrey remains an important part of the Cowboys ' plans. He has made 17 of 22 field-goal attempts overall this season, and his career conversion rate remains impressive. He also set a franchise record with a 65-yard field goal in 2024.

The immediate test comes against the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, November 15. Dallas enters the matchup at 4-5, while San Francisco boasts a 7-1 record and has won its last four meetings with the Cowboys. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX.

If Dallas wants to pull off an important victory, Schottenheimer may need to show more aggression on fourth down. Aubrey's ability is not necessarily the biggest problem.

It is the possibility that the coaching staff is still making decisions as though every long-range attempt is a near certainty.

articles.title: Jerry Jones faces four costly disappointments as Cowboys reach the halfway point of a frustrating season
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys need to make the playoffs; it's their worst playoff drought since 2010-13
articles.summary: The Cowboys need to make the playoffs; it's their worst playoff drought since 2010-13
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys face a monumental test this weekend when they host arguably the strongest team in the NFL, the San Francisco 49ers . Currently sitting at 4-5 , “America’s Team” desperately needs an upset victory on Sunday because a favorable stretch awaits right afterward, featuring matchups against the Tennessee Titans and Philadelphia Eagles , two struggling teams sitting near the bottom of the league standings.

With the Washington Commanders recently knocking off the New York Giants , Dallas has a prime opportunity to pull within a single game of the Giants atop the NFC East . Yet while Dak Prescott and the Cowboys’ sixth-ranked offense ( 27.3 points per game ) usually hold up their end of the bargain, Dallas’ defense will likely surrender at least 20 points to San Francisco.

Despite aggressive offseason changes, highlighted by the hiring of defensive coordinator Christian Parker , the unit remains a glaring liability, ranking 25th in points allowed ( 26.2 per game ) and 30th in total yards surrendered .

Three Costly Defensive Disappointments Holding Back the Dallas Cowboys

Although half of the 2026 NFL regular season remains, the Cowboys have looked decidedly mediocre and far removed from genuine championship contention.

Owner Jerry Jones invested heavily in revamping the roster, yet several high-profile defensive pieces have failed to deliver on expectations through nine weeks. In particular, three key defenders stand out as the franchise’s biggest disappointments so far:

Von Miller : Brought in primarily to provide championship leadership in the locker room, the former Super Bowl 50 MVP has generated virtually zero impact as a pass rusher. Through nine games, Miller has managed just one sack and 11 quarterback pressures , a dramatic decline from the nine sacks and 36 pressures he recorded during the 2025 campaign.

DeMarvion Overshown : This season was supposed to be the year Overshown solidified himself as an elite, every-down linebacker following a promising 13-game sophomore campaign that ended with the second major knee injury of his young career. Instead, durability has derailed his momentum once again; Overshown has missed six of Dallas’ first nine contests due to a lingering hamstring injury suffered in Week 1 that flared back up in Week 9. With unrestricted free agency looming in 2027, his future in Arlington looks increasingly bleak.

Rashan Gary : Acquired to serve as the primary anchor of Dallas’ pass rush, Gary has generated 32 quarterback pressures, good enough to tie for 11th-most among edge defenders. However, generating disruption without bringing the quarterback down isn’t enough; the Cowboys desperately need him to finish plays in the backfield, and with only one sack on the stat sheet, he simply hasn’t closed the deal.

articles.title: “It’s best for everyone”: Jerry Jones stands by the unpopular 18-game NFL schedule that players hate
articles.standfirst: Cowboys owner believes expanded NFL season is inevitable despite players' concerns
articles.summary: Cowboys owner believes expanded NFL season is inevitable despite players' concerns
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones isn't backing away from his support for an expanded NFL regular season, insisting that introducing an 18-game schedule would benefit everyone involved despite considerable opposition from players.

Jones recently reiterated his position during an appearance on 105.3 The Fan, telling listeners that he expects the proposed change to become reality.

“It’s in everybody’s best interest,” he said, adding that he anticipates the expanded schedule arriving in the near future. "I would anticipate that coming.”

The Cowboys owner has supported the idea for years. Back in 2018, when the NFL played 16 regular-season games and four preseason contests, Jones suggested moving to 18 regular-season games while reducing the preseason to two games.

The league subsequently introduced a 17-game format in 2021, leaving three preseason contests. Jones believes replacing another exhibition with a meaningful regular-season game would create greater value for the league, its players and its audience.

His argument also focuses on financial rewards. An additional regular-season contest would generate more revenue, and Jones believes players should receive their fair share. He previously suggested the proposal could deliver more than $1 billion to players.

Jones has also questioned the value of an extended preseason, arguing that exhibition football can expose players to unnecessary injury risks without offering the same competitive benefits as regular-season games.

Player safety remains the biggest obstacle to Jones' proposal

Jones ' argument hasn't convinced everyone, particularly those responsible for taking the field every week. Several prominent players have expressed reservations about extending an already demanding season.

Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes previously admitted he wasn't enthusiastic about playing an additional game. However, he suggested that introducing more bye weeks could help address the physical demands.

“I think that you’d have to find a way to have more bye weeks, more time spread out,” Mahomes said.

Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow has also advocated additional recovery time, proposing another bye week around the later stages of the season. Such an adjustment could give players more time to recover before the final stretch.

The NFL Players Association has been equally cautious. Former interim executive director David White said players had little appetite for another game without meaningful protections for their health, recovery and working conditions.

Current executive director JC Tretter has maintained that player safety will remain central to any discussions. The former NFL center also recognizes that any scheduling changes must be negotiated rather than imposed by team owners.

Meanwhile, international expansion remains another consideration. The NFL has nine international games scheduled for 2026 and plans to increase its international presence in the coming years. Owners see additional regular-season inventory as an opportunity to accommodate the league's growing global ambitions.

Commissioner Roger Goodell has previously acknowledged interest in an 18-game season but stressed that expansion isn't guaranteed.

There is also a significant contractual obstacle. The existing collective bargaining agreement runs through the 2030 season and prohibits owners from independently increasing the regular season beyond 17 games. Any expansion therefore requires agreement with the players' union.

Furthermore, formal negotiations over the proposed change hadn't begun by June 2026, making a 2027 introduction difficult to arrange.
